540673|2026-03.headline: SIS Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 31% YoY to INR4,489 crore with a record INR207 crore EBITDA at 4.6% margin.
540673|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as its best quarter ever, with record revenue, EBITDA and PAT, and ROCE of 16.5% versus 14.3% a year earlier. India Security delivered its highest-ever revenue (INR1,925 crore, up 34.2%), partly from the APS acquisition, and International Security also posted record revenue (INR1,950 crore, up 36.9%). Facility Management was the slowest grower at 8.1% YoY to INR635 crore. A INR290 crore gratuity/leave charge taken in Q3 under the new Labour Codes was partly reversed (INR38.8 crore) through OCI in Q4, and management said past-period recovery from clients is under discussion.

financial_highlights.change: reassessment after Q3 INR290 crore exceptional charge

financial_highlights.value: INR70 crore in Q4 vs INR55 crore in Q3
financial_highlights.change: FY26 INR215 crore vs FY25 INR163 crore
up from about INR20 crore YoY

segments.name: India Security
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,925 crore (+34.2% YoY, includes APS consolidation); EBITDA INR98.4 crore at 5.1% margin. Ex-APS, Security grew 11% YoY at about 5.5% margin.

segments.name: Facility Management
segments.commentary: Revenue INR635 crore (+8.1% YoY); EBITDA margin 5.5%, up from roughly 4.5% previously. Management said the monthly run rate rose to INR31 crore versus INR21 crore a year ago. Headcount fell from about 85,000 to 82,000, which management attributed to closed contracts after surge work.

segments.name: International Security
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,950 crore (+36.9% YoY); EBITDA margin 3.8%, stable QoQ, with EBITDA up 28.7% YoY. Q4 included about AUD20 million from the Australian Open and Australian Grand Prix, which management said recur every Q4.

segments.name: APS (AP Securitas)
segments.commentary: Q4 EBITDA margin 4.2%, against 5% per one answer and 5.5% for SIS Security ex-APS; management targets closing the 50 bps gap over 18 months or more.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for 15%+ growth and 15%+ ROCE/ROE on a multi-year basis; it gave no segment-level guidance.
EBITDA margins are expected to hover around 5-6.5%; management declined to say whether 6% is reachable in FY27 or FY28.
APS margin gap closure to SIS levels is targeted over roughly 1-1.5 years via branch consolidation, back-office sharing and procurement integration.
Cash business (Q-Comm-type cash logistics) IPO is deferred; management hopes to proceed within FY27, with SEBI extending DRHP validity to September 30.
Management said a Rs 20,000 crore revenue figure attributed to it in the press was a misquote, though possible.
Labour Code wage pass-through is built into contracts; working-capital benefits from invoicing and collection changes are possible but unquantified.
capex_capacity: Depreciation rose INR15 crore QoQ, of which INR10 crore relates to a new Australian office lease (MSS lease), implying about INR40 crore annually.
25 residential training facilities across 14 states; supply centres in eastern, East India and Central India states.
Workforce of about 343,000 on payroll.
Management cited depreciation averaging about 1.2% of revenue since FY21.
demand_pricing: Management said Labour Codes and minimum-wage hikes are a positive: Haryana raised minimum wages by about 50%, UP by about 28% (later referred to as about 20%), and Punjab and Uttarakhand by over 15% in the last 30 days.
SIS prices a few percentage points above local competitors, attributed to service fees, technology, training and kit fees.
Management said SIS holds about 5% security market share; the largest security firms in the US and UK hold more than 15%.
Management said SIS is about twice the size of Group 4, the next-largest Indian security company.
Corporate offices make up less than 10% of FM customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FM margin sustainable and what is the monthly run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Rituraj Sinha said FM margins have moved from 4.5% or lower to about 5.5% and are sustainable. Monthly run rate was cited at INR31 crore versus INR21 crore a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: How long are International contracts and what was the Q4 bump?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikram Kannoth said Australia and New Zealand contracts run 3-5 years. Q4 events (Australian Open and Grand Prix) added about AUD20 million (about INR120 crore) without matching headcount, and Q1 normalises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the APS integration plan and margin gap?
qa_highlights.answer: APS Q4 margin was corrected to 4.2% against SIS Security's 5.5%. Management expects the gap to close over 1-1.5 years via branch consolidation, back-office sharing and procurement.

qa_highlights.question: Was the INR290 crore labour code charge reversal recognised in the P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: Brajesh Kumar said the INR38.8 crore reassessment must go through OCI under accounting norms. Future costs are passed through in customer rate cards; past-period amounts will be recovered when paid to retiring employees.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROE aspiration and how is the cash business IPO progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has no formal ROE target, but aims for 15%+ growth and returns above 15%, and wants PAT of INR500 crore to enter the top 100 listed companies. The cash IPO is deferred due to geopolitics and IPO market conditions; the company hopes to proceed in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation and expected credit loss rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation rose INR15 crore QoQ, of which INR10 crore was the Australian lease. Credit loss allowance rose to about INR50 crore from about INR20 crore YoY, which management called prudent provisioning requested by the Audit Committee.

risks_watch: Gratuity/leave liability: INR290 crore charge taken in Q3; recovery of past-period costs from clients is still under discussion and not accrued.
International revenue depends on Q4 event timing (Australian Open, Grand Prix); management says Q1 normalises.
APS margin at 4.2% against a target of about 5.5%; integration timing is 1-1.5 years or more.
Expected credit loss allowance rose to about INR50 crore from about INR20 crore YoY; management attributed this to prudence.
Minimum-wage hikes across several states could raise costs before pass-through, and labour unrest was reported in Haryana and Greater Noida.
Cash business IPO timing depends on geopolitics and market conditions; no fixed date.
FM headcount declined from about 85,000 to 82,000 and FM revenue growth was 8.1%.
540673|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY26 and Labour Code tailwinds, but cautious on the cash IPO timing and evasive on FY27 segment growth and when margins reach 6%. Management pushed back firmly on questions about one-offs and depreciation.
key_quotes: This industry is not a 10% EBITDA margin industry. This is a growth and ROCE industry.
The barriers are not to entry, the barriers are to scale.
So FY26 is a good story.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin at 4.6% in Q4 with a 5-6.5% guided range; FM margin rose to 5.5% from about 4.5% and APS gap of 4.2% vs 5.5% for SIS Security is targeted to close over 18 months via branch consolidation, but Q4 event revenue normalises and management declined to say 6% is reachable in FY27 or FY28.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or branches are guided; the only addition is the Australian MSS office lease adding about INR40 crore annual depreciation, not productive capacity, and the 25 training facilities are existing.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets around 15% multi-year revenue growth against Q4 growth of 31% (flattered by APS consolidation and Australian events), Security ex-APS grew only 11%, and FM grew 8.1% with headcount falling from 85,000 to 82,000.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex not discussed; utilisation not disclosed, so no utilisation-driven capex call can be made.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no segment guidance and no upgrade; the 15%+ multi-year growth and 5-6.5% EBITDA margin range were only reiterated or newly framed, with 6% reachability declined.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gratuity reversal of INR38.8 crore is through OCI and the INR290 crore past-period recovery is not accrued, Q4 International included about AUD20 million of event revenue (about INR120 crore) that normalises in Q1, and credit loss allowance rose to about INR50 crore from about INR20 crore, with minimum-wage hikes (Haryana about 50%, UP about 28%) possibly raising costs before pass-through.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products, brands or service lines were discussed.

rows.label: Labour Code working-capital benefit from invoicing and collections
rows.why: Management said benefits are possible but unquantified, while DSO already fell 4 days QoQ to 63 days.

rows.label: Cash business (Q-Comm-type cash logistics) IPO
rows.why: IPO is deferred on geopolitics and market conditions, with the DRHP validity extended to September 30 and no fixed date; management hopes to proceed in FY27.

rows.label: Labour Code gratuity/leave past-period recovery from clients
rows.why: The INR290 crore Q3 charge has only INR38.8 crore reversed through OCI, and recovery of past-period costs is under discussion and not accrued, so any recovery is an upside not in the numbers.

tone.note: Management was confident on record FY26 results, Labour Code pass-through and the FM margin at about 5.5%, but cautious on cash IPO timing and evasive on FY27 segment growth and when margins reach 6%; analysts pushed on one-offs, the INR290 crore gratuity charge, depreciation and credit loss allowan

540673|2026-06.headline: SIS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29.7% YoY to INR 4,604 crore; consolidated EBITDA up 36.2% to INR 207 crore at 4.5% margin.
540673|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR 4,604 crore, up 29.7% YoY and 2.5% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR 207 crore (4.5% margin), flat QoQ but up 36.2% YoY. PAT was INR 101.7 crore (2.2% margin). India Security crossed INR 2,000 crore in quarterly revenue for the first time, while International Security hit its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR 1,982 crore. Management tied the coming quarters to labour code implementation (rules notified 8-9 May 2026) and minimum wage pass-throughs, and announced an open-market buyback of INR 106 crore at a maximum price of INR 478.50.

segments.name: India Security
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 2,004 crore (+37.3% YoY), first quarter above INR 2,000 crore; EBITDA INR 103 crore at 5.1% margin. Management said the acquired A P Securitas business, with revenue INR 332 crore and EBITDA INR 12.2 crore in the quarter, runs at lower margin and will be integrated over 4 to 8 quarters.

segments.name: Facility Management
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 642 crore (+8% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 5.5%, which management described as a normalised new level. Aspirational target is near 6%.

segments.name: International Security (Australia-led)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,982 crore (+31% YoY, +7% constant currency), highest ever quarterly run rate; EBITDA INR 69.6 crore (+52% YoY) at 3.5% margin, down from Q4 as high-margin events fade in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Management expects labour code implementation to be accretive to EBITDA and PAT over the next 3-4 quarters, with impact more visible in Q2 and Q3.
Minimum wage hikes in several states (Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana, Uttarakhand) reportedly ranged 20% to 47%; management expects more state-level hikes over the next 6-9 months.
India business margins targeted to move from about 5.3-5.4% blended toward 5.5-6%.
Acquired business margins expected to converge toward the group's original margin profile over 4 to 8 quarters through integration and synergies.
Open-market buyback of INR 106 crore, maximum price INR 478.50, expected to open the week after the call; promoters not participating.
capex_capacity: Acquired 51% stake in an entity (A P Securitas referenced) roughly 20% of SIS's size; remaining 49% to be acquired over the next couple of years, with anniversary in 2028.
Cash business IPO: DRHP filed; management is waiting for a more opportune window given peer de-rating, and declined to share its financials.
Buyback: fifth buyback approved; cumulative capital returned would exceed INR 700 crore after completion.
demand_pricing: Contracts have open-book costing and rise-and-fall clauses; minimum wage hikes are passed through to clients, with a time lag from invoicing and customer payment cycles, not tied to contract renewal.
Australia minimum wage rise of 4.75% was flagged by an analyst; management said contracts pass it through via rise-and-fall clauses.

Management says 30-40% of Indian customers use compliant operators versus about 90% in Australia; the new principal-employer definition in the labour codes is expected to shift the cost arbitrage to clients.
SIS manages more than 16,000 contracts in India; no single contract exceeds 1% of revenue.
No labour shortage beyond the usual April-June pre-monsoon seasonal pattern, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What were the revenue and EBITDA of A P Securitas this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue INR 332 crore and EBITDA INR 12.2 crore (CFO Brajesh Kumar).

qa_highlights.question: Did labour shortage affect the business and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nothing exceptional; the April-June shortage is seasonal and eases by July, in line with prior years.

qa_highlights.question: How will state minimum wage hikes affect SIS and when will they be passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Hikes are passed through to clients as a revenue boost, EBITDA-accretive with little gross-margin impact; the Q1 effect is limited since the process began 8 May, with Q2-Q3 more visible.

qa_highlights.question: Are India margins sustainable and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: India blended margin is about 5.3-5.4% (Security 5.1%, FM 5.5%); management said it is sustainable and aims for 5.5-6%.

qa_highlights.question: Australia: will the 4.75% wage hike be passed on only at contract renewal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rise-and-fall clauses allow immediate pass-through, with only a billing and payment lag, not dependent on renewal dates; the Australia CEO was to follow up separately, and the line was disrupted.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Updater Services share purchase a treasury operation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is a treasury operation and that it is the only single stock bought so far.

risks_watch: Pace and extent of state-level minimum wage notifications and whether pass-through lags delay margin benefit beyond Q3.
Working capital: DSO rose 3 days to 66 days; management attributes this to seasonality and it needs to revert in later quarters.
International Security margin at 3.5% is sensitive to the fading of Australian Q4 high-margin events and to currency effects.
Integration of the acquired 51% stake, which runs at lower margin than the core security business.
Smaller-operator cost arbitrage narrowing under the new principal-employer rules is management's view; its actual effect on share and pricing is not yet evident.
540673|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on labour code tailwinds, buyback and return ratios. Evasive on the Cash business IPO financials, the Australia wage-pass-through follow-up (line disrupted), and contract-level detail for the Hyderabad business.
key_quotes: So, it is completely designed for our minority shareholders. Promoters are not participating.
This is a tectonic shift. It has not happened before in this industry.
We want to drive SIS into that box of 100 companies in this country which deliver INR 500 crore plus in PAT

540678|2026-06.headline: Cochin Shipyard Q1 FY27 PAT fell to INR 151.45 crore from INR 187.82 crore on turnover of INR 1,094.21 crore; ISRF JV with DP World's Drydocks World valued at INR 1,800 crore.
540678|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 turnover rose about 2.4% YoY to INR 1,094.21 crore, but PBT fell to INR 202.49 crore from INR 249.54 crore and PAT to INR 151.45 crore from INR 187.82 crore. Management cited EBITDA margin around 24% and PAT margin around 14% for the quarter. The company delivered three vessels in the period, plus three by subsidiary Udupi Cochin Shipyard. Management announced several strategic moves: a 50:50 JV with Drydocks World for the ISRF ship repair facility, a scaled-down block fabrication plan after HD KSOE talks failed, a Tuticorin hybrid yard lease, and a Green Maritime battery JV.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 1,068.59 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +2.4%)
vs INR 249.54 crore in Q1 FY26 (about -19%)
vs INR 187.82 crore in Q1 FY26 (about -19%)
Around INR 27,000 crore after NGSV contract (L1, about INR 5,000 crore)

segments.name: Shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Management said shipbuilding is about 70% of turnover at 10-12% EBITDA margin. Deliveries in FY27 so far include the third of eight ASW shallow water crafts, a second multipurpose vessel for a German client, and a Ro-Ro ferry for Kochi Municipal Corporation.

segments.name: Ship repair
segments.commentary: Ship repair is about 30% of turnover at roughly 20-24% EBITDA margin. ISRF has a 6,000-ton ship lift, about 1,400 m berthing and annual capacity of up to 82 ships.

segments.name: Udupi Cochin Shipyard (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Delivered three vessels in the period: two 3,800 TDW general cargo vessels to Wilson Group, Norway, and a 70-tonne bollard pull tug to Polestar Maritime (Adani Group). Management said land constraints limit its new order intake.

segments.name: Green Maritime battery JV (with HBL, 40% CSL)
segments.commentary: Incorporated June 2026 for marinized energy storage systems. Target revenue INR 640 crore by year 5 and about 20% EBITDA margin (ballpark, business plan not final). Total capital INR 50 crore; no manufacturing facility, as HBL will manufacture.

guidance_outlook: Turnover growth guidance of about 12% per year, with management saying it could reach 12-15%.
Blended EBITDA margin guided at around 14-15% for the year on a conservative basis, down from prior years' higher margins.

Target to deliver about 10 vessels in FY27 (three delivered so far in Q1): two more ASWs by December 2026, two more multipurpose vessels, a trailing suction hopper dredger next month, and commissioning service vessels and Samskip container vessels through early 2027.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive in FY27 as delivery-linked milestone payments come in.
ISRF JV transaction targeted for completion before end of FY27, subject to Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, DIPAM, and CSL shareholder (postal ballot) approvals.
New investments targeted at a return on capital of about 14-15%.
capex_capacity: ISRF JV: INR 1,800 crore slump-sale consideration, 50% in cash and 50% in JV equity. Expected revenue about INR 600 crore over the next 2 years, scaling to INR 1,000-1,200 crore over 5 years. Plan adds 10 workstations.

Block fabrication: Earlier 1 lakh tonne plan with HD KSOE is now a solo facility of about 60,000 tonnes per annum. Current capacity is about 12,000 tonnes per annum, for total throughput near 72,000 tonnes.

Vadinar (Gujarat) ship repair with Deendayal Port Authority: two floating drydocks for ~250 m vessels. CCEA approval received May 2026. Environmental clearance expected shortly; operations targeted within 36 months of EC. Revenue about INR 300-600 crore after 3 years.

Tuticorin (V.O. Chidambaranar Port): won 30-year lease at one-time payment of INR 305.76 crore for about 110 acres land and 17.29 acres waterfront. In DPR stage; revenue of INR 650-700 crore initially, scaling to INR 1,800-2,000 crore over 7-8 years.

Total capex over about 5 years estimated by an analyst at INR 6,000-6,500 crore across the four projects. Funding targeted at about 80:20 debt-equity. Applied for Shipbuilding Development Scheme (25% capex subsidy) and MDF Interest Incentivisation Fund (up to 3% interest subvention).
demand_pricing: Defence pipeline per management: LPD (4 numbers, about INR 32,000 crore), MCMV (12 numbers, about INR 36,000 crore), P-17 Bravo (7 numbers, about INR 49,000 crore). Management said these are RFPs with competition; LPD and MCMV seen as more suitable than P-17 Bravo.
NGSV: CSL is L1 for five next-generation survey vessels worth about INR 5,000 crore; order signing expected around November 2026. Navy procedures are slow (CCS and PNC approvals).

Commercial: Dredging Corporation of India sister dredger (about INR 1,300 crore, nomination basis) expected within about two months. Andaman 4 x 500-passenger vessels under nomination discussion. Government demand aggregation for about 432 vessels over 10 years, with SCI/BCSL tenders in progress. MR tanker technical bid indicative cost about INR 1,700 crore; Aframax EOI indicative cost about INR 2,600 crore.
Export: European commercial vessels from 2023-24 orders are 80-90% complete but only about 30% paid; payment is tail-ended (around 70% on delivery).
Management said the Green Tug Transition Program could create about INR 1,000 crore of battery-led investment over 10 years, with real volume expected in 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Green Maritime battery JV: product basket, 3-year scale, and timing of meaningful contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Target product range is marine energy storage and power management systems, with revenue target of INR 640 crore by year 5. Management said the JV will not contribute much revenue immediately; it has placed an order for the battery systems for four green tugs being built, and the JV's turnover will be battery-system only, not the tug. Total capital is INR 50 crore, with no manufacturing facility; HBL manufactures.

qa_highlights.question: ISRF JV with Drydocks World: will it serve DP World vessels only, and how is overlap with CSL's business handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CSL will take orders and the JV will execute them, with DDW free to bring in its own clients. Management said the ISRF only handles vessels up to 130 m and 6,000 tonnes, larger vessels go to the main yard, and the two parties have a clear understanding that DDW will not enter CSL's other segments.

qa_highlights.question: Defence and commercial order pipeline and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence RFPs: LPD 4 numbers (about INR 32,000 crore), MCMV 12 numbers (about INR 36,000 crore), P-17 Bravo 7 numbers (about INR 49,000 crore). NGSV contract expected around November 2026. DCI sister dredger (about INR 1,300 crore, nomination) expected within about two months. Demand aggregation of 432 vessels over 10 years is in tender stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 operating cash flow negative, and what are the normalised cash conversion and ROC targets?
qa_highlights.answer: European export contracts are tail-ended: about 30% received against 80-90% construction completion, with 70% due on delivery. Management expects operating cash flow to turn positive in FY27 as deliveries come in, and targets a return on new investments of about 14-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why are EBITDA margins falling from the past three years, and how should the 14% full-year guide be read against a Q1 margin above 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Past higher margins came from nominated orders (indigenous aircraft carrier, two aircraft carrier refits) and interest income on a cash surplus of INR 2,000-3,000 crore that has been used for ISRF and drydock capex, so is no longer available. Shipbuilding runs at 10-12% EBITDA margin (about 70% of turnover) and ship repair at 20-24% (about 30%), giving a blended 14-15% on a conservative basis. Management said EBITDA includes interest income as a recurring item.

qa_highlights.question: Vessel delivery schedule for FY27 and the capex revenue potential for the four new projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is about 10 deliveries in FY27, with three done. Two more ASWs by December 2026, two more MPVs, a trailing suction hopper dredger next month, two Cyprus commissioning service vessels (October 2026 and around February/March 2027), and one Samskip container vessel by February. ISRF revenue of about INR 600 crore over 2 years, rising to INR 1,000-1,200 crore over 5 years. Vadinar about INR 300 crore after 36 months from EC. Tuticorin INR 650-700 crore initially, scaling to INR 1,800-2,000 crore over 7-8 years. Funding around 80:20 debt-equity, with 25% capex subsidy and 3% interest subvention applied for.

risks_watch: Full-year EBITDA margin guide of 14-15% sits well below prior years; loss of nominated, high-margin defence and refit work and of interest income from the cash surplus are the drivers.

Operating cash flow was negative in FY26 and is expected to turn positive only in FY27, dependent on about 7 vessels of delivery-linked milestone payments (around 70% of contract value) from European export orders that are about 30% paid.

Order inflow depends on RFPs and tenders with uncertain timing: NGSV (about INR 5,000 crore, expected around November 2026), DCI dredger (about INR 1,300 crore), and MR and Aframax tenders. Management declined to give a timeline for LPD, MCMV and P-17 Bravo.
ISRF JV needs MoPSW, DIPAM and CSL postal-ballot approvals before completion, targeted before end FY27. Watch for the postal ballot notice and EC for Vadinar.

Green Maritime JV economics are not final: the business plan is still being prepared, the 20% EBITDA margin is ballpark, and the JV's revenue is battery-only and largely unconsolidated (CSL holds 40%).

Capex of about INR 6,000-6,500 crore across four projects relies on subsidy and interest support; monitor debt levels, the 80:20 funding mix and execution of the block fabrication facility, now solo at about 60,000 tpa.
key_quotes: Since then, CSL and HD KSOE have had series of discussions and engagements. However, we have not been able to arrive at a mutually agreed definitive terms for establishing BF facility through a joint venture.

So, we have, between the 2 of us, have a very clear understanding that there will be no ingress into that market by DDW, and the current market share of CSL in the other segments will continue to be held by CSL.
So, blended will be around 14%, 15%, something like that on a very conservative basis.
But going forward, we cannot expect such margins from the commercial orders or the defense order, because now all the tenders from the defense is also on a tender basis.
540678|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on the order pipeline, the ISRF JV and capex revenue targets, but cautious on margins and cash flow. It said the defence and commercial tenders are outside its control and gave no firm timelines, and it declined to give a firm margin for the Green Maritime JV or other ventures, calling the figures ballpark.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Full-year blended EBITDA margin guided to ~14-15% (conservative) versus Q1 at ~24%, as nominated defence/refit work and interest income on the INR 2,000-3,000 cr cash surplus (now used for capex) roll off; shipbuilding runs 10-12% vs ship repair 20-24%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

540692|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 14% to INR931 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 405 bps to 7.7%, while Q4 volume fell to 1,912 MT from 2,349 MT.

Q4 FY26 revenue was INR168 crore versus INR197 crore, on volume of 1,912 MT versus 2,349 MT, while Q4 EBITDA margin rose to 9.8%. Non-US markets, led by the EU (up 19% in FY26, 15% in Q4), became the largest sales contributor at about 52% for the first time, as US volumes fell on tariffs and logistics disruption. Management expects US volumes to recover now that tariffs have fallen to about 10%, and it is targeting roughly 30% volume growth in FY27, though it said this is subject to production and shipping constraints.

segments.commentary: EU grew 19% YoY in FY26 and 15% in Q4 FY26; management says the EU accounts for about 50% of total volume. UK FTA is expected soon and EU FTA around end of calendar 2026.

qa_highlights.answer: Rebate of about 5% to 6% of exports, subject to caps and no policy change; management described it as a duty reimbursement rather than an incentive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East impact on logistics?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight costs rose only marginally; the main issue is shipping line equipment shortages causing 3 to 5 day shipment delays.

Farm-gate price trends and government feed-price measures in Andhra Pradesh.

Sustainability of margin, which management linked partly to inventory usage and favourable raw material prices.

540692|2026-06.headline: Apex Frozen Foods Q1 FY27 PAT rose 138% YoY to INR22 crores on 15% higher shrimp realisation (INR930/kg), despite 13% lower volumes at 2,624 MT.
540692|2026-06.overview: Revenue was flat at INR257 crores against INR258 crores a year earlier, while EBITDA rose 79% to INR33 crores and margin expanded to 12.7% from 7.1%. Shrimp sales volume fell to 2,624 MT from 3,015 MT, hit by April-May labour shortages, container and equipment shortages, and EU shipment clearance delays that spilled into Q2. Management kept full-year production guidance at around 12,000 MT and said Q2 volume should recover, subject to global transport normalising. Realisation was guided to hold near INR900 per kg in Q2.

segments.name: USA
segments.commentary: Accounted for 70% of shrimp sales in Q1 FY27 vs 54% a year earlier; sales rose 13% YoY and 121% QoQ. Pricing includes a 10% tariff plus ADD/CVD (about 9%).

segments.commentary: Contributed 25% of shrimp sales vs 39% in Q1 FY26, hit by war-led transport disruption and origin-side testing and certification requirements; management said EU volumes spilled into Q2.

Q2 volume recovery expected, subject to global transport normalisation; order book covers sales until about mid-Q3 FY27.

demand_pricing: Realisation of INR930/kg is up about INR80-90/kg YoY, helped by higher USD unit values, a weaker rupee and a higher RTE mix.
US buyers placed more orders after tariff uncertainty eased; the 10% tariff has been stable since the start of the year.
Farm-gate prices rose about 6-7% over the 3-4 weeks before the call; Q1 prices were described as stable.
Management said realisations above a certain level would hurt consumption and volumes, as in FY22-23.
UK-India FTA effective 15 July 2026, but non-tariff barriers such as 50% testing of Indian shipments remain; EU FTA expected around December 2026 or January 2027.
Ocean freight costs have more than doubled since Q4 FY26 due to war-led disruption.

qa_highlights.question: How are fish meal and feed price increases affecting farmers and the company, and are they temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said feed manufacturing is not part of the business. Farm-gate prices rising gave farmers comfort; margins should stay stable, with freight and farm-gate price increases as partial offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume below the 12,500-14,000 MT run-rate, and what growth is expected for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is about 12,000 MT. Q1 was hit by labour shortage and container shortages, and EU shipments slipped into Q2, which made US volumes look high. The order book is firm to mid-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RTE contribution and its margin premium over RTC?
qa_highlights.answer: RTE was 16% of Q1 volume and is expected to reach at least 18-20% in FY27. The margin premium is at least USD 0.50/kg over RTC, with some products higher.

qa_highlights.question: Will US tariff refunds be received?
qa_highlights.answer: No refunds have been received yet. Timing and outcome are unclear because of ongoing US legal proceedings.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 realisation a new high versus history, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Similar levels were seen in FY22 during COVID phase 2, but those were driven by panic buying and hurt volumes. The company aims for a sustainable level through a richer value-added mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US CVD and ADD outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: ADD is at 3.4%, up from 1.35%, with a final determination around September 2026. CVD could fall by about 5.77% in December 2026 if duty drawback and RoDTEP are accepted as non-subsidies.

qa_highlights.question: What new adjacent products are being commercialised?
qa_highlights.answer: Proprietary customer-developed RTE and RTC products are already being shipped, estimated at 3-4% of sales (about 300-400 MT on 12,000 MT), rising to about 500 MT annually.

540699|2026-03.headline: Dixon Q4 FY26 revenue flat at INR10,520 crore; FY26 revenue up 26% to INR48,893 crore, with FY27 guided to INR56,000 crore ex-Vivo.
540699|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was flat, with management citing geopolitical concerns, softer consumer demand, brand inventory rationalisation and memory-chip cost inflation in smartphones and IT hardware. Q4 EBITDA excluding exceptional gain was INR418 crore and PAT after minority interest was INR192 crore. For the full year, revenue rose 26% to INR48,893 crore and PAT rose 20% to INR845 crore, excluding exceptional gain. Management guided FY27 to about INR56,000 crore excluding Vivo, with mobile volumes flat and smartphone selling prices up 12-15%, and said the PLI roll-off will compress margins this year.

540699|2026-06.headline: Dixon Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR15,557 crore, but EBITDA of INR472 crore (ex fair value gain) and PAT of INR218 crore reflect margin compression as Mobile PLI 1 expired.
540699|2026-06.overview: Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was INR15,557 crore, with EBITDA of INR472 crore and PAT after minority interest of INR218 crore, both excluding the fair value gain on the Aditya Infotech stake. Management attributed the margin compression to the expiry of Mobile PLI 1 in March 2026 and to input cost pass-through, which lowers percentage margins optically, mainly in mobile and IT hardware. Management guided against margin recovery in the current fiscal and pointed to FY28 for component-led margin improvement. Working capital absorbed roughly INR800 crore in the quarter, which management called temporary, linked to strategic inventory build and payouts of end-March cash.

540701|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 19% to INR 851 crore, with EBITDA of INR 163 crore (19.1%) despite INR 30 crore extra onerous-contract provisions.
540701|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 851 crore, up about 19% YoY, with CDMO up 21% to INR 690.8 crore and marketable molecules up 9.3% to INR 160.5 crore. EBITDA was about INR 163 crore (19.1% margin), held back by roughly INR 50 crore higher other expenses from onerous-contract provisions and a one-off CHF 2.5 million Swiss pension provision. For FY26, revenue was INR 2,932 crore (up about 8%), EBITDA INR 565 crore (19.3%, up 200 bps) and PAT INR 97.4 crore versus INR 3.2 crore. Management announced a promoter-entity 10-year unsecured external commercial borrowing, subject to shareholder approval, to repay high-cost Indian debt.

qa_highlights.question: How should depreciation and tax rate be modelled for FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation has been broadly flat QoQ in functional currency, with FX translation adding to INR figures. Effective tax rate is seen at about 40% in FY27, about 30% in FY28, and 15-20% in about three years as loss-making subsidiaries turn profitable.

qa_highlights.question: Will interest cost fall after refinancing, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly interest could be INR 30-35 crore, conservatively from Q2 or Q3 FY27, after replacing about INR 800 crore of Indian debt costing about 10.5-11% with cheaper promoter-entity borrowing at about 4%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there FX risk from the Swiss-franc borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Swiss-franc revenue from India and subsidiaries acts as a natural hedge, so no hedging is planned. It cited India revenue of about INR 5,000 crore in foreign currency over the 10-year tenor against about INR 800 crore of debt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 India outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 India revenue and profit are expected to be above FY26, with FY28 target of about INR 500 crore; the FY27 figure may be below the INR 400 crore mentioned. Management said the target holds whether or not the Swiss tech transfer proceeds.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the goodwill increase from INR 4,054 crore to INR 4,798 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was purely FX restatement at closing rates, with no additions. About INR 550 crore is standalone India goodwill from the 2017 merger and the rest is consolidation goodwill.

qa_highlights.question: Why did borrowings rise and cash build up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said syndicated facilities were drawn to avoid commitment fees and the USD proceeds are held as deposits earning interest, while Swiss-franc borrowing costs under 4%. Management said net debt is the right metric.

qa_highlights.question: What is the French subsidiary outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 French revenue was about EUR 8 million with EBITDA loss of about EUR 9 million. FY27 target is EUR 11-12 million revenue and about EUR 6 million loss; breakeven is aimed for FY28, which the analyst noted had slipped.

540701|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell 4% to INR 6,776 mn and EBITDA to INR 600 mn, mainly from an INR 10 mn order deferred to H2.
540701|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 6,776 mn versus INR 7,080 mn a year earlier, a 4% decline, which management attributed mainly to an order pushed from Q1 into the latter half of FY27. EBITDA fell to INR 600 mn from INR 1,406 mn, and the company posted a loss before tax of about INR 512 mn after finance costs of about INR 370 mn and an FX loss of about INR 117.3 mn. The CDMO segment revenue fell to INR 5,343 mn while Marketable Molecules rose to INR 1,432 mn. Management guided to single-digit group revenue growth for FY27 with EBITDA margin similar to or slightly above FY26, and said a promoter-level ECB of up to CHF 200 mn is expected to close in 60-90 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why does cash stay overseas rather than repay India debt?

540716|2026-03.headline: ICICI Lombard FY26 PBT rose 10.2% to ₹36.59bn and 1/n PAT 10.5% to ₹27.72bn; Q4 GDPI grew 18.2% but FY26 GDPI grew only 7.0%.
540716|2026-03.overview: FY26 profit grew double digits despite a ₹0.55bn wage code charge, with Q4 1/n PAT up 7.3% to ₹5.47bn. Top-line growth was 7.0% for FY26 versus the industry's 9.2%, with commercial lines lagging (5.4%) and retail health (51.1%) and Q4 motor (15.0%) accelerating. Management flagged intensifying commercial and fire competition, a Motor TP loss ratio it says is overdue for repricing, and a transition to Ind AS starting FY27 with a plan to seek forbearance. Solvency stayed high at 2.67x and the final dividend was ₹7.00 per share (₹13.50 total).

Ind AS: IRDAI mandates Ind AS from April 1, 2026. The company intends to seek forbearance for the first year and will submit quarterly pro forma Ind AS numbers from Q1 FY27. Management guided to a 300-450 bps combined ratio decline in the adoption year, with economic value converging over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 Motor TP loss ratio much lower, and why is the crop loss ratio negative? Has IFRS PAT been quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said to judge Motor as a category over full year (66.3%, range 65-67%) and reserving philosophy is unchanged. Crop was booked mostly in Q2 at about 100% loss ratio, and the Q4 release reflects favourable experience. No Ind AS PAT quantification yet; the company will return with CoR and ROE impact.

qa_highlights.question: Solvency is high at 2.7x; can excess capital be deployed via dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Solvency 1 (exposure-based capital) and a pending risk-based capital transition. It will use some solvency for growth as growth returns, and continues a dividend policy of about 25% of PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Health loss ratio split between retail and group, and Motor TP price hike outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Employer-employee loss ratio was 98.1% in Q4 and 91.9% for FY26; retail indemnity was 57.6% in Q4 and 64.6% for FY26, with a 65-70% target range. Industry Motor TP loss ratio is about 85%, and a price hike is overdue but not in the company's control.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company claw back commercial market share and sustain 16% H2 growth into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 share fell about 0.7-0.8 pp from 13.7% and it will be selective, not chasing volume. It expects an industry growth slowdown in commercial, possibly single digit, and was confident of positive Q1 and Q2 but declined to predict the H2 run-rate.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of H2 motor outperformance and FY27 outlook, and the Motor TP reserve and CV growth question?
qa_highlights.answer: New vehicle sales grew 18.8% for the company vs 13.4% for renewals; retention improved about 5%. CV share of book remained around 22%, with cost of acquisition and a fleet management system cited. Management declined to give the Motor TP reserve figure as a useful metric.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the commission (EOM) tightening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tightening applied uniformly would benefit ICICI Lombard, which says it has stayed within expense-of-management limits. It favours a single-slab EOM structure and awaits regulatory direction.

540716|2026-06.headline: ICICI Lombard Q1 FY27 PAT fell 46.0% to ₹4.03 bn, driven by a ₹1.65 bn Motor TP judgement provision and two large Fire losses.
540716|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 GDPI grew 7.5% to ₹83.18 bn, below industry growth of 10.9%, with retail lines driving growth while commercial lines de-grew 13.8%. Combined ratio rose to 107.2% from 102.9%, including a 2.8 pp hit from the Supreme Court Motor TP judgement provision and a 1.0 pp hit from two Fire large losses. Excluding these items, the combined ratio was 102.3% versus 102.2% a year ago, and PAT would have been ₹5.75 bn (down 23.0%). Investment income fell to ₹11.74 bn from ₹12.88 bn as capital gains halved, partly offset by higher portfolio yield and duration.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: De-grew 13.8% in Q1 FY27 amid pricing pressure; SME share rose to 33.6% from 28.4%. Fire line declined 27.8% for the industry and the company de-grew about 32%; June Fire de-growth improved to about 18% for the company.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Grew 14.0% in line with industry (13.9%), market share 10.5%; new vehicle sales up 33.6% vs industry 14.9%. Mix: private car 49.8%, two-wheeler 28.7%, commercial vehicle 21.5%. Motor combined ratio 106.6% in FY26 vs industry 128.0%.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Grew 24.9% vs industry 20.1%. Retail Health grew 69.5% with share up to 4.5% from 3.5%; Group Health grew 16.3% with 10.3% share. Management attributed the higher health loss ratio to industry-wide claim incidence, not company-specific.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give a quantified forward impact of the Motor TP judgement; said it is too early and will update each quarter.
Expects an upward Motor TP premium rate revision; judgement-driven industry loss ratio impact estimated at 12-15%, which it sees as the minimum price change needed.
Expects Fire price aggression to moderate after Q1, though full recovery of de-growth in the rest of the year is uncertain.
Health claim incidence watch-point for Q2 (monsoon-linked); next detailed update to come with October results.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning plans were discussed on the call; the call covered underwriting, pricing, reserving and claims only.

Capacity was referenced only qualitatively: management said reinsurance renewals were relatively soft and capacity had been made available across the industry, which drove Fire price competition. No company-specific capacity figures were given.

Motor claims and servicing scale were cited as operating metrics, not capacity: Preferred Partner Network served 75.6% of non-OEM motor claims in Q1 FY27 vs 74.6% in Q1 FY26; 168,521 health and travel claims were serviced through the IL TakeCare app vs 141,116 a year earlier.
Digital servicing capacity: digital interactions rose to 624K in Q1 FY27 from 214K in Q1 FY26; digital share of servicing was 69.0% in Q1 FY27 and 71.0% in June 2026.
Management did not discuss any new product launches, branch or distribution expansion, or timelines for system or platform commissioning.
demand_pricing: Industry Fire rates were cut sharply in the April renewal cycle; the reinsurance renewal was relatively soft, enabling capacity and competition.
Motor TP has seen no third-party price change for several years; the judgement adds a Motor TP loss ratio impact of 12-15% for the industry.
Retail Health share gain: contribution from long-term book in new retail health business rose to 53.4% from 31.8%.
Digital interactions rose to 624K from 214K; digital share of servicing 69% in Q1 FY27 and 71% in June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹165 crore (₹1.65 bn) Motor TP provision only for Q1 business, and will it recur each quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the provision is a holistic assessment of exposures as at June 30, covering past book as well as Q1 business; it declined to say whether it will recur, citing variability in future quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does the judgement affect closed cases, and what is the Fire loss ratio excluding the two large losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Closed cases typically do not reopen after court finality, so impact is largely on open exposures. Excluding the two large losses, Fire loss ratios should be within the historical 65-70% average range; the company has never exceeded 100% in Fire.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Health loss ratio rise despite GST benefit, and will it rise further in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise reflects industry-wide higher claim incidence, similar to last year's Q1; it is watching monsoon-linked claims into Q2 and will update in October.

qa_highlights.question: Arbitration award of about ₹78 crore: provision and impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The award relates to a policy about seven to eight years old and is on a gross basis; the company will pursue legal remedies and believes the net P&L impact is not material given reinsurance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the reserve prudence buffer still generate releases given the ₹165 crore charge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its reserving philosophy is unchanged, prudence will continue, and reserving triangles should continue to show favourable development over cycles.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Ex one-offs the combined ratio was 102.3% vs 102.2%, so no underlying expansion; management expects an upward Motor TP premium rate revision (12-15% industry loss-ratio impact) and Fire pricing to moderate after Q1, which could help margins but is not quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: Motor TP premium rate revision
rows.why: Management expects an upward Motor TP premium rate revision, with the judgement-driven industry loss-ratio impact estimated at 12-15%, which it sees as the minimum price change needed.

rows.label: Fire pricing normalisation

rows.label: Motor TP review petition and commission norms

540716|2026-09.headline: ICICI Lombard Q2 FY27 PAT rose 27.5% YoY to ₹10.31 bn, while H1 PAT fell 5.8% to ₹14.54 bn on a weaker Q1 and Motor TP reserving.
540716|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 profitability improved sharply: PBT grew 27.8% to ₹13.59 bn and PAT 27.5% to ₹10.31 bn, with combined ratio at 104.5% (102.7% ex-CAT). H1 was weaker, with PAT down 5.8% to ₹14.54 bn and combined ratio at 105.2%, reflecting the Q1 Supreme Court (Shishupal) Motor TP reserving of ₹1.65 bn and Q1 commercial large losses. GDPI grew 5.4% in H1 versus industry 8.9%, though ex-Crop and Mass Health Q2 growth of 13.9% was ahead of industry 13.2%. Management said no further Motor TP reserve top-up is needed and that the judgment is now business as usual.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: H1 growth 13.0% vs industry 13.1%, market share 10.3%; mix PC 49.8%, 2W 28.1%, CV 22.1%. Motor combined ratio 108.3% in Q1 FY27 vs industry 131.4%; management cites ~23 pts gap. H1 Motor loss ratio ~65.4% vs 66.6% last year.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: H1 growth 26.8% vs industry 21.0%. Retail Health grew 66.4% (industry 32.0%), share 4.7% in H1 and 5.0% exiting September. Group Health grew 15.4%, share stable at 8.8%; Group Health loss ratio 97.9% in Q2 vs 93.7% a year ago.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: Ex-Fire growth 20.0% in Q2 and 13.2% in H1. Fire de-growth moderated to 21.2% in Q2 from 32.1% in Q1, with September at -6.0%. Fire market share 11.9% in Q2 (11.4% prior year); Marine cargo 19.0%; Engineering 16.4%; Liability 16.6%.

segments.name: Crop
segments.commentary: Management said it was deliberately cautious in underwriting Crop this year, which muted headline top-line growth against NEP growth.

guidance_outlook: Management expects earned premium momentum to continue into Q3 and Q4, with gross premium growth ahead of industry.
No further Motor TP reserving requirement anticipated after the ₹1.65 bn Q1 provision; judgment treated as business as usual, with ongoing monitoring.
Motor loss ratio range kept at 65% to 67% (aggregate Motor), with Group Health underwritten around mid-90s and Retail Health at 65% to 70%.
Digital sourcing to be scaled from 6.0% to 15% of business under a defined roadmap.
Expense of management kept within the 30% limit on an annual basis; the draft 25% limit is seen as a positive for the company.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call.
Digital journeys handled 73% of customer interactions vs 39% a year ago; IL TakeCare app has 23.3 mn downloads.
Health underwriting WhatsApp GenAI bot used in over 40% of agency new business daily.
demand_pricing: Industry vehicle sales grew 21.1% in H1 FY27 and 26.9% in Q2, with September up 32.0%; management expects Motor growth to moderate on a higher base from Q3 after GST reform effects.
Retention improved 3% to 5% across retail lines (Motor and Health) in H1 vs last year.
Banca and corporate tie-ups contribute 12.5% to 15% of full-year premium, with single-digit exposure outside ICICI.
Reinsurance accepted is kept at a single-digit share of the overall book; management says no change in book quality in Q2.
Q2 Motor OD loss ratio was hit by Q2 flood events: ~₹118 mn of flood losses vs ~₹74-75 mn last year.

qa_highlights.question: Did Q1 Motor TP loss ratio jump reflect the Supreme Court judgment, and is more provisioning needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ₹1.65 bn was reserved in Q1 and no further reserving is needed; the judgment is now business as usual and development will be monitored over long cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Will IRDAI distribution reforms and commission cuts pressure third-party tariffs and renewals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reform is a recalibration that may lower costs and aid penetration, and tariff impact is uncertain. Retention rose 3% to 5%, and the company is increasing its renewal focus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Group Health and Retail Health loss ratio trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Group Health loss ratio was 97.9% in Q2 vs 93.7% a year ago, but down from ~99.9% in Q1. Retail indemnity was 64.6% vs 65.4% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Motor OD loss ratio deteriorate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to Q2 flood events (~₹118 mn vs ~₹74-75 mn last year). Ex-CAT, OD loss ratio was sequentially better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did commission and other opex ratios rise in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a higher retail mix, which carries higher acquisition cost but better loss outcomes, and said opex changes are business as usual.

qa_highlights.question: How would the 25% expense-of-management limit affect the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is well within the 30% EOM limit on an annual basis and sees the draft 25% limit as a positive for market share.

risks_watch: Motor TP tail development after the Shishupal judgment; any reserve release or strengthening in later quarters.
Distribution reform outcome: commission cuts, possible TP tariff changes, and POSP disruption in CV TP.
Commercial lines loss experience: Q1 large losses and Fire de-growth continuing; September Fire at -6.0%.
Base effect from GST reforms in Q3 and Q4 may moderate Motor growth.
IFRS transition impact not yet quantified; management said a separate briefing will follow.
Crop underwriting caution and Q2 flood/CAT events may weigh on loss ratios.
540716|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on Motor momentum, Health and Q2 recovery, but guarded on Commercial line loss trajectory and on the timing and economics of the distribution reforms, which management called "early days". Management was evasive on IFRS impact, saying it would revert at a later date.
key_quotes: Honestly, it is now a part of our business as usual and genuinely, we do not believe the need for us to separately call out any specific additional charge consequent to the Supreme Court judgment.
Motor is not a discretionary purchase. Motor is the law of the land where you are expected, if you are plying your vehicles on road, you are expected to have a coverage.
And the range that we have always spoken is to kind of see the book running at between 65% to 67%.

540719|2026-03.headline: SBI Life FY26 VoNB rose 12% to INR66.7bn at a 27.5% margin, but PAT grew only 2% to INR24.7bn due to GST and Labour Code one-offs.
540719|2026-03.overview: FY26 new business premium grew 20% to INR425.5bn with a 21.4% private market share, and individual APE grew 13% to INR221.1bn. Reported PAT rose only 2% to INR24.7bn; excluding GST and Labour Code impacts it would have been INR31.2bn (up 29%). VoNB was INR66.7bn (27.5% margin), and excluding GST it would have been INR70.3bn at a 29% margin. Management guided to around 14% growth and a 26-28% VoNB margin range, with the GST impact on commissions and expenses now reflected for the second half of FY26.

financial_highlights.change: +2% YoY; ex-GST and Labour Code INR31.2bn, +29%

segments.name: Individual protection
segments.commentary: Individual protection APE INR10.3bn (+24%); pure protection APE grew 122%; protection overall 9% of APE at INR22.4bn (+10%).

segments.name: Participating (par)
segments.commentary: Individual par APE INR17.3bn, up 133% on a low base after new par launches; par sum assured up 166%.

segments.name: Non-par guaranteed savings
segments.commentary: INR42.7bn of business, 19% of individual APE; a new non-par product was launched in January to reflect current yields.

segments.name: ULIP
segments.commentary: INR144.2bn, 65% of individual APE versus 70% last year; management cites a 66:34 ULIP:non-ULIP mix on an individual regular-premium basis.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group new business premium INR127.7bn (30% of new business premium, +39%); group credit life APE INR2.9bn (+14%).

segments.name: Bancassurance (SBI and RRBs)
segments.commentary: 60% of total APE; individual APE INR141.2bn (+11%); SBI branch productivity INR6.0m (+10%).

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Individual APE INR68.6bn (+15%); agent productivity INR2.6 lakh; non-ULIP share rose from 34% to 39%; over 1.2 lakh agents added gross and 120 branches opened.

segments.name: Other channels (direct, brokers, online, aggregators)
segments.commentary: Grew 22% and contributed 11% of total APE; online channel grew 47% on APE (own website 48-50%).

guidance_outlook: Medium-term APE growth target of around 14%, in line with the 3-5 year CAGR; FY26 individual APE growth was 13% versus 13% guidance.
VoNB margin guided to 26-28% range for FY27-28, with the company aiming to report above 27%; management declined to extend the range to FY27-29.
GST impact on first-year commission for business written before 22 September 2025 is about 1.8-1.9% of margin on an annual basis; management says it is largely absorbed in the 27.5% margin.
Opex ratio expected to carry a full year of GST in FY27, but management expects it not to rise materially; IT and branch spend to continue.
Deferred annuity (regular-pay) product targeted for launch by June 2026, otherwise the next quarter.
Ind AS transition: forbearance sought, with adoption from 1 April 2027.
capex_capacity: Opened 120 new branches in FY26 and added over 1.2 lakh agents on a gross basis; management says newer branches are on track but not yet at breakeven.
Continued investment planned in branches, IT infrastructure and agency training; management says no other major expense is planned beyond IT strengthening.
Solvency of 1.90 funded by internal accruals with no fresh capital raised; the company is assessing Ind AS and RBC impacts.
demand_pricing: Customers are investing where they see value despite geopolitical volatility; February and March growth was described as decent, and management expects continued sales growth.
Q4 bancassurance sales declined year on year; management said the whole insurance sector was sluggish in Q4 and that banca met its internal budget for the year.
Non-par pricing is being adjusted with interest rates; a new non-par product replaced the existing one to reflect current yields, passing some benefit to customers.
Management is not planning higher sum assured ULIPs for now, but will decide on launching them in due course.
Online business grew 47% on APE; 99.7% of individual proposals were submitted digitally and 57% of individual policies went through automated underwriting.

qa_highlights.question: Is the persistency assumption change a negative in the VNB walk, and is there a reset in persistency assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is about 50 bps and not significant; changes were minor refinements across mortality, persistency and expenses, with a persistency improvement from long-term protection.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 14% growth at risk given banca grew only 9-11% for three years, and is banca realistically 10-11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not guide channel-level growth; growth would come from agency and other channels, with 14% as an optimal mix. Protection growth is ticket-size-light and supports policy count.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 27-28% margin guidance conservative given FY26 ex-GST margin of 29%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a matter of perception; the range gives flexibility to balance 14% growth with margin, and the product mix is being improved.

qa_highlights.question: What is the GST impact on margins going forward and the opex ratio trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: GST for the second half is already in the 27.5% margin, and the full-year effect is about 1.8-1.9%. Opex ratio would be about 5.5% without GST and the Labour Code versus 5.3% in FY25; the 6.1% reflects GST and Labour Code costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EV operating variance strongly positive while VNB assumptions were strengthened?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said positive variance comes mainly from mortality and persistency, with lower expenses contributing. Assumption changes are minor refinements, and new and in-force business differ in product mix. Economic variance of 3.66% is split as 2.15% from equity, with the balance from bonds.

qa_highlights.question: Does open architecture in banca pose a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is unaware of any such decision, that RBI guidelines are draft and due from 1 July and do not mention open architecture, and that the company will respond to regulatory changes if they arise.

risks_watch: GST treatment on commissions: the full-year impact in FY27 and whether it is offset by product mix.
Persistency: the 61st-month drop linked to COVID-era ULIP sales, and the effect of assumption refinements on VNB.
Banca growth at around 9-11%: the agency and other channels must carry the 14% target.
Equity market volatility affecting ULIP demand and the 65% ULIP share of individual APE.
Regulatory: draft RBI guidelines effective 1 July, Ind AS transition from FY28 and RBC framework, plus any open architecture mandate for banks.
Deferred annuity launch timing (June 2026 target) and non-par repricing with yield volatility.

So we stuck to our range and we will continue to maintain that kind of margin in coming years also.
So our endeavor is to launch this deferred annuity product in this quarter itself.

rows.why: Deferred annuity (regular-pay) product targeted to go live by June 2026, otherwise next quarter, and a new non-par product was already launched in January 2026 to reflect current yields.

rows.why: RBI draft guidelines are due from 1 July; management says they do not mention open architecture, but banca is 60% of APE and any mandate would hit the core channel.

rows.why: Management sought forbearance and is assessing Ind AS and RBC impacts, so reported earnings metrics could shift from FY28 once adopted.

540719|2026-06.headline: SBI Life Q1 FY27 VNB rose 29% to INR14.1bn, but VNB margin fell to 26.2% as GST and a one-off GTI group deal diluted mix.
540719|2026-06.overview: Individual rated premium grew 14% to INR39.7bn with private market share of 22.2%, and all product segments and channels grew. Profit after tax rose 22% to INR7.2bn, helped by supportive market conditions, while the GST impact was INR2.3bn for the quarter. VNB margin of 26.2% was down year on year, which management attributed mainly to a higher share of lumpy group business (GTI) in APE. Management said the margin was within its 26–28% guidance, at the lower end, and expects it to move to the upper end as individual mix normalises.

financial_highlights.change: Margin down YoY; GST impact INR2.3bn

segments.name: Individual rated premium / APE
segments.commentary: Individual APE INR39.9bn, +14% YoY; ULIP INR24.5bn (61% share vs 65% in Q1 FY26); guaranteed non-par savings INR9.7bn, +27%. Non-ULIP share of IRP reached 38%.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group NBP INR32.9bn (37% of NBP), +41% YoY; group APE INR53.8bn, +36%; group protection APE INR12.3bn, +313%, driven by a large one-off GTI contract.

segments.name: Protection
segments.commentary: Individual protection APE INR1.9bn, +18%; pure protection +41% on individual APE; ROP share of individual protection 68% vs 73% a year ago.

segments.name: Bancassurance (SBI and RRBs)
segments.commentary: 47% of total APE; individual APE INR24.5bn, +10%; SBI branch productivity INR4.1mn, +7%. Other banks grew 19% on individual NBP and 31% on APE; their mix is about 80% non-ULIP.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Individual APE INR13.1bn, +20%; agent productivity INR2 lakh; non-ULIP share rose from 43% to 46%; 34,000+ agents added gross and 11 new branches opened.

segments.name: Other channels (direct, corporate agents, brokers, online)
segments.commentary: Grew 160% and contributed 28% of total APE; management did not split this into organic and group components.

guidance_outlook: IRP growth guidance of 14–15% for FY27 reaffirmed.
VNB margin guidance of 26–28% for FY27 maintained; management expects the margin to move toward the upper end as individual mix normalises.
GST drag expected for one more quarter (Q2 FY27), with the impact ending thereafter; GST was waived from 22 September, so about 2.5 months of impact remain in Q1.
Pure protection growth expected to keep outpacing ROP; the company is shifting focus from ROP to non-ROP and pure protection.
Regular-pay deferred annuity plan expected to launch within the next quarter.
Non-ULIP share of IRP targeted to be sustained at around this level for the year.
Other-expense ratio expected to normalise over the next three quarters, but higher stamp duty tied to sum assured growth will persist.
capex_capacity: Agency network: more than 100 branches opened over the last two to three years, and 11 new branches in Q1 FY27.
Agent additions: over 34,000 agents added on a gross basis in Q1 FY27.
New corporate agency tie-up with J&K Bank; business expected to start in the current quarter.
Automation: 99.9% of individual proposals submitted digitally; 67% processed through automated underwriting.
demand_pricing: Individual sum assured grew 46% YoY and group new business sum assured grew 265%; rider sum assured is 39% of individual sum assured.
Rider attachment on ULIP is about 45–50%, up from roughly 35% when introduced about 1–1.5 years ago; management expects it to hold or improve.
Non-par pricing is reviewed against yield movements; IRR for customers was raised in June after the yield curve moved.
The 61st-month persistency dip is attributed to the COVID cohort moving through policy years; management expects it to normalise by end-Q3 FY27.
Credit protect business was flat YoY; management expects an uptick in coming quarters.
Misselling ratio 0.02%; death claim settlement ratio 98.8%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 60 bps product-mix drag on VNB margin is due to the GTI group deal, and what is the normalised margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 60 bps mix drag relates only to GTI and that the company does not disclose product-wise margins. It said margin should return to normal as IRP share normalises. The 40 bps assumption-related item reflects the March 2026 annual review, and there was no assumption change in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GST drag going to persist, and how do expenses look?
qa_highlights.answer: GST drag of about 1.1 percentage points in Q1 is expected to continue into Q2 and then fade. Management said the rise in other expenses reflects one-off stamp duty tied to higher sum assured and labour code impacts, and it expects these to normalise over the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will agency growth be sustainable and will the channel mix shift affect costs or margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Agency APE grew 20% in Q1, with the current quarter at 19%-plus. Management expects a stronger contribution from agency in the remaining three quarters and a balanced mix of banca and agency going forward. It did not discuss cost impact in detail.

qa_highlights.question: What proportion of ULIPs carry rider attachment, and how is protection classified?
qa_highlights.answer: Rider attachment on ULIPs is about 45–50%, up from roughly 35% when riders were introduced 1–1.5 years earlier. Riders are counted within individual protection, and rider APE was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is individual protection growth lower than peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift from ROP to pure protection lowers ticket size, which makes headline growth look subdued. Individual protection grew 22% by its own measure against pure protection growth of 41%, with ROP share at 68%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the regular-pay deferred annuity plan launch slip, and what are the non-par and regulatory views?
qa_highlights.answer: The deferred annuity plan is expected in the next quarter and is being developed for an opportune time. On non-par, management said pricing is reviewed against yield movements. On regulation, management said it sees the company as well placed and expects future rules to be positive for the industry.

risks_watch: Group/GTI lumpiness: a large one-off group contract diluted Q1 VNB margin; sustainability of group APE mix and margin recovery to 26–28% range is the key test.
GST drag of about 110 bps on margin in Q1 FY27 with another quarter expected; watch whether Q2 drag falls as indicated.
Other-expense ratio rising (opex ratio 7.7% vs 6.3%) due to stamp duty and labour codes; watch cost discipline.
61st-month persistency dip due to COVID cohort; management expects normalisation by end-Q3 FY27.
Credit protect flat YoY; watch for the promised uptick.
Rider APE not disclosed; pure protection ticket size is smaller, so protection growth optics may stay weaker than peers.
Regulatory changes flagged as an open question by management; details not yet clear.

Management was evasive on quantifying the GTI margin drag and product-level margins, and declined to comment on individual contracts.

rows.why: Management only reaffirmed IRP growth of 14-15% and VNB margin of 26-28%; no raise was signalled, and Q1 IRP growth of 14% sits at the bottom of the range.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Individual APE grew 14% and ULIP share fell to 61% from 65%, and the 61st-month persistency dip plus opex ratio rising to 7.7% from 6.3% could pressure growth or margin if they persist.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management guided the regular-pay deferred annuity plan to launch within the next quarter, and the J&K Bank corporate agency tie-up starts in the current quarter.

rows.label: Group/GTI lumpiness drives APE mix
rows.why: Group APE rose 36% to INR53.8bn with group protection APE +313% from one large GTI contract, so the individual mix and margin recovery depend on whether group lumpiness fades.

rows.label: ULIP rider attachment rising
rows.why: Rider attachment on ULIPs is about 45-50%, up from roughly 35% 1-1.5 years ago, and management expects it to hold or improve, supporting protection mix.

rows.label: Opex ratio normalisation
rows.why: Opex ratio rose to 7.7% from 6.3% on one-off stamp duty and labour code effects; management expects normalisation over three quarters, though stamp duty tied to sum assured growth persists.

tone.note: Management was confident on IRP growth of 14-15% and the 26-28% VNB margin guide (toward upper end) but defensive on the margin decline, and evasive on quantifying the GTI drag; analysts pressed on margin normalisation and the drivers behind the lower protection growth.

540719|2026-09.headline: SBI Life H1 FY27 VoNB rose 19% to INR32.7bn at a 27.9% margin, while PAT grew 17% to INR12.7bn despite a INR5.3bn GST hit.
540719|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 showed solid value growth: VoNB up 19% to INR32.7bn with margin of 27.9% (Q2 at 29.3%), and embedded value up 15% to INR873.5bn. Individual rated new business premium grew 12% to INR97.2bn, but management said IRP growth of about 12% in H1 is below the 14-15% full-year target it reiterated. A one-off GST impact of INR5.3bn weighed on profit and opex ratio; excluding it, PAT was INR16.9bn (+39%) and VoNB INR33.8bn (+19.4%). Management said the mix shift toward non-par and annuity products helped margins, while the agency channel slowed in Q2 and the banca channel was softer in September.

financial_highlights.change: +12% YoY; private market share 22.6%, total market share 16%
vs 6.2% / 10.9% in H1 FY26; opex ratio ex-GST 5.8%

segments.name: Individual protection
segments.commentary: Individual protection APE INR4.3bn, +16%; pure protection +26%; including riders, protection APE +30%. Pure protection share moved from 90:10 to 58:42 versus ROP, and rider attachment is about 49%.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group new business premium INR65.3bn (+6%), 32% of NBP; group APE INR117.5bn (+18%); group protection APE INR16bn (+134%). Credit life APE about INR140 crore in H1, roughly flat.

segments.name: Bancassurance (SBI and RRB)
segments.commentary: Contributes 53% of total APE; individual APE INR59.9bn (+10%). SBI branch productivity INR5 million on individual APE for the period.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Individual APE INR32bn (+12%); non-ULIP share rose from 39% to 47%; agency individual sum assured +50%. Added over 72,000 agents gross; average productivity about INR2 lakh. Q2 growth slowed to about 6%.

segments.name: Other channels (direct, corporate agents, other banks, brokers, online)
segments.commentary: Grew 67% and contributed 19% of total APE. Growth driven by a low base and new partners; J&K Bank added as a banca partner. Other-bank channel growing 30%+, mainly non-par.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: ULIP share 62% of product mix versus 65% in H1 FY26. Guaranteed non-par savings INR24.7bn (+27%); annuity and pension NBP INR46.2bn; participating individual APE INR5.1bn (+9%).

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 IRP growth guided at 14-15%, reiterated despite H1 at about 12%; Q3 is seasonally stronger.
VoNB margin guidance of 26-28% maintained for the current half.
Management expects limited impact from IRDAI distribution-economics consultation paper and sees SBI Life as among the least impacted insurers; final guidelines awaited.
Plans to launch a regular-pay deferred annuity soon (possibly in Q3), with margin similar to or above company average.
Full-year ULIP share target of about 63%; H1 closed at about 62%.
IFRS 17 transition approach to be finalised by end-March 2027, with adoption from June 30, 2027; investor day planned before that.
capex_capacity: Branch expansion: 14 new branches opened in the period.
Agent network: over 72,000 agents added on a gross basis.
Digital: 99.9% of individual proposals submitted digitally; 71% processed through automated underwriting.
Hedging: 80% of premium hedged per policy; management views 80% as optimal.
demand_pricing: Non-par pricing repriced in Q2 with a pass-through of yield benefits to customers; management says it will keep repricing in Q3 and Q4.
Uniform commission and uniform product pricing across channels, so margins are the same across channels.
Management attributes about 70bps of H1 margin gain YoY to yield curve movement.
Individual sum assured +36% and group sum assured +78%; rider sum assured 40% of individual sum assured.
Persistency at 13th, 25th and 49th months: 87.6%, 78.4% and 69.3%, up 44, 110 and 40bps YoY.
Death claim settlement ratio 99.1%; misselling ratio 0.035%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company satisfied with about 12% IRP growth versus its 13-15% aspiration, and what is the reason for the negative operating-adjustment impact in the VoNB walk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 14-15% IRP growth for FY27 and said it is in line with industry growth. The VoNB negative came from a March 2026 assumption refinement (mortality, persistency, expenses), not a change made in the period; operating variances were all positive.

qa_highlights.question: How did banca trend in October and what is the outlook for non-par and annuity distribution across channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q3 is seasonally strong and expected to be higher growth. Products are available across all channels and uniformly priced; the uptick has been stronger in agency than banca, and banca sales of these products are being pushed.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins move higher than the 26-28% guidance, and how much of Q2 margin gain came from non-par?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stick to 26-28% guidance. It does not disclose the non-par margin contribution, but said the mix change helped Q2 margin and that repricing will continue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the IRDAI distribution paper, including credit life and bancassurance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SBI Life is among the least impacted; credit life attachment is under 50% of the bank portfolio and largely paid via loans. It has little partnership outside SBI, so no challenge is seen yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why did agency growth slow sharply in Q2 and what is the protection mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said agency growth will normalise within a couple of months and the FY27 target is intact. Pure protection moved to 58:42 versus ROP, and the sum assured growth is the highest in the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the conservation ratio fall to about 82% from 84%, mainly in linked pensions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is marginal and not a concern; 13th and 25th month persistency improved and renewal collections grew at high double digits.

risks_watch: IRP growth of about 12% in H1 versus the 14-15% full-year target; Q3 must deliver a sharp acceleration.
Final IRDAI distribution guidelines (commission caps, differential pricing), which could affect banca and credit life economics.
IFRS 17 transition approach and treatment of ULIP CSM release, still undisclosed.

Q2 agency slowdown and reliance on the Q3 banca season.

As far as the impact is concerned, you are aware that SBI Life is going to be one of the least impacted company because of this.
