540725|2026-03.headline: Share India standalone Q4 FY26 PAT rose 368% YoY to INR 75 crore on revenue of INR 383 crore (+103%).
540725|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue nearly doubled to INR 383 crore and PAT rose to INR 75 crore from INR 16 crore, with EPS of INR 17.6 versus INR 11.7. For FY26, standalone PAT rose 20% to INR 298 crore on revenue of INR 395 crore. Consolidated FY26 PAT was flat-to-down at INR 324 crore versus INR 328 crore, held back by fair value adjustments on investments held by group companies. Management pushed diversification into MTF, PMS, wealth distribution, debt (Share India Cred), AIF and commodities, while flagging RBI curbs on intraday bank limits for prop trading.

segments.name: Broking and trading (prop vs client)
segments.commentary: Prop contributed ~70% of revenue but ~49% of consolidated FY26 profit (~52% standalone). Client turnover reportedly exceeded prop turnover (53% vs 47%) for the first time; target 60% client share of turnover by year-end.

segments.name: MTF (margin trading finance)
segments.commentary: MTF book grew from INR 239 crore (FY25) to INR 424 crore (FY26); Dec-25 level was INR 457 crore. FY27 target INR 650 crore; FY28 vision also cited as INR 650 crore.

segments.name: NBFC
segments.commentary: Reported NIM of 17.64% for FY26, roughly flat with FY25; management said NIM will decline as the book shifts to secured lending.

segments.name: uTrade (algo platform)
segments.commentary: Active clients crossed 5,000 in FY26 (5,231 currently); still small in revenue, with focus on adoption. Multi-broker plan slowed by a SEBI circular requiring vendors to set up separately for each broker.

segments.name: Wealth management and PMS
segments.commentary: PMS launched in Q4 FY26 with AUM above INR 100 crore; FY27 target INR 200 crore. Third-party distribution team under Charu Sehgal to start operations in Q3. AIF CAT-3 application filed with SEBI, approval expected by end-Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Share India Cred (debt)
segments.commentary: Started operations in Q1 FY27 with six issues closed; FY27 target at least INR 500 crore of issues.

segments.name: Institutional business
segments.commentary: Institutional empanelments rose 35% from 137 to 186.

segments.name: Other subsidiaries
segments.commentary: NBFC, merchant banking, insurance and technology together contributed about 7% of FY26 bottom line. MSCI (Metropolitan Stock Exchange) cash segment doing INR 300-400 crore daily volume; Sizable stake held.

guidance_outlook: Annual EBITDA ~38% (+/-2%) and PAT margin ~22% (+/-2%) reaffirmed; management says no structural Q4 pressure.
MTF book target INR 650 crore by FY27, with mgmt saying INR 200 crore incremental is achievable if markets stay normal; deviation possible in low single digits on sentiment.
Target 30 new Tier-3 company-owned branches in next 2-3 years; 6 more targeted by FY27 year-end on top of 7 existing.
Prop share of profit targeted to fall to ~30% in three years; client share of turnover to reach 60% by FY27 year-end.
Share India Cred target INR 500 crore of issues in FY27; PMS AUM target INR 200 crore by FY27-end.
Silverleaf merger pending at NCLT; expected to conclude within about a quarter.
capex_capacity: Seven company-owned Tier-3 branches operating (Hyderabad, Indore, Bhopal, Varanasi, Agra, Raipur, Nagpur), with six more targeted by end FY27.
Target of at least INR 10-15 crore MTF per Tier-3 branch per year; 30 branches implied INR 300-500 crore.
AIF CAT-3 approval awaited from SEBI; wealth-management operations to start Q3 FY27.
Silverleaf merger pending at NCLT; post-merger plans include HFT trading.
MSCI exchange planning IPO segment, SME segment, and derivatives launch in FY27 (subject to approvals).
demand_pricing: Management said Q4 was volatile, with commodities (gold, silver, crude, natgas) driving turnover; cash ADTO rose to ~INR 2,000 crore in Q4 FY26 from ~INR 1,500 crore, and total ADTO rose to ~INR 4,500-5,000 crore from ~INR 1,400 crore in Q4 FY25 (figures as stated in call). Options were ~18% of Q4 ADTO.
MTF demand said to have risen in the last 1.5 months; Tier-3 pricing reportedly better because of less competition from sub-brokers.

RBI curbs: intraday bank limits for prop trading withdrawn; bank guarantees allowed for client business. Management estimates ~20% impact on overall deposits/limits used but minimal bottom-line effect; bank guarantees valid to 30 June can continue to expiry (up to March 2027).
SEBI market-making framework expected in 3-4 months; company is lobbying RBI for liquidity-provider relief.
Mgmt estimates INR 40,000-50,000 crore of capital to exit the market due to RBI curbs, which it expects to widen per-trade margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why do margins dip every March quarter and is that sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said Q4 was weak in FY25 and FY26 due to volatile markets; management prefers annual view with EBITDA ~38% and PAT ~22% (+/-2%). Sachin Gupta said Q4 pressure is not structural.

qa_highlights.question: Status of uTrade multi-broker plans and monetisation model?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said talks with Motilal Oswal and Dhan stalled after a SEBI circular requiring third-party vendors to set up infrastructure separately per broker, which is costly. No monetisation details were given.

qa_highlights.question: At what MTF AUM does the interest spread become meaningful, given borrowing costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said full-year borrowing costs will flow into FY27 and new NCD and third-party borrowing lines could cut costs by a few hundred basis points. Tier-3 direct branches are meant to remove mediators and lift NIM.

qa_highlights.question: Break up of brokerage vs prop income?
qa_highlights.answer: Prop contributes ~70% of revenue but ~49% of FY26 consolidated profit (52% standalone). Client turnover exceeded prop turnover for the first time (53% vs 47%).

qa_highlights.question: Impact of RBI regulation on prop business and Market Maker regime?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated ~20% impact on limits used and minimal impact on bottom line. Company sought liquidity-provider status; the company is hybrid-classified and can continue bank guarantees until expiry (up to March 2027).

qa_highlights.question: Ballpark revenue diversification in the next three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for 70% client and 30% prop share of profit over three years. Non-broking segments were ~7% of FY26 bottom line; detailed split not disclosed.

risks_watch: RBI curbs on prop intraday limits effective around 1 July 2026; watch for actual impact on prop turnover and margins versus the ~20% management estimate.
Consolidated PAT flat YoY due to fair value losses on group investments; recurrence risk.
NIM compression expected in NBFC as lending shifts to secured products; MTF book is cyclical with market sentiment.
Regulatory changes: SEBI vendor-per-broker circular hurts uTrade multi-broker plans; market-making framework still pending.
Silverleaf NCLT approval and AIF CAT-3 approval timing are uncertain.
540725|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and diversification, but defensive and hedged on the RBI prop curbs and market-dependent targets. Management repeatedly stressed that targets depend on normal markets and geopolitical stability.
key_quotes: So, the Company should be able to continue with the current margins. There is nothing like Q4 type of pressure on us.

So, hardly 20% impact in the overall limits will be there from the prop side, but on the bottom-line side, I don't think there will be much impact or there will be any impact, because per trade margin will improve.
So, MTF definitely depends on the market performance, and whatever the external reasons are, if market is performing good, demand for MTF goes up.

540725|2026-06.headline: Share India Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 48% YoY to Rs 124.41 crore on revenue of Rs 448 crore; management targets ~20% growth this year.
540725|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the company's strongest quarterly performance to date despite SEBI derivatives curbs and RBI funding restrictions on prop desks. Standalone revenue rose 28% YoY to Rs 349 crore and PAT rose 32% to Rs 90.85 crore; consolidated revenue rose 31% to Rs 448 crore and PAT rose 48% to Rs 124.41 crore, with consolidated PAT up 114% QoQ. Growth was attributed to MTF lending income, new subsidiaries (Share India Cred, GIFT City), PMS launch and merchant banking. Management plans CP and NCD issuance to offset funding constraints.

financial_highlights.value: Rs ~74 crore across six issues; EBITDA Rs 1.08 crore; PAT Rs 40 lakh

segments.name: Broking and trading (prop vs client)
segments.commentary: Management said prop contributes ~52% of profitability and ~48% from broking; on revenue, prop is ~58-60%. Client volume is ~60% versus prop ~40%.

segments.name: MTF lending
segments.commentary: MTF book ~Rs 470 crore at end Q1, targeted at Rs 1,000 crore in two years; management called MTF the main source of sustainable interest income.

segments.name: PMS / wealth
segments.commentary: PMS AUM Rs 150 crore at end Q1 (launched in Q1); target ~Rs 250 crore by year-end. Wealth distribution team hiring, operations targeted from Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Share India Cred (debt trading)
segments.commentary: Started operations in Q1 FY27 under Keshav Goyal; ~Rs 74 crore underwritten/sold across six issues, PAT Rs 40 lakh.

segments.name: GIFT City / IFSC
segments.commentary: Turned positive in Q1 with ~Rs 2 crore of income per management, after prior losses.

segments.name: Institutional and merchant banking
segments.commentary: Active institutional clients 212 versus 186 at Q4 (+15%). Merchant banking completed a main-board IPO raising Rs 167 crore (subscription above 12x) and one SME IPO of ~Rs 200 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management expects ~20% growth in the current financial year, subject to market conditions.
Target of 25-30 new Tier-3 branches over 24 months; seven opened recently (six in Banaras, Indore, Bhopal, Raipur, Agra, Nagpur plus Hyderabad cluster).
Branch economics: each branch targets Rs 15 crore MTF book within ~8 months to break even; branches not profitable after 12 months to be shut.
AIF launch expected in Q3 FY27 pending regulatory approval; wealth distribution operations also targeted from Q3 FY27.
PMS AUM target ~Rs 250 crore by financial year end.
Plans to issue commercial paper (rated Crisil A1+) and NCDs to diversify funding; CP programme initiated.
capex_capacity: Seven new branches opened recently against a 30-branch target over two years; branches rolled out in tranches of about eight.

Acquisition of Enshrine (property-holding company, up to Rs 45 crore consideration) to secure ~18,000 sq ft carpet-area office in Mumbai (Interface 11 area); management cited property value above Rs 42 crore.
Silverleaf (HFT technology firm) acquisition previously announced; expected to add technology stack and HFT protocols and support geographic expansion.
AI, automation and in-house platform Techyon cited as technology investments.
demand_pricing: Management said realisations improved during the quarter and commodity business showed improvement.
Industry headwinds cited: SEBI F&O regulatory tightening and RBI curbs on prop-desk top-desk funding; management said smaller brokers face difficulty meeting higher capital requirements.
Retail MTF demand in Tier-3 cities described as underserved, with limited broker options for MTF.
Mid and small-cap volatility affected MTF book; management said it held its numbers with mild growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the payback period for Tier-3 branches given lower ticket sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said each branch should reach break-even in ~8 months by building a Rs 15 crore MTF book; branches not profitable after 12 months will be closed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the stock underperforming despite low PE and high growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on share price, attributing it to industry regulatory consolidation and cited diversification, institutional clients and subsidiaries as positives.

qa_highlights.question: What is the purpose of acquiring Silverleaf, the tech company?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said Silverleaf (founded by IIT Bombay graduates, 12+ years in business) brings a technology stack and HFT protocols, supporting third-country expansion and back-end technology.

qa_highlights.question: What drove broking and trading performance and what is the prop vs broking split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business has shifted toward lending via MTF (~Rs 465-470 crore) and fee streams from PMS, MF distribution and third-party products; prop contributes ~52% of profit and broking ~48%.

qa_highlights.question: Why pay up to Rs 45 crore for Enshrine, a company with Rs 2-3 crore turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: Kamlesh Shah said the acquisition is mainly to obtain a Mumbai property (~18,000 sq ft carpet area, valued above Rs 42 crore) to consolidate Mumbai offices.

qa_highlights.question: Is prop still a very high share of total revenue and PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said prop was ~58-60% of revenue and ~52% of profit now, versus ~85-90% of revenue and ~70-75% of profit 8-9 years ago.

risks_watch: Prop trading still ~52% of profit and ~58-60% of revenue, exposed to SEBI derivatives rules and RBI prop-desk funding curbs.
Funding transition: CP and NCD programmes not yet issued; funding costs and timing are open.
Regulatory approval pending for AIF launch (targeted Q3 FY27).
Stock underperformance despite strong earnings; management attributed this to sector consolidation and external factors.
Q1 benefited from merchant-banking IPOs and valuation gains; sustainability of these flows is not assured.
Branch expansion carries execution risk; management set a hard stop at 12 months for loss-making branches.
Enshrine acquisition value (up to Rs 45 crore) and Silverleaf integration: limited disclosure on rationale and financials.

key_quotes: Despite this industry -wide headwinds, I am pleased to share that Share India has delivered its strongest quarterly financial performance to date.
Subject to overall market condition, we remain confident of delivering around 20% growth during the current financial year.
So, our goal is 8 months branch should be at par within 8 months.

rows.why: Share India Cred underwrote/sold about Rs 74 crore across six issues in its first quarter (PAT Rs 40 lakh), and management plans CP and NCD issuance under a Crisil A1+ rated CP programme to offset funding constraints.

540735|2026-03.headline: IRIS RegTech targets INR500 crore revenue, needing ~30%+ growth over 4-5 years; FY26 revenue grew ~23% with EBITDA margin ~14%.
540735|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as steady: total revenue grew about 23% and EBITDA margin was about 14%, with management asking analysts to judge the business on annual rather than quarterly numbers. IRIS CARBON ARR grew 33% on disclosure-management wins and iDEAL ARR grew 17%, while SupTech added 3 new logos including the Government of Qatar. Post the TaxTech divestment, cash was about INR155 crore and net worth rose to INR200 crore from INR76 crore. Management reiterated the INR500 crore revenue aspiration and said the Middle East crisis is a watch item rather than a current drag.

Delayed Indian customer decisions in H1 FY26

Sales and marketing spend is planned to be stepped up in a measured way, at about 1.1-1.2x net ARR, and kept EBITDA positive.

segments.commentary: ARR grew 17% despite slower Indian purchase decisions in H1 FY26. Company is exploring Africa and Middle East, with some Europe interest; revenue mix is subscription, implementation and licence.

segments.name: SupTech - iFile
segments.commentary: Added 3 new logos in FY26, including Government of Qatar for tax reporting, plus a deposit insurance management segment. Product suite is being extended to licensing, risk-based supervision, case management and decision management. Revenue is lumpier and expected to grow slower than SaaS; management expects 3-4 SupTech wins in a typical year.

segments.commentary: Spun off into a subsidiary for sharper focus. Loan facilitation piloted from February 2026 with 3 lenders onboarded so far; monetisation is at an early stage and management's internal target is earlier than the 2-year horizon an analyst suggested.

qa_highlights.answer: Management sees AI as both opportunity and threat; it is building AI offerings and embedding AI in the development process. No competitive intensity increase seen so far from enterprises building in-house or AI-native entrants.

qa_highlights.answer: SaaS impact seen as minimal given Europe and US focus. SupTech pipeline linked to Middle East regulators could see delays if the crisis persists beyond roughly June; 3-4 SupTech wins still expected.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~30% growth be achieved: markets, products, headcount?
qa_highlights.answer: CARBON is the flagship with ESG added; adjacencies in capital-markets and energy reporting are early. iDEAL to expand into Africa, Middle East and Europe. iFile adding licensing, risk-based analytics and case management. Developed-market sales hiring has started.

540743|2026-03.headline: Godrej Agrovet Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR2,333 crore; FY27 guidance is early double-digit revenue and mid-teens PBT growth.
540743|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 9% YoY to INR2,333 crore and PBT before exceptional items rose 16.8% to INR87 crore, driven by volume growth and better mix. For FY26, revenue crossed INR10,000 crore at INR10,233 crore (+9%) and PBT before exceptionals rose 17.2% to INR569 crore. Animal Nutrition volumes grew 15% in Q4, Astec reached EBITDA break-even for the year, and Crop Care was hit by co-marketing channel inventory carry-forward. Management guided to early double-digit consolidated revenue growth and mid-teens PBT growth for FY27, with the Iran war and a weak monsoon forecast flagged as variables.

segments.name: Animal Nutrition
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes +15% YoY, well ahead of industry; cattle feed +24%. Margins expanded, helped by new Type 1 products, East and Central share gains, raw material cost reconfiguration, and a ~INR9.5 crore pet food manufacturing income booked in other income.

segments.name: Oil palm
segments.commentary: FY26 marked by record area expansion, strong volume growth and an all-time high oil extraction ratio. Q4 is seasonally weak (~60,000 t of FFB out of 6.37 lakh t annually) but margins held. Specialty fat refinery to start rolling out in May 2026.

segments.name: Crop Care
segments.commentary: Q4 hit by carry-forward of co-marketing channel inventory, lowering in-house volumes; partly offset by specialty products. FY27 is guided as a recovery year, with recovery from Q2 and very high double-digit growth in top and bottom line.

segments.name: Astec LifeSciences
segments.commentary: Achieved EBITDA break-even in FY26; Q4 revenue and EBITDA grew strongly on CDMO volumes, realisations and utilisation. FY26 mix was ~48% enterprise and ~52% CDMO; exports ~53% of revenue. Board reconstituted with Arijit Mukherjee as Executive Director.

segments.name: Creamline Dairy (CDPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~5% YoY ex bulk sales in Q4; profitability pressured by elevated milk procurement costs. Management expects milk prices to ease gradually from Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Godrej Foods
segments.commentary: EBITDA margins improved significantly in Q4 on Live Bird and Yummiez; branded revenue salience above 80% in FY26. Live Bird trading is being phased out; momos and frozen chicken entries planned.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth targeted at early double-digit, volume-led.
FY27 consolidated PBT growth targeted at mid-teens (described as mid-strong double-digit, mid-teens).
Animal Nutrition: double-digit volume-led revenue growth targeted in FY27.
Crop Care: FY27 a recovery year, with very high double-digit top and bottom line growth expected; full recovery from Q2.
Astec: top-line growth around 15% targeted, CDMO growing faster; CDMO salience guided to 52-53%+, with ~20% growth aspiration mentioned.
FY27 capex around INR350-400 crore (about 75-80% growth capex, ~50% to oil palm); post-capex cash surplus around INR100-125 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and PBT outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated early double-digit revenue growth, volume-led, and mid-strong double-digit (mid-teens) PBT growth; the Iran war is the main overhang.

qa_highlights.question: How does a below-normal monsoon (IMD/Skymet El Nino forecasts) affect the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guidance stands for now; the severe impact is expected in August-September, and Crop Care's skew to South and West may be less affected. Oil palm is not expected to see an impact this year, with possible effects next year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Astec's raw material comes from China, and how is currency managed?
qa_highlights.answer: About 47% of total imports came from China last year. Being a net exporter, the currency impact is described as roughly neutral, with a possible mild positive.

qa_highlights.question: What is behind the Animal Nutrition volume acceleration and margin sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers are East and Central share gains, Type 1 higher-yield products, and raw material reconfiguration. The Rs9.5 crore pet food income sits in other income as a contract manufacturing profit, with no revenue recognised.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Astec structure or chemicals business change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to comment on structure; a decision is expected over the next two to three quarters. Arijit Mukherjee was elevated to Executive Director and COO-led growth continues.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing contributed about 30% of last year's profit jump; the specialty fat refinery and a 50-55% value-added target by FY31 are meant to cushion volatility.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the payout has been around 48% and is decided with promoters as results come in; no commitment was made.

540743|2026-06.headline: Godrej Agrovet Q1 FY27 consolidated sales rose 10% to INR2,852 crore; Crop Care fell 16.2% on delayed monsoon, while management still targets double-digit FY27 PBT growth.
540743|2026-06.overview: Consolidated sales grew 10% YoY to INR2,852 crore despite a delayed monsoon and geopolitical-driven inflation. Animal Nutrition (revenue +12.6%, reported segment result +29%) and Oil Palm (revenue +28.9%, segment result +14.4%) carried the quarter. Crop Care revenue fell 16.2% on a dry June and slower kharif sowing, and Dairy margins were squeezed by milk procurement costs and packaging inflation. Astec reached EBITDA breakeven versus an INR11 crore loss a year ago. Management reiterated FY27 double-digit consolidated PBT growth (versus earlier mid-teens guidance) but deferred a firmer view on Crop Care until end-September.

financial_highlights.change: Cattle feed volume +15%; total segment volume +7%
Segment result +14.4%; EBIT margin ~17% vs 19% a year ago (per analyst)
vs EBITDA loss of INR11 crore in Q1 FY26
Value-added share of sales 49% vs 42% a year ago

segments.name: Animal Nutrition
segments.commentary: Revenue +12.6% on robust demand and better realisations; cattle feed volume +15% and overall segment volume +7%. Poultry volumes deliberately reduced in unprofitable geographies. Cattle feed is about 55-56% of the segment; fish feed about 7%.

segments.name: Oil Palm
segments.commentary: Revenue +28.9% on higher CPO and PKO realisations and volume; FFB volumes broadly flat versus a strong early-monsoon base. Segment result +14.4%, with margin down on a pricing-formula effect that management calls one-off.

segments.name: Crop Care
segments.commentary: Revenue -16.2% as a dry June and slow kharif sowing hit cotton herbicide volumes, with margin contraction. Ashitaka and Takai together contribute about 18-20% of Q1 sales; Ghassnash soybean herbicide launched.

segments.name: Astec LifeSciences
segments.commentary: EBITDA breakeven versus an INR11 crore loss a year ago; revenue moderately lower on product mix. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of more than 20%, with an 8-9% Q1 dip to be recovered; CDMO dissilience around 50-52%.

segments.name: Dairy (CDPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue +11.4% and volume +8%, but profitability hit by elevated milk procurement prices and packaging inflation. Route-to-market reconstitution (about 18-20 months) under new CEO Gaurav is starting.

segments.name: Godrej Foods
segments.commentary: Revenue broadly stable as live bird trading is planned to fall 15-20% a year and go near zero over 3-4 years. Branded B2C (Yummiez, Real Good) volume +28% and about 32% of the Foods business; profitability hit by input costs.

segments.name: Bangladesh JV (ACI Godrej Agrovet)
segments.commentary: Returned to growth, with double-digit growth in volume, revenue and PBT.

qa_highlights.question: What FFB volume growth and EBITDA trajectory can Oil Palm deliver over 3-5 years, and what capex and returns are involved in value addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Kataria guided FFB volume growth of high single digit to early double digit over 4-5 years, targeting double digit; specialty fats refinery to start in September, with a 16-18% IRR hurdle and about 200 bps EBITDA uplift at scale. He did not give an explicit EBITDA number.

qa_highlights.question: Can Crop Care recover in H2, and is the consolidated mid-teens PBT growth still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was hit by a 40% June deficit; July is better than last year's base, and it will decide on the recovery by end-September. Consolidated growth now targeted at double digit, with the exact level to be given by end-Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Astec: revenue outlook and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Arijit Mukherjee said FY27 revenue growth is now expected at more than 20%, with the 8-9% Q1 dip to be recovered; CDMO margins intact and enterprise margin normalising as prices fall.

qa_highlights.question: Will the palm oil shift need extra capex, and what is the Foods/Dairy pricing picture?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex stays within the INR300-350 crore envelope already guided. Dairy volume grew 8% but packaging and milk costs hit margin; Foods B2C is in a 3-4 year investment phase, with live bird trading being wound down.

qa_highlights.question: How much maize inflation has Animal Nutrition passed through, and what is EBIT per tonne?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60-70% of commodity cost increases passed on; EBIT per tonne guidance held at roughly INR2,050-2,150, with Q1 EBITDA per tonne in that range or slightly higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Oil Palm segment margin fall from 19% to 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to a one-off pricing-formula change in the quarter and flat FFB, offset by better OER; expects margins to even out over the year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Crop Care lagging peers, and what are margins on the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is segment-mix and macro driven (cotton herbicide concentration), not share loss; new products carry lower margin than Hitweed but healthy, with total Crop Care EBIT margin seen at about 26-27%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated PBT growth: management still targets double-digit growth, narrowed from the earlier mid-teens guidance; exact position in the range to be given by end-September (end Q2).

Astec LifeSciences: FY27 revenue growth guided at more than 20% (up from the ~20% earlier guidance); Q1 revenue dip of 8-9% to be recovered in later quarters; CDMO dissilience around 50-52% for the year, with some CDMO shift from H1 to H2.
Astec enterprise margin: Q1 benefited from low-priced raw material and war-driven finished goods price increases; prices now easing, margin normalising. CDMO margins intact.

Oil Palm: FFB volume growth of high single digit to early double digit over the next 4-5 years (LRP); management says it targets double digit; full-year FFB growth guided at high single digit to double digit; margin drop expected to even out over the year.
Animal Nutrition: EBIT per tonne guidance held at roughly INR2,050-2,150 per tonne.
Crop Care: no firm FY27 numbers; recovery quantum to be assessed by end-September after cotton herbicide season. Crop Care EBIT margin expected to hold around 26-27% despite tough year.

Dairy: milk procurement prices expected to stay at current elevated levels for 2-3 quarters; packaging inflation expected to ease by August; some impact may persist in Q2; cost initiatives to be doubled down on in H2.
Godrej Foods: live bird trading to decline 15-20% a year and go near zero over 3-4 years; branded B2C to be in investment phase for 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Overall business-level capex guidance of roughly INR300-350 crore, phased over 3-4 quarters; includes the integrated palm oil complex (phase 1 started, nursery and CPO mill; seed garden in 18-24 months; refinery later) and specialty fats refinery (rollout late August/early September 2026); management says no new investment beyond this envelope.

Oil Palm area expansion: added about 17,000 hectares last year and on track to repeat this year; LRP target to take area from about 80,000 ha to about 150,000 ha, with Telangana and Northeast expansion; about 50% of plantations are juvenile (0-4 years).

540749|2026-03.headline: MAS Financial Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 25% YoY to INR104 crore, with AUM at INR15,304 crore, up 19%.
540749|2026-03.overview: Consolidated PAT for Q4 FY26 was INR104 crore versus INR83 crore a year earlier, and full-year PAT was INR379 crore, up 21%. Standalone AUM grew 18.71% and standalone PAT grew 23.39% YoY in the quarter to around INR100 crore. Standalone net Stage 3 was 1.70%, slightly better than 1.72% in December 2025, while gross Stage 3 edged up to 2.57% from 2.56%. Cost of borrowing fell 42 bps YoY to 9.39%, and management guided to 9.20-9.25% over the next two to three quarters. Credit cost was elevated because of deliberate aggressive write-offs of 90+ DPD assets, which management said were funded from profit.

segments.commentary: AUM rose about 20% to INR5,737 crore from INR4,793 crore.

segments.commentary: AUM grew 35.43% to INR1,063 crore from INR785 crore; yields cited at 19-23%.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: AUM grew 11% to INR1,085 crore from INR979 crore; growth being deliberately slowed for 1-2 quarters.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Salaried personal loan
segments.commentary: AUM grew around 22% to INR1,264 crore from INR1,040 crore.

segments.name: Housing finance subsidiary
segments.commentary: AUM rose 22.41% to INR940 crore from INR768 crore; Q4 PAT INR3.70 crore vs INR2.64 crore, net Stage 3 0.68%. Management aims for INR1,000 crore, now about a quarter later than planned.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 20-25% on a sustained basis; long-term target of INR1 lakh crore AUM by 2036.

Branch additions of 30-35 planned in FY27 after a year of consolidating existing branches.
Dividend: final dividend INR0.75 per share, total INR2 per share for FY26, about 10% payout.
Capital adequacy to be maintained at around 20%; debt tie-up for about half of FY27 done, full-year tie-up expected soon.
capex_capacity: More than 200 branches and about 16,500 centres; branch network to grow by 30-35 in FY27.
Average cash and cash equivalent balance of about INR1,000 crore plus unutilised cash credit of over INR200 crore.
Cash credit facility of about INR1,500 crore across 14 banks, utilised at 70-75%.
Sanctioned facilities over INR2,000 crore as of 31 March (term loans, NCDs, direct assignment, co-lending).
Term loan sanctioned pipeline of about INR1,300 crore; INR750 crore term loan raised in Q4 at 3-5 year tenor; INR100 crore NCDs raised in Q4.
Direct assignment of INR940 crore executed in Q4; a further INR500 crore+ of direct assignment and co-lending sanctions to be used in the current quarter.
demand_pricing: Direct sourcing is about 64% of the book; fintech partnerships are about 10% of business.
Yield rose about 40 bps sequentially, attributed to fintech mix and 2-wheeler growth; SME yields were also higher.
Management said assignment income is amortised, not upfront, and the NII rise was mainly from lower borrowing cost and the MCLR reset.
Standalone 90+ write-offs were aggressive in FY26 (more than 0.10% of assets), mostly unsecured per management.
Caution list added petrol pumps, gas agencies, transporters and some chemical industries in Feb-March 2026, alongside textile and agro, due to West Asia supply concerns.
Management reported no slowdown in disbursement growth as of the call.

qa_highlights.question: How is MAS using data and AI for risk-adjusted growth, and what early warning systems exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it back-tests risk models on its own repayment experience, not generic bureau scores; it moved from LOS to business rule engines and plans AI-based risk management after 6-9 months. Field checks included more than 2,000-3,000 commercial vehicle borrowers after the Middle East crisis, plus bounce data from 100% bank or e-NACH collections.

qa_highlights.question: Will the West Asia crisis and inflation affect lending and asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset quality should hold but is being watched closely; it is growing CV more slowly as an energy- and logistics-linked precaution. Disbursement growth has not slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for cost of borrowing and the Q4 cost of borrowing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of borrowing is 9.39% and is expected to fall to 9.20-9.25% over 2-3 quarters. Q4 interest expense was about INR222 crore vs INR219 crore in Q3, with the MCLR reset adding to NII.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the origination and fee cost high, and what is driving opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the fees and commission depend on product structure. Fintech partners get the spread as commission, and yields rose about 0.5%. Opex is judged against ROA, not in isolation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise and what is the normalised level?
qa_highlights.answer: The rise was from deliberate write-offs of 90+ DPD assets, not stress. Normal credit cost is 1-1.25% of closing AUM; 1.5% is possible in quarters with aggressive write-offs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is CV growth slow, and what is the write-off and recovery policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is slowing CV growth for 1-2 quarters due to logistics and transport risk. Write-offs occur after 360 days across all products; recoveries are credited to P&L net.

risks_watch: Rising inflation and energy costs from the West Asia crisis could hit logistics, transport and fuel-linked MSMEs.
Credit cost is a function of aggressive write-off policy; quarterly credit costs could run towards 1.5%.

Gross Stage 3 is at 2.57%, up slightly QoQ.

540749|2026-06.headline: MAS Financial Q1 FY27: consolidated AUM up 21% to INR16,100 crores and PAT up 27% to INR110 crores; credit cost guided 1.25%-1.75%.
540749|2026-06.overview: Consolidated AUM grew about 21% YoY to INR16,100 crores and PAT rose about 27% to INR110 crores, with standalone PAT up 25% to INR105 crores. Asset quality was stable, with standalone GNPA at 2.58% and NNPA at 1.70%, flat QoQ, and a management overlay of INR17.60 crores held. Borrowing cost fell 55 bps YoY to 9.25%, while credit cost rose to about 1.6% of AUM, which management attributed to higher on-book mix, a 5 bps rise in Stage 1/2 provisioning and prudent write-offs. Management reiterated 20-25% AUM growth guidance, with the call leaning toward the upper end for FY27.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance maintained at 20-25%, with management saying the full year is very likely to be at the higher end of the range.
Credit cost to stay in a 1.25%-1.75% range, depending on product mix; management pointed to commercial vehicles as high-yield, high-loss.
ROA target of 2.75%-3.25%, with an aspiration of 3%+.
Net interest margin target of 8%-8.5% on a 7%-7.5% spread; incremental borrowing cost 9.2%-9.25%, expected to stay stable (9.2%-9.3% per Q&A).
Direct distribution share (currently 66%-67%) expected to reach 70%-72% in 1-1.5 years; off-book target kept at 20-25% of AUM.
Used CV growth expected to pick up only after 1-2 quarters; housing finance AUM expected to inch up in the next few quarters.
Credit rating upgrade being pursued, timing not given; sub-9% borrowing cost called far-fetched in the next 1-2 quarters.
capex_capacity: Distribution of 16,500 centres through 209 branches, with more than 200 NBFC partners providing about 33% of originations; direct share 67%.
Employee count reduced by 380 in Q1 due to technology adoption; no quantified headcount target given.
In-house tech team of close to 100 people; LOS live for all products, with BRE added and straight-through processing improving.
Branches opened after March 2024 expected to mature (sweat) by 2027-28 or earlier.
demand_pricing: Standalone MSME/SME demand stable across manufacturing and trading; eligible demand fell in Q1 due to tighter credit screens on energy-dependent sectors (restaurants, gas-dependent manufacturing, export businesses).
Used CV demand robust, but eligible demand lower because of fuel-cost tightening.
Two-wheeler Q1 degrowth QoQ attributed to seasonality; monsoon and Gujarat floods flagged as temporary and not expected to cause major stress.
Working capital demand rising for some businesses on higher input costs; underwriting parameters also tightened.
Write-offs were INR29 crores in March and INR19 crores in June, offset by higher ECL provisioning, keeping impairment cost flat QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise from about 1.2-1.3% to about 1.6% of AUM despite the microfinance impact and Q4 write-offs last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher on-book assets (on-book up 8.25% QoQ vs AUM up 5.5%), which added INR6-7 crores of Stage 1/2 provisioning from a 5 bps rise to 0.7%. Prudent write-offs and mix shift toward higher-yield commercial vehicles also contributed; ROA not affected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20-25% growth guidance at risk given the West Asia conflict and energy-linked stress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said energy-dependent segments were tightened early and stress was limited; eligible demand fell in Q1 and Q2 but normalised, and guidance is expected to hold with the upper end targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Will borrowing cost fall further from 9.25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to predict and depends on RBI and liquidity; the target is to stabilise at 9.2%-9.3%, with a credit rating upgrade being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the Stage 1/2 provisioning increase and whether there are macro-related buffers?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 1/2 provisioning rose to 0.7% from 0.65%, adding INR6-7 crores; management described it as a buffer.

qa_highlights.question: What was the nature of the INR10 crore OCPS redemption in the subsidiary MRHMFL?
qa_highlights.answer: The OCPS was refunded to the parent because the housing subsidiary's CRAR exceeded 37% and it did not need the capital.

qa_highlights.question: Why did off-book share fall and what is the housing finance growth plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Off-book is dynamic and chosen by price; target stays at 20-25%. Housing finance plans to expand into Tamil Nadu and Karnataka from Q1, with results expected in Q3-Q4.

risks_watch: Used CV: eligible demand softer on fuel-cost-driven credit tightening; management says growth push is 1-2 quarters away, and CV is high-yield, high-loss, so credit cost direction depends on mix.

Credit cost: rose to about 1.6% of AUM from about 1.2-1.3% a year earlier; management guides a 1.25%-1.75% range and Stage 1/2 provisioning went to 0.7% from 0.65% (INR6-7 crores), which management calls a buffer.
Energy-linked and West Asia stress: eligible demand fell in Q1 and Q2 and management says it has normalised; the next quarter will show whether this holds.
Borrowing cost: 9.25% average with incremental cost at 9.2%-9.3%; a sub-9% level is called far-fetched in the next 1-2 quarters, and the credit rating upgrade has no timing.

Off-book share fell below the 20%-25% target this quarter; management says it is opportunistic and the target is unchanged. Gujarat floods and monsoon effects on two-wheeler and collections are still unquantified.
key_quotes: So, very high possibility, yes. We are working on that quite optimistic. Can't predict, but you are thinking on the right lines.
So, that is the impact which translates to roughly around between INR5 crores to INR7 crores in provisioning.
Difficult to comment right now because the cost of borrowing is dependent on the macro situation.
So, currently, sub-9 immediately within next 1 or 2 quarters looks like a far -fetched assumption.

540749|2026-09.headline: MAS Financial Q2 FY27 consolidated AUM rose 23.3% to INR 17,042 crores; PAT grew about 26% to INR 115 crores.

540750|2026-03.headline: IEX Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 10.8% YoY to INR 129.8 crore on record 39.4 billion units traded volume.
540750|2026-03.overview: IEX delivered record quarterly electricity volume of 39.4 billion units (up 24.3% YoY) and consolidated revenue of INR 196.4 crore (up 12.5%), with PAT up 10.8% to INR 129.8 crore. Full-year PAT rose 14.9% to INR 492.9 crore and a final dividend of INR 2 per share was declared. Exchange prices fell sharply on higher sell-side liquidity (DAM down 12.2% YoY in Q4), and other income dropped about 29% sequentially-adjusted per analyst, attributed to treasury mark-to-market losses in March. Market coupling (CERC draft of April 17, 2026 naming Grid India as MCO, comments till May 16) is the dominant overhang, with management disputing its benefit. Gas exchange (IGX) volumes fell 8% in Q4 on Middle East supply disruption and management expects no growth in Q1 FY27.

540750|2026-06.headline: IEX Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose about 12% to Rs 134.8 crore on Rs 202.8 crore revenue, with electricity volume up 16% to 37.5 billion units.
540750|2026-06.overview: IEX reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of Rs 202.8 crore and PAT of Rs 134.8 crore, up about 12% YoY, on electricity volume of 37.5 billion units (+16%). Real-Time Market growth was the main driver, with RTM up about 25% in Q1 and its share of mix reaching about 34% last year. Management used the analyst meet to push a set of new products (Green RTM, peak contracts, 11-month TAM, carbon trading, coal exchange) while pushing back on CERC's proposed market coupling and the Day-Ahead Market pilot, which it has challenged at APTEL and the Supreme Court. The call was mostly a policy and product narrative; no formal FY27 guidance was given.

segments.commentary: RTM is now roughly the size of DAM; DAM share of mix fell from 95% in FY16 to about 39%, RTM rose to about 34% in FY26, and RTM is up about 25% in Q1 FY27. Term-Ahead Market and Green Market are about 7-8% of the mix.

segments.name: IGX (gas exchange, associate)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 42 crore; Q1 FY27 volume 27.5 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 16 crore. DRHP filed for IPO of a 22.3% stake to bring IEX's 47.3% holding down to 25% under PNGRB rules, after a one-year extension.

segments.name: ICX (I-REC / environmental)
segments.commentary: Sole I-REC issuer in India; management cited about 200% growth in I-REC volumes last year. Q1 REC volumes were down sharply YoY, which management attributed to the first quarter and possible RPO buy-out confusion.

segments.name: Indian Coal Exchange (new)
segments.commentary: Incorporated as a separate company in June 2026; coal rules notified 4 June 2026 require e-auction and marketplace trades to move to exchanges within six months of launch. Market size cited at about 120 million tonnes today, with a target of at least 100 million tonnes in year one.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 volume or revenue guidance given; management expects RTM volumes to grow about 25-30% a year.
Management expects carbon credit trading to begin in FY27, with BEE targeting 1 October 2026.

Management sees the exchange-routed share of electricity rising to about 25% over five to six years, against about 14-15% short-term market today.
Management said it would consider a buyback in future, citing SEBI's revised market-buyback rules.
Management said the coal exchange's fee should exceed those of MSTC and M-Junction, since exchanges perform price discovery, clearing and settlement.
capex_capacity: Management cited about 80 GW of thermal capacity in the pipeline, 41 GW under construction with PPAs signed, 20 GW awarded, and 16 GW in planning; most is expected in FY31-FY33.
Management said it has built a hot standby for RTM and a DC-to-DR switch; both were positioned as ready for the proposed 5-minute bidding window.

BESS merchant capacity cited: ACME about 3,200 MWh, Juniper about 500 MWh, Adani about 3,400 MWh, with more than Rs 9,000 crore of BESS VGF support. Management said the arbitrage window may last 3-5 years.
The SECI 500 MW CfD pilot for peak power was cited as launched; it is a peak-power product, not solar.
demand_pricing: Management expects demand growth of about 5-5.5% a year, versus 11% in Q1 FY27 on heat and delayed monsoon. Peak demand touched about 271 GW in May and July.
Management said exchanges as a group grew 18% in FY26 against 1% demand growth.

On market coupling, CERC proposed Grid India as Market Coupling Operator, with DAM first. Management said it has challenged the July 2025 order at APTEL (order dated 13 February 2026) and is now before the Supreme Court; a second hearing was held on 27 July 2026.
Management said that even after coupling, DAM share could fall 20-40%, but said business impact would not be significant. The market-share loss figure is management's own estimate.
Management said top-10 sellers account for about 40% of the sell side and the top-buyer concentration is 50-60%, with 800-900 participants daily.

Management cited an RTM realisation issue in a Q&A: an analyst's per-unit realisation calculation (about 0.4 paisa vs 3.7 paisa a year earlier) was not reconciled; management pointed to incentives in REC and TAM.

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to 25-year PPAs covering about 85% of DISCOM demand, with DAM used for seasonal and daily shortfalls and RTM used to handle renewable variability; it said PPAs will persist because banks lend only against them.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-duration 11-month Term-Ahead contract timeline, given the application is over two years old?

qa_highlights.question: How does the 0.3% social welfare gain claim and DAM coupling risk relate to customer concentration, and what is the buyer/seller concentration?

qa_highlights.question: Are there further price hikes from customers to offset steel-driven margin compression in Engineering and MFP, or is Q1 profitability the underlying run-rate?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly Rs 40-50 Cr reduction in e-mobility negative EBIT, and is this one-off?

qa_highlights.question: Are e-mobility losses past peak and what are breakeven timelines?

qa_highlights.question: How much standalone capital will be infused into new ventures in FY27?

540767|2026-03.headline: NAM India posted record FY26 PAT of INR 15.29 bn (+19% YoY) and record quarterly operating profit of INR 4.93 bn (+39% YoY) in Q4 FY26.
540767|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was a record operating profit quarter for Nippon Life India AMC, with revenue of INR 7.39 bn (+30% YoY) despite a 14.5% QoQ fall in the Nifty. Mutual fund QAAUM grew 30.1% YoY to INR 7.25 trn and market share rose to 8.89%, its highest since June 2019. Profit after tax of INR 3.85 bn was down 5% QoQ, mainly due to negative other income and a lower tax rate. Management flagged flattening industry SIP net inflows, a pass-through SEBI regulation impact of 3.5-4 bps on equity AUM from April 1, and a proposed SIF launch that is not yet live.

540767|2026-06.headline: Nippon Life AMC posted record quarterly PAT of INR 5.04 bn (up 27% YoY) and operating profit of INR 4.94 bn (up 31% YoY) on 22.7% YoY MF QAAUM growth.

Mutual fund market share rose to 9.04%, its highest since June 2019, with the largest absolute AUM growth in the industry. Revenue grew 26% YoY, while operating expenses rose 19% YoY and 11% QoQ on digital, technology and brand investment, which management expects to continue for six to eight quarters. Management also outlined SIF readiness, a proposed DWS JV for the AIF subsidiary (DWS to take 40%, pending approvals), and a temporary cap on bullion ETF inflows.

540767|2026-09.headline: NAM India's Q2 FY27 operating profit hit a record INR 5.23 bn (+25% YoY), but PAT fell to INR 3.24 bn after a INR 96.76 crore SEBI settlement charge.
540767|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to INR 7.96 bn and operating profit rose 25% YoY to a record INR 5.23 bn, with operating expenses up 14% YoY. PAT declined both YoY and QoQ to INR 3.24 bn because of a one-time exceptional item: the INR 96.76 crore settlement with SEBI over the Yes Bank AT-1 bond investments by certain NIMF schemes. Mutual fund market share was 9.02%, flat QoQ, and equity yield compressed to 52 bps (ex-arbitrage) from about 54 bps in Q1, which management attributed to telescopic pricing and equity inflows. The Board declared an interim dividend of INR 9.50 per share.

qa_highlights.question: Why did equity yield fall QoQ when peers saw yield improvement from mix shift, and was the drop sharp after adjusting for an extra day?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the compression to rapid equity AUM growth (among the highest in the industry) and telescopic pricing, with no regulatory impact in Q2 since changes occurred in Q1. Equity yield was 52 bps ex-arbitrage versus about 54 bps in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What was the AT-1 bond case about and what triggered the provision this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the INR 96.76 crore settlement details and said there is nothing further to add until SEBI communicates further. The provision was made after SEBI's in-principle acceptance of the settlement terms during the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company launch SIFs and when?

qa_highlights.question: How are flows in small-cap and flexi-cap holding up amid corrections, and what is the distributor communication?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it stopped lump-sum flows into its small-cap fund three years ago, and inflows are dispersed to multi-cap and large-cap. Monthly SIP inflows of about INR 32 bn (roughly INR 3,200 crore) are cited as a protection, and distributors are being pushed toward hybrid, multi-asset and fixed-income products.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost and opex outlook, and ESOP expense for FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Is the offshore AUM decline reversible and what new offshore products are planned?

540768|2026-03.headline: Mahindra Logistics returned to profit in Q4 FY26, with reported PAT of INR20.2 crores versus a INR6.7 crores loss a year earlier.
540768|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14% YoY to INR1,791 crores and gross margin expanded to 10.5% from 9.5%. Adjusted EBITDA (after deducting long-term lease rent) rose to INR57 crores, a 3.2% margin versus 2.4% a year earlier. Full-year reported PAT was INR2.3 crores against a INR35.8 crores loss in FY25, after a Q3 exceptional gratuity charge under the new Labour Codes. Express (MESPL) remained EBITDA-negative for FY26 but gross-margin positive for the full year and close to EBITDA breakeven per management. Freight forwarding faces West Asia-related headwinds going into FY27.

segments.name: Contract Logistics
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR1,381 crores (+12% YoY); FY26 revenue INR5,490 crores (+16%) and reported EBITDA INR389 crores (+24% vs INR314 crores). Management cites gross margin growth of 19% in Q4 from exiting non-profitable customers.

segments.name: Express (MESPL)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 49% YoY; FY26 revenue INR449 crores (+25%), gross margin 1.3% for the full year. Quarterly GM rose from INR20 lakh in Q2 to INR2.7 crores in Q3 and INR6.6 crores in Q4. FY26 EBITDA loss INR31 crores vs INR51 crores loss in FY25.

segments.name: Freight Forwarding
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR89 crores (+17% YoY); gross margin +50% YoY. FY26 revenue grew 14%, EBITDA INR10.1 crores vs INR6.8 crores in FY25. Q4 growth is now facing West Asia-related headwinds.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR386 crores (+22% vs INR316 crores). Q4 revenue grew 42% YoY and gross margin 17% YoY; growth driven by large B2B accounts, with utilisation improvement a focus on the asset-heavy Alyte Prive premium offering in Delhi.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR72 crores (-18% YoY, from INR89 crores) after deliberate site exits. Gross margin rose to INR6.5 crores in Q4 from INR2.7 crores in Q3; EBITDA moved from a INR1 crore loss in Q3 to a INR2.2 crore profit in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is Express volume growth, and can it sustain mid-teens revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Express volume growth is mid-to-high teens YoY, and that a mid-teens revenue growth target is achievable. Volume is no longer disclosed alone as it is not a sufficient metric without yield.

qa_highlights.question: Is adjusted EBITDA margin likely to surpass the pre-Ind AS FY18-19 levels of about 3.6-3.9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it agreed directionally but gave no forward guidance and said the turnaround has only just started.

qa_highlights.question: When will Express reach EBITDA breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA breakeven is the immediate goal and it is 'very close', but gave no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further last-mile pruning or declines to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all last-mile pruning was done in FY26 and the business is now expected to grow with profitable clients.

qa_highlights.question: Are there similar receivable provisions expected? What drove the INR28 crore credit provision?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the provision reflects prudence on aged receivables under management judgment. She said nothing similar warrants provisioning at present.

qa_highlights.question: Is the West Asia conflict affecting other segments, and how would a fuel price spike affect the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only Freight Forwarding is affected so far; other segments are on plan. A 10-15% diesel rise would be passed through immediately, but management flagged broader economic inflation risk.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share industry-level yield comparisons or the e-commerce share of Express revenue, citing competitive sensitivity.

540768|2026-06.headline: Mahindra Logistics swung to Q1 FY27 PAT of INR 25.4 crore from a INR 10.8 crore loss, with consolidated revenue up 23% to INR 2,003 crore.

Adjusted (Ind AS 116) EBITDA was INR 57 crore, up 76% YoY, at 2.8% margin. PAT of INR 25.4 crore includes INR 4 crore of interest on income tax refund, so operating PAT was about INR 21.4 crore. Contract Logistics gross margin was diluted YoY by start-up costs, manpower shortages and minimum wage revisions, while the Express business reached a positive gross margin and narrower EBITDA loss.

rows.label: Express EBITDA breakeven in FY27

540768|2026-09.headline: Mahindra Logistics Q2 FY27 PAT rose to INR26 crore (from a INR10 crore loss) and MESPL (Rivigo) turned EBITDA-positive at INR2.3 crore.

Contract logistics (about 80% of revenue) grew 28% with EBITDA of INR115 crore, while gross margin stayed at 10.1% consolidated (up 40 bps QoQ). MESPL (Rivigo) posted its first EBITDA-positive quarter, and management pivoted the last-mile business from a no-loss to a growth strategy. Freight forwarding revenue fell 44% YoY on leadership transition, and a tech transformation project was approved for start around Q4 FY27.

vs loss of INR10 crore in Q2 FY26; vs INR25 crore in Q1 FY27
vs minus INR210 crore in H1 FY26

qa_highlights.question: Why was the sequential contract logistics gross margin improvement only 30 bps given fuel pass-through and onboarding?

qa_highlights.answer: Growth from new clients, wallet share, e-commerce and LMD; cost control largely played out, so growth is the main lever now. New business wins are running ahead of the 3.5x internal target.

Monsoon shortfall (14% below LPA) and uneven regional impact.

540769|2026-03.headline: New India Assurance FY26 profit after tax rose 40% to INR 1,384 crore, but combined ratio worsened to 122.57% on wage-revision charges.

Incurred claim ratio rose to 98.65% on Motor TP court awards, the Air India aviation loss, marine claims and NATCAT flood claims not fully recovered under reinsurance. Management guided to a Motor single-digit growth and double-digit overall growth in FY27, led by Health Retail.

540774|2026-03.headline: IFGL Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 2% YoY to INR 276 crore and FY26 consolidated income grew 14% to INR 1,904 crore; consolidated Q4 EBITDA margin 8.6%.
540774|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 total income was INR 278 crore (+2% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 11.8%, while FY26 standalone EBITDA margin was 11.3%. Domestic revenue grew 7% YoY in Q4 and 20% for FY26 to INR 864 crore, but exports fell 11% in FY26 on geopolitical and market headwinds. Margins were hit by product mix shifts, lower exports and higher raw material and freight costs. Management also announced a senior leadership reshuffle, with Mukesh Rawal moving to India operations and Manoj Rakhecha to international operations.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 2.15 per share (21.5% of face value)

segments.name: Domestic (India)

segments.name: Exports (India-made)
segments.commentary: Export revenue fell 11% in FY26 on geopolitical and external market headwinds. Management says volumes have started to improve, and it has added manpower to rebuild export accounts.

segments.name: USA (Americas)

segments.commentary: Management reports strong performance with healthy growth, operating leverage and sustained customer demand. Phase 1 of the India technology transfer is complete.

segments.name: Hofmann Ceramics (Germany)
segments.commentary: Losses fell significantly in FY26 after turnaround steps and cost cuts. Management expects the business to move close to breakeven during FY27.

segments.name: Monocon (UK)
segments.commentary: Revenue recovered despite losing a key high-margin UK customer after a plant closure. Management targets breakeven by Q4 FY27 and is entering foundry and new geographies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Monocon's turnaround and pricing?

qa_highlights.question: Why are exports underwhelming, and is it a deliberate pullback?

540774|2026-06.headline: IFGL Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA fell 17% YoY to INR31 crore on raw material and LPG cost spikes, while consolidated PAT rose 58% to INR17 crore.
540774|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue rose 8% YoY to INR297 crore, with domestic up 7% and exports up 9%, but gross margin fell to 43% from 47% on higher raw material prices. Standalone EBITDA dropped 17% YoY to INR31 crore as input costs and LPG availability constraints outpaced price increases, which management says will pass through with a lag. Consolidated total income rose 13% YoY to INR515 crore and consolidated EBITDA rose 2% to INR40 crore, with PAT up 58% to INR17 crore. The Europe segment was weak because British Steel's low output cut offtake at Sheffield Refractories, while US operations grew double digits with improving margins.

540775|2026-03.headline: Khadim India Q4 FY26 revenue fell to INR83.6 crores (vs INR93.8 crores) with PAT of just INR0.77 crores; FY27 target is ~INR400 crores at 14% EBITDA.
540775|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations declined to INR83.6 crores from INR93.8 crores a year earlier, with gross margin of 51.5%, EBITDA of INR11.9 crores (14.3% margin) and PAT of INR0.77 crores (0.9% margin). For FY26, revenue fell 12% to INR367.1 crores, EBITDA was INR49.1 crores (13.4%) and PAT INR3.1 crores. Management attributed the decline to store closures, lower primary sales to franchisees and deliberate inventory and creditor reduction, which cost an estimated INR10-15 crores of sales over the last two quarters. The company also completed the demerger of its distribution and manufacturing business into KSR Footwear Limited during the year.

qa_highlights.answer: Price cuts on products under INR500 over the last 1-2 years; Q4 margin improved and FY27 ASP increases should keep gross margin at 48-50%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was inventory reduced sharply (about 40% YoY)?
qa_highlights.answer: A deliberate call to cut inventory days; some Q4 sales were lost, and the company cleared discounted stock and reduced creditors.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue not recover in Q4 after inventory correction?
qa_highlights.answer: Stock replenishment ordered in Q4 arrives in Q1, so the benefit flows in one to two quarters; INR10-15 crores of sales lost over the last two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company moving from mass value to premium?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said Khadim remains a middle-class mass value brand and will add premium products such as British Walkers and Sharon as a blend.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade payables fall from about INR196 crores to INR111 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly the demerger, since last year's figure included both entities; the rest came from deliberately reduced purchases and creditor payments in Q3 and Q4.

Revenue was INR 865 million (INR 86.5 crore) and first-half revenue grew 13% to about INR 1,750 million. Net profit was INR 7.1 crore, lower than Q1, as the company chose to keep investing in technology, product and brand. The rights issue lifted net worth to INR 11,360 million from INR 650 crore at end-March 2026, and the company launched a rebuilt trading and investing app, AlgoSpace and AI assistant "Ask 5paisa".

segments.commentary: Average funding book around INR 480 crore, spread across a large client base rather than a few clients; management said growth is being pursued carefully.

540777|2026-03.headline: HDFC Life FY26 VNB rose only 2% to INR 4,034 crores; NBM fell to 24.2% after GST and surrender-value impacts, with Q4 growth slowing at HDFC Bank.
540777|2026-03.overview: FY26 individual APE grew 7% YoY, but top-line growth fell below the company's original expectation, with the slowdown concentrated in Q4 from unabsorbed GST, softer bancassurance and deferred demand in March. Proprietary channels grew 15-16% in Q4 and FY26, and protection grew 43% for the year. VNB rose 2% to INR 4,034 crores and NBM fell 140 bps to 24.2%, with 130 bps from GST/SSV, 90 bps from fixed-cost absorption, and 40 bps from persistency assumption strengthening, partly offset by 120 bps of product mix. Management said the GST drag is tapering (about 110 bps in Q4) and should be neutralised by H1 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: 16% growth excl. GST and labour code impact

segments.commentary: Unit-linked 44%, non-par savings 18%, participating 25%, term 7% (vs 5% in FY25), annuity 5%. Management expects non-par to regain share in FY27.

segments.commentary: Grew 43% in FY26 and 46% in Q4; retail protection mix rose about 200 bps to 7.2%, and about 10% including riders. Around 80% of post-GST protection buyers are new to HDFC Life.

segments.commentary: Mix rose about 300 bps YoY to around 8% of individual APE in Q4; AGNI, a variable annuity linked to Nifty 50, launched in Q4 at a ticket size of INR 25 lakh and above.

segments.commentary: Grew about 500 bps ahead of the company; over 250 branches added in 30 months contribute about 13% of agency top line. FC base grew 43% gross.

segments.commentary: MFI business grew about 13% for the full year; Q4 MFI growth exceeded 40% on a subdued base.

demand_pricing: Competition in the HDFC Bank channel is driven by aggressive pricing and underwriting. Management says it has stepped back from loss-making cohorts and will not match outlier IRRs on non-par.

Unit-linked demand remained resilient through FY26, with higher protection multiples and better rider attachment.

qa_highlights.question: How has counter share in HDFC Bank changed in Q4 vs the nine months, and what gives confidence it will normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 counter share was lower than the 9-month level; FY26 closed in the early 60s% vs mid-60s% prior year. Management says it knows which cohorts it let go and what it takes to compete back, and expects to regain share as GST costs are absorbed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the participating fund in deficit and why is new business strain rising faster?
qa_highlights.answer: Deficit reflects GST ITC loss on renewal commission and maintenance expenses, plus higher surrender-value reserves from October 2024 regulation changes. Strain rose because of protection and credit protect growth, higher ULIP multiples and rider attachment, and GST impact.

qa_highlights.question: Can VNB grow in line with the 2023 plan, and what is the normalised three-year VNB CAGR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says FY23-FY26 CAGR was about 3%; adjusting for roughly INR 1,000 crore of GST and SSV effects, the normalised three-year VNB CAGR would be about 9-10%. Management expects a 1.8x-2x growth over four years to remain the aim.

qa_highlights.question: Why did persistency assumption changes and the yield-curve movement not show up separately in the VNB walk?
qa_highlights.answer: Economic assumption changes are captured within product profile rather than shown separately, since repricing is dynamic. Persistency sensitivity rose because ULIP mix increased and surrender-value rules now affect non-linked margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand to deeper markets, and what are the returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says Tier 2 and 3 is a priority, with customers acquired in FY26 over 72% new to HDFC Life and Tier 2/3 growing faster than Tier 1. Payback is about 1.5x longer than metro branches.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the dividend maintained when a INR 1,000 crore preferential issue is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the capital is growth capital for protection, the dividend is business as usual for retail and pension shareholders, and the company balanced both objectives by keeping the payout flat.

540777|2026-06.headline: HDFC Life Q1 FY27 VNB rose 9% to INR 879 crores at a 25% margin, with individual APE up 7% and HDFC Bank channel subdued.
540777|2026-06.overview: Individual APE grew 7% YoY and overall APE 9%, led by credit life and group, while channels excluding HDFC Bank grew about 17% with agency up 21%. VNB rose 9% to INR 879 crores and new business margin was 25%, up 100 bps QoQ, after absorbing about 60 bps residual GST impact. Profit after tax was INR 611 crores (up 12%, or 17% excluding GST), embedded value INR 65,860 crores and solvency 185%. 13-month persistency moderated about 200 bps to 84%, and HDFC Bank channel business stayed soft as the company ceded share during competitive pricing in FY26 and says it has now recovered.

financial_highlights.change: +100 bps QoQ; GST impact approx. 60 bps
Improved after INR 1,000 crore preferential allotment by HDFC Bank; additional sub-debt capacity INR 500 crores (about 4% upside)

segments.commentary: Grew 21% YoY, ahead of company average, with healthy traction in protection and annuity. Branches opened in the past 24 months contribute about 16% of agency APE; term and annuity share of agency rose from 15% to 27%.

segments.name: Non-bank alliances
segments.commentary: Retail protection grew 60% YoY, driven mainly by aggregators; market share across partners broadly stable.

segments.name: HDFC Bank channel
segments.commentary: Subdued growth as the bank base is large and the company let share go in competitive segments in 4-6 months of FY26. Share has recovered toward year-ago levels on a run-rate basis; HDFC Bank contributed 47% of retail APE this quarter.

segments.name: Banca beyond HDFC Bank
segments.commentary: Grew about 15% in the quarter as competitive intensity moderated across other banks.

segments.name: Product mix (individual APE)
segments.commentary: Unit-linked 44%, non-par savings 22% (run-rate mid-20s by quarter-end), participating 15%, retail protection 8% (about 11% including riders), annuities 11% (nearly doubled from 5%). Protection grew over 40% YoY; credit protect grew 19%.

segments.commentary: Market share 43% with AUM of about INR 1.75 lakh crores, up 33% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 aspiration unchanged: grow in line with or faster than the industry, and deliver VNB growth broadly in line with APE growth.
Industry growth base case about 15-17%; company needs to grow a little over 16% over the remaining nine months to match industry-level growth.
New business margin expected to remain range-bound around current levels (about 25%); management says the company will prioritise growth over margin expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Why has margin improved only modestly over the last 7-8 years versus peers, and what is the basis for confidence in FY27 growth and VNB?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins expanded 100-150 bps per two-year period to FY22, then fell about 90 bps (FY22-24) on regulatory changes, with 26.3% in FY24 and a 100 bps surrender-charge impact in FY25; the GST impact was 300 bps, of which about 110 bps remained at FY26 end, 50 bps was absorbed in Q1 and about 60 bps is still to go. Growth confidence rests on agency (up 21%) and proprietary channels (up over 20%).

qa_highlights.question: Will non-par and product mix sustain, and what happens to margins if ULIP picks up?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said ULIP mix will not rise meaningfully, non-par expected to hold mid-20s share, annuities to stay well above last year, and NBM to stay around 25%-odd. Protection's share may stay roughly where it is, and growth may be higher in the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Has the HDFC Bank counter share recovered, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bank share has returned to roughly the level of a year ago on a run-rate basis, with pricing more benign; the company declined to give channel-wise growth guidance and said it is tracking selectively by segment (non-par, protection, par over unit-linked).

qa_highlights.question: Is the non-par recovery demand-led or a result of company pricing and yield-curve effects?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it is a combination: competitor intensity has eased, the company can compete on sensible terms, headline rates are higher than a year ago, and customer asset allocation toward guaranteed products is also a driver. He said the company will not compete on price alone.

qa_highlights.question: What is the banca growth outlook, and how does HDFC Bank compare on a 2-year CAGR basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Banca beyond HDFC Bank grew about 15% in Q1. HDFC Bank was described as marginally lower or flattish YoY; on a 2-year CAGR basis it is similar to other banks at about 10%, and management guided 10-12% growth for HDFC Bank.

qa_highlights.question: How much runway does capital have before a fundraise, and what is the variable annuity opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Solvency is 185% with INR 500 crore sub-debt capacity (about 4% upside); management is comfortable with 15-18 months runway at the current run rate. Variable annuity: two product structures launched, aimed at customers willing to commit for a longer period, slightly younger and with lower ticket sizes; margins said to be above company average.

qa_highlights.question: What is the persistency outlook, given traditional persistency fell from 88-89% to about 83%?
qa_highlights.answer: Appointed Actuary cited a shift to lower ticket sizes after the tax change, a product feature that drove lapses (now moderated, about 40-50 bps effect), and the Q1 March-pace effect. Expected traditional persistency range is 84-85%; 87-88% was not expected in the near term.

540777|2026-09.headline: HDFC Life H1 FY27 VNB rose 12% to ₹2,037 crore at a 24.7% margin, while solvency fell to 180% on capital consumption.
540777|2026-09.overview: Q2 individual APE growth of 13% (overall) and 11% in H1 kept HDFC Life ahead of the private industry, with individual weighted received premium up 11% in Q2 and market share up 10bps to 16.2%. VNB reached ₹2,037 crore (up 12%, Q2 up 15%) and margin expanded to 24.7% from 24.5%. Persistency softened on unit-linked renewals and a non-par cohort, and the EV walk showed negative operating and investment variances from equity underperformance, yield rises and wider credit spreads. Solvency fell to 180%, prompting a ₹500 crore subordinated debt raise. Management spent much of the call on the IRDAI distribution-economics consultation paper, where it was non-committal on specifics.

qa_highlights.question: What changed at HDFC Bank that drove growth recovery, and did IRRs or commissions change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited granular branch-level engagement, a withdrawal of extra contests about a year ago, and fixing credit and people issues over the last 3-4 months. Rates were kept competitive with higher yields; no change in commercial payouts.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EV walk operating variance is persistency, and what drove the investment variance?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating variance was primarily unit-linked persistency plus residual non-par run-off. Investment variance came from equity returns of about 3-3.5% versus 5% expected, a 25-30bps short-end yield rise, and wider credit spreads.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the capital consumption and how will solvency evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term profitable products lock capital under the current regime; the sub-debt adds about 4 percentage points, and management expects to remain comfortably above 150% through FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How do the proposed commission limits affect VNB margin and EoM?
qa_highlights.answer: Expense ratio about 21%, with commissions more than half; under the proposed levels, commissions fall to half or less, so a 15% EoM is mathematically achievable, subject to scale and glide-path considerations.

qa_highlights.question: Is persistency pressure concentrated in TULIPs or the wider unit-linked book?
qa_highlights.answer: Not limited to any product: pressure is uniform across unit-linked. Recent unit-linked persistency variance is captured in the EV; management expects most to be recovered by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit life share, and what is the HDFC Bank share of it?
qa_highlights.answer: HDFC Bank contributes less than one-third of credit life business, which is diversified across MFIs, NBFCs, banks and the HDFC Group. Management would not disclose the bundled-versus-separate premium collection mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Palghar GST demand, and does the appeal change the provisioning stance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the balance-sheet figure is correct and it is treated as a contingent liability (₹942 crore base, with the accrued total in the books). Interest is excluded and management is confident on the merits, so no provision was taken; contingent liabilities rose to ₹2,207 crore from ₹1,870 crore.

Equity and yield volatility driving investment variance and the EV walk.

540795|2026-03.headline: Dynamic Cables Q4 FY26 revenue growth slowed to 7% YoY (core products ~20%), with a greenfield plant delayed to September 2026 and order book at INR808 crores.

Q4 overall growth was only 7% because low-value LV conductors and railway signalling cables were discontinued, while core products grew about 20%. The greenfield capacity has slipped roughly 15 months versus earlier guidance and is now targeted to start production around September 2026. Order book stood at INR808 crores at 31 March 2026, with management attributing softer March order booking to aluminium and PVC price spikes.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 growth came from volume versus realisation, and why is growth soft?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall Q4 growth was 7%, but core products grew about 20%; the gap reflects discontinued LV conductors and railway cables. Realisation grew 12% and volume 8% for core products. The high Q4 FY25 base (38-39% growth) and March order deferrals also weighed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 growth outlook given the capex delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated that it does not give yearly guidance and that long-term growth is 18-20%. H1 FY27 is to be served from existing capacity, with the new plant targeted for September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the greenfield plant slip?
qa_highlights.answer: Three causes: delayed regulatory approvals, imported machinery shipments delayed by freight issues after the Iran war, and AERB compliance requirements. Management now says most machinery and civil work is done.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to gross margin and other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin varies with product, customer and freight mix and steered analysts to operating margin, which was steady at the 10.5-11% guided range. Employee cost decline was attributed to a one-time Q4 FY25 bonus accrual.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TS Conductor tie-up and what does it mean for revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an entry step into the high-voltage conductor market using carbon core HTLS technology, mainly for the domestic market. Product approvals and type testing take about a year, and there is no hard revenue timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 capacity be enough, and what is the next capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is fungible across products. Next capex is not yet decided, but incremental capex is directionally expected to sustain growth.

The company entered the US market in the quarter with first supplies, and the new capacity expansion is on track for commissioning from September 2026, with meaningful revenue expected from Q4. Order book stood at INR811 crore as of 30 June 2026, with customers booking shorter cycles at elevated prices.
