rows.why: Credit cost fell to 1.8% from 2.0% in Q4 FY26 and management expects a slight further improvement within the 1.6%-1.8% guide, though EEB credit cost is 3.3% and 0-90 DPD rose to 3.5% from 3.1%.

rows.label: Tech cost taper
rows.why: Tech cost ~8% of total cost to be kept within 10% and tapered to 8%; management says investment years run to FY28 with productivity gains in about 18 months, so opex relief is back-ended.

tone.note: Management was confident on credit cost, asset quality, CASA growth and the 14% advance guide, but cautious on margin (6.5% NIM line of sight withdrawn), opex-to-assets at 4.3% and the ROA aspiration; analysts pushed on funding costs, why the ROA was cut, and the slowdown in retail and mortgage grow

541153|2026-09.headline: Bandhan Bank Q2 FY27 PAT rose 5.5x YoY to INR 622 crore, with ROA at 1.2% and ROE at 9.3%.
541153|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed a sharp earnings recovery: PAT of INR 622 crore (up 23.9% QoQ, 5.5x YoY) and operating profit of INR 1,556 crore (up 18.8% YoY). Net CD ratio fell to 89.5% from about 92% as deposits grew 4.7% QoQ without FCNR(B) support. Loan book grew 13.1% YoY to about INR 1.58 lakh crore, with the EEB book stabilising sequentially. CASA weakened as savings balances ran off after rate recalibration, and management flagged this as below expectations.

segments.name: EEB (Emerging Entrepreneur Business)
segments.commentary: Portfolio INR 52,616 crore, broadly flat QoQ and +1.7% YoY; de-growth arrested. Collection efficiency 99.3% vs 98.9% in Q1; EEB DPD pool fell to INR 1,529 crore from INR 1,842 crore; EEB slippages INR 655 crore.

segments.name: Wholesale Banking
segments.commentary: Grew 31.6% YoY and is now 34% of advances; management says wholesale ROA is improving and rising ROA supports overall ROA.

segments.name: Retail assets
segments.commentary: Grew 41.9% YoY, led by commercial vehicles, construction equipment, auto and gold loans; 11% of advances. Retail products remain not yet ROA-positive.

segments.name: Housing finance
segments.commentary: 22% of advances; growth impacted by verticalisation and asset-quality issues, with management saying impact may extend one more quarter.

segments.name: Microfinance (MFI)
segments.commentary: Book flat QoQ after several quarters of decline; management targets 8%-10% growth in Q3 and Q4. Current yield about 21.69%; new origination rates 23.5%-23.9%.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Total INR 1.73 lakh crore, +9.2% YoY and +4.7% QoQ; retail deposits 72.7% of base; CASA INR 46,132 crore (+4.3% YoY), CASA ratio 26.7%; current accounts +36.9% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 loan growth target of about 14% maintained; implies roughly 6% growth per half in H2 per analyst arithmetic.
Q4 FY27 exit ROA guidance of 1.2%-1.4% unchanged; 1.2% already achieved in Q2. Medium-term ROA aspiration 1.6%-1.8%, timing under review.
NIM expected to remain in 6.1%-6.2% range; repo-linked repricing from January 1 (Q4) could give a positive NIM impact.
Operating expense to total assets guidance of 4.2% unchanged.
Credit cost could improve from 1.8% to 1.7% per management's illustrative ROA bridge.
Full-year FY27 PSLC cost around INR 120 crore (about INR 31 crore per quarter); expected to be near zero in FY28.
Employee cost assumed to stay at about similar levels through Q4 FY27 (analyst reference INR 1,300-1,400 crore run rate).
Deposit growth to remain slightly above loan growth; management acknowledged deposit growth needs to be faster.
ECL transition impact estimated at about INR 2,200 crore against capital, with RBI five-year amortisation window; flow impact of 15-20 bps per quarter.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 2,001 branches (13 added in quarter) and 4,414 banking units (14 added).
Housing finance centres converted into branches under branch banking; onboarding, underwriting and operations segregated.
Credit card launched in the quarter with four variants: Sparks, Ignite, Flare and Lumina.
Technology platform replacement generated about INR 50 crore annual savings (INR 12 crore per quarter), benefit received in Q2; ongoing technology spend continues.
demand_pricing: Processing fee income +30% YoY, driven by higher EEB disbursements and a 25 bps processing-charge increase in February.
Third-party distribution income +26% YoY and +26% QoQ; ARC-related income +16% YoY; treasury gains on investment sales +39% QoQ.
Bancassurance: draft commission cap could cut third-party income; management has not completed a detailed study and says mitigation levers include product mix, mutual funds and wholesale fee income.
Savings account balances fell after rate recalibration; Annapurna scheme flows (about INR 4,000 crore monthly, West Bengal) shifted timing and affected CASA.
Retail sub-scale products (book INR 2,000-3,000 crore each) are not yet ROA-positive; management expects positive ROA in two to three quarters.
Industry deposit comparisons are harder as peers used FCNR(B) leverage facilities that Bandhan did not have.

qa_highlights.question: How much SA attrition and cost of funds/NIM pressure is expected in H2 after the SA rate cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said deposit costs have not come under pressure, cost of funds should moderate, and it still expects NIM in the 6.1%-6.2% range. CASA dip was attributed partly to Annapurna timing; new digital features and credit cards are expected to help.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ECL day-one impact and credit cost implications?
qa_highlights.answer: Transition impact estimated at about INR 2,200 crore based on March 2026 flow rates, hitting capital not P&L, with a five-year amortisation window. Flow impact 15-20 bps per quarter; management expects a favourable change as DPD pools improve.

qa_highlights.question: Could bancassurance income fall about 60% under the draft norms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not completed a detailed study; says insurance business is predominantly retail and semi-urban, consent-based, with no credit-linked insurance, and expects to offset a large part through other fee lines.

qa_highlights.question: Is processing fee growth sustainable, and what is the implied H2 loan growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Processing fee growth is tied to disbursements and expected to continue. Management maintains 14% full-year loan growth target and aims for deposit growth slightly above loan growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Assam SMA uptick and is EEB slippage likely to ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Four districts moved to moratorium (INR 406 crore), with 5% additional provision and over 96% of the book standard. Assam SMA-0 rose from 0.8% to 1.3% due to floods; management sees no material impact from Karnataka, Maharashtra or Andhra Pradesh climate-affected areas.

qa_highlights.question: How will repo changes affect NIM and what share of the book is repo-linked?
qa_highlights.answer: Repo changes apply to existing loans from the next quarter start, so the January change lands in Q4; Q3 largely unaffected. About 49% repo-linked, 3% MCLR, 48% fixed. Management does not expect a major effect this year; 25 bps repo move transmits about 10-11 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why did wholesale and retail grow faster and how is opex trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets one-third each of EEB, wholesale and retail/housing; EEB share now about 33%. Employee cost is up about 20% due to the new Labour Code wage norms; headcount broadly stable for three quarters.

risks_watch: SA balances and CASA ratio (26.7%) under pressure after rate recalibration; watch whether attrition continues into Q3.
Bancassurance commission cap: management has not quantified impact; analyst cited a possible about 60% fee hit if draft norms are adopted as proposed.
Housing business: management says disruption may extend one more quarter into Q3.
EEB stress from Assam floods (SMA-0 at 1.3%) and drought areas; Maharashtra is 2.6% of EEB book.
Deposit growth lag (9.2% YoY) versus industry boosted by FCNR(B) flows; bulk deposits used for liquidity management.
ECL transition impact of about INR 2,200 crore to be recalculated on March 2027 portfolio.
541153|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on earnings momentum and asset-quality trends, but cautious and somewhat defensive on savings deposits, housing and deposit growth. Several answers were hedged ("hopeful", "we are working on it") when asked about bancassurance impact and H2 growth, with no quantified bancassurance estimate given.
key_quotes: Our performance during the quarter demonstrates the underlying resilience of the franchise.
We do not intend to use bulk funding as a structural source to drive loan growth.
There is no change in our guidance.
We should have performed much better in home loans.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM guided flat at 6.1%-6.2% (Q2 at 6.1% vs 6.2% in Q1), with repo-linked repricing from January 1 expected to help Q4; 49% of book is repo-linked but 25 bps repo move transmits only about 10-11 bps, so impact is limited.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch network grew by 13 to 2,001 and banking units by 14 to 4,414 in Q2, and housing finance centres are being converted into branches; the pace is steady but modest, not a major capacity step-up.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 loan growth target of about 14% is held, but Q2 was 13.1% YoY, so H2 needs roughly 6% per half; MFI is guided at 8%-10% growth in Q3 and Q4 and deposits are growing 9.2% YoY, slightly below the loan book.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not discussed and no new plant or major capex is flagged; the spend focus is on technology, with about INR 50 crore annual savings from the platform replacement already received.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q4 exit ROA guidance of 1.2%-1.4% is unchanged even though Q2 already hit 1.2%, and FY27 loan growth of about 14%, opex-to-assets of 4.2% and credit cost guidance were all held rather than raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Bancassurance draft commission cap could cut third-party income, with an analyst-cited possible fee hit of about 60% not quantified by management; housing disruption may run one more quarter; SA/CASA attrition (CASA ratio 26.7%) and Assam SMA-0 rising to 1.3% add risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Credit card launched in Q2 with four variants (Sparks, Ignite, Flare, Lumina); retail sub-scale products of INR 2,000-3,000 crore each are expected to turn ROA-positive in two to three quarters.

rows.label: Bancassurance commission cap under draft norms
rows.why: Analyst cited a possible about 60% hit to bancassurance fee income if draft norms pass as proposed; management has not completed a study, and mitigation via product mix, mutual funds and wholesale fees is only hinted.

rows.label: ECL transition impact on capital
rows.why: About INR 2,200 crore capital impact at March 2026 flow rates, amortised over five years under RBI norms, with flow impact of 15-20 bps per quarter; to be recalculated on March 2027 portfolio.

rows.label: Technology platform savings
rows.why: Platform replacement is generating about INR 50 crore annual savings (INR 12 crore per quarter), already received in Q2, though employee cost is up about 20% from Labour Code wage norms.

tone.note: Management was confident on earnings momentum, ROA at 1.2% and asset quality (GNPA 3.1%, collection efficiency 99.3%), but cautious and defensive on SA deposits, CASA at 26.7%, housing and deposit growth lagging the loan book; analysts pressed on bancassurance impact, H2 loan growth implied at about

541154|2026-03.headline: HAL FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR33,050 crore and EBITDA 13,472 crore; FY27 guided to 10-12% growth, with LCA Mk-1A deliveries pushed to August-September.
541154|2026-03.overview: HAL reported FY26 revenue from operations of INR33,050 crore (up 7% from INR30,981 crore), with EBITDA up 11% to INR13,472 crore at around 30% margin and PBT up 12% to INR12,112 crore. Manufacturing revenue rose to INR9,227 crore from INR7,957 crore, while ROH revenue was INR20,524 crore. Order book rose to INR2,54,538 crore after FY26 fresh orders of INR97,028 crore. The main overhang is the delayed LCA Mk-1A delivery to the IAF, which management now targets for August-September 2026, tied to GE engine supply.

financial_highlights.change: +11% vs INR12,168 crore; ~30% of revenue, flat YoY

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR9,227 crore, about 28% of total, driven by ALH, AL-31FP and RD-33 deliveries. Management expects it to grow faster than ROH as LCA Mk-1A and HTT-40 deliveries start; mix is expected to move towards 50:50 over time.

segments.name: ROH (repair and overhaul) and spares
segments.commentary: FY26 ROH revenue INR20,524 crore, about 62% of total. Spares sales fell by about INR500-600 crore YoY, while R&O was flat because no new platform was added. ROH is expected to rise once LCA and LCH enter overhaul cycles, with LCA ROH expected in roughly three years.

segments.name: Exports and development
segments.commentary: Export revenue was INR501 crore in FY26, and the export order book is about INR400 crore. Development order book is about INR3,000 crore, roughly 10% of total mix.

segments.name: LCA Mk-1A (97 aircraft contract)
segments.commentary: Inventory for LCA is about INR7,500-8,100 crore including raw material and WIP. Management targets about 20 LCA deliveries in FY27, with the first deliveries expected August-September 2026 as GE engines arrive.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at double-digit, specified as about 10-12% minimum, versus about 7% in FY26.
EBITDA margin guided at around 30-31%, which management says will be maintained with manufacturing mix rising.
About 20 LCA Mk-1A deliveries targeted in FY27 (GE engine supply of around 20 expected), with first delivery August-September 2026; 1 engine expected in June, 2 per month from August.
HTT-40: about 20+ units planned for FY27, Honeywell engines expected from next month; LCH delivery as per contract in FY27-FY28.
Su-30 MKI: 1 aircraft due in FY27 and 11 in FY28-29 per contract.
Expected orders of about INR90,000 crore including ROH over the next 2 years, with 143 ALH and 40 Do-228 upgrades in approval.
Plan to invest about INR12,000 crore by 2030 in new manufacturing infrastructure (LCA Mk-2, GE F414, IMRH engines, SSLV).
capex_capacity: Third LCA Mk-1A production line at Nashik inaugurated 17 October 2025, establishing 8 aircraft per annum capacity; total LCA production lines now 3 (2 Bengaluru, 1 Nashik) with capacity of 24 LCA per year referenced.
HTT-40 now has two lines (Bengaluru and Nashik); ALH augmented in the helicopter division with private vendors helping on structures; ALH output of about 20-25 per year.
Management says none of the lines are idle; 20+ LCA airframes are built with engine ground runs complete, and 97-aircraft order will utilise facilities fully.
Su-30 MKI upgrade is in design phase, with CCS approval expected this fiscal; design to take 5-6 years before production.
Tejas Mk-2 prototype rollout targeted by March 2027 (joint design with ADA); rotary UAV (CATS Warrior) actual build underway with flight expected next year.
AL-31FP target of 32-35 engines per year; RD-33 has 15 engines left, to be delivered in FY27.
demand_pricing: Order book INR2,54,538 crore; FY26 fresh orders INR97,028 crore (manufacturing INR69,668 crore, ROH INR26,539 crore). Major wins: 97 LCA Mk-1A for IAF, 6 ALH Mk III for ICG, 8 Do-228 for ICG, 10 ALH Dhruv NG for Pawan Hans, 2 Hindustan-228 for Guyana.
Major platform order book of about INR2.84 lakh crore across LCA, Su-30, AL-31FP, Do-228, ALH, LCH, HTT-40 and RD-33.
Pipeline: 143 ALH for the Army, Su-30 upgrade, upgrade of 40 Do-228; ALH 137 is the largest contributor. Values not disclosed as contracts are not finalised.

Pricing: ROH is priced on cost-plus under the PPRC mechanism (10-15% margin cited); ERV (exchange rate) clause is in every contract including ROH; material escalation factored into contracts; 97 LCA purchase orders already placed, so no FY27 cost increase expected.

Revenue recognition for manufacturing is on delivery, not percentage of completion, so FY28-29 could be lumpy. Unbilled revenue relates to delivered aircraft awaiting documentation, not to undelivered inventory.

qa_highlights.question: When will the IAF accept the first LCA Mk-1A lot, and what are FY27 revenue and EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CMD said six GE engines received and aircraft flying; remaining tests to be discussed with IAF, targeting stabilisation by August or September. CFO guided double-digit revenue growth and EBITDA margin around 30-31%.

qa_highlights.question: What is holding up LCA delivery and how big is the issue?
qa_highlights.answer: CMD said testing refines already-tested items and is an iterative design and development process; declined to give details, saying HAL is confident of a September deadline.

qa_highlights.question: How many LCA are factored into guidance and how does GE supply ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 20 LCA planned for FY27. GE committed 15-20 more engines; 1 engine in June, 2 per month from August, and 15-20 by year-end. Engines take 30-45 days to convert to delivery.

qa_highlights.question: Will the lumpy LCA revenue and inventory of about INR9,000 crore be realised, and is there any penalty on GE?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory for LCA about INR7,500-8,100 crore. Penalty on GE is a commercial matter under PO terms; management declined to quantify until deliveries occur.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ROH growth slow, and what drives the margin mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Spares fell INR500-600 crore YoY; R&O flat as no new platform added. Manufacturing mix to move from 30:70 towards 50:50, with R&O margin slightly above manufacturing, but management sees no profitability stress.

qa_highlights.question: Provisioning was low in FY26 — what is the steady-state level?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 included INR800 crore provision after a Su-30 accident; no equivalent event in FY26, so management declined to give a provision-to-revenue guidance.

risks_watch: LCA Mk-1A first delivery slipping beyond August-September 2026; testing and software refinements still in progress, and the 20-aircraft FY27 target depends on GE engine receipts (1 in June, 2 per month from August).
Global supply chain slowness at Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors affecting components for Su-30, HTT-40 and LCH; Honeywell engine supply stabilised per management.
Unbilled revenue and inventory build (inventory about INR33,000 crore including ROH; unbilled tied to documentation); revenue recognition on delivery makes FY27 and FY28 lumpy.
Penalty on GE for engine delays not quantified; outcome uncertain.
Manpower constraints and private-sector competition; ALH 143-unit order and Su-30 upgrade contract not yet signed (CCS approval expected this FY).
Uttam radar integration not in 83-LCA batch; planned for 97-LCA batch subject to DRDO clearance.
541154|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY27 guidance and on ALH, HTT-40 and LCH timelines, but noticeably guarded on LCA: the CMD repeatedly declined to detail the technical issues and the penalty amount, and the timeline moved from earlier commitments to August-September.
key_quotes: We are confident that we will be able to meet the September deadline.
So we are expecting around 20.
And that 30% will be maintained.
Yes, the deliveries of ALH, we have no issues. We have delivered everything as per contract.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin guided at 30-31%, held flat from FY26's ~30%, with manufacturing mix rising towards 50:50 and cost-plus ROH pricing with ERV clauses; no FY27 cost increase is expected because 97 LCA purchase orders are already placed.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Third LCA Mk-1A line at Nashik already commissioned (8 aircraft per annum), with HTT-40 now on two lines and about INR12,000 crore planned by 2030, though the new lines are already live rather than a fresh announcement in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: About 20 LCA Mk-1A and 20+ HTT-40 deliveries are planned in FY27, and FY26 manufacturing revenue rose about 16% to INR9,227 crore, though the LCA timing hinges on GE engine supply.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management plans about INR12,000 crore of investment by 2030 for LCA Mk-2, GE F414, IMRH engines and SSLV, and FY26 capex was INR2,386 crore, so further project-level announcements are likely as the plan is detailed. Utilisation was not quantified; management says no line is idle.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance is a 10-12% minimum with about 20 LCA deliveries, which already rests on a delayed LCA start, so management has little room to raise it near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The LCA Mk-1A first delivery has slipped to August-September 2026 and the 20-aircraft FY27 target depends on GE engine receipts (1 in June, 2 per month from August), while the penalty on GE is unquantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Aug-Sep 2026 (LCA Mk-1A); HTT-40 ongoing in FY27; Tejas Mk-2
rows.why: First LCA Mk-1A deliveries are set for August-September 2026, about 20 HTT-40 units are planned in FY27, and the Tejas Mk-2 prototype is targeted by March 2027.

rows.label: Expected orders of INR90,000 crore over next 2 years incl. ROH
rows.why: Order book of INR2,54,538 crore after FY26 fresh orders of INR97,028 crore, with 143 ALH and 40 Do-228 upgrades in approval and Su-30 upgrade awaiting CCS approval this fiscal.

rows.label: Su-30 MKI upgrade CCS approval
rows.why: Upgrade is in design phase with CCS approval expected this fiscal, but production is 5-6 years away, so it adds to order book rather than near-term volume.

rows.label: LCA ROH cycle ramp
rows.why: Spares fell INR500-600 crore YoY and R&O was flat, and LCA ROH is expected only in roughly three years, so ROH growth will not lift the next 2-4 quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 revenue guidance, the 30-31% EBITDA margin and the ALH, HTT-40 and LCH timelines, but guarded on LCA, declining to detail the technical issues or the GE penalty; analysts pressed on the LCA delay, engine supply and the lumpy FY27-28 revenue.

541163|2026-03.headline: Sandhar FY26 consolidated revenue INR 4,852 crore (+25%), EBITDA INR 513 crore (10.6% margin); FY27 guided to grow over 15% before any price re-trigger.
541163|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: consolidated revenue rose 25% to INR 4,852 crore, EBITDA rose 28% to INR 513 crore at a 10.6% margin, and PAT rose 40% to INR 199 crore. Q4 consolidated revenue grew 29% YoY with an 11% EBITDA margin, and the India business grew 28% in FY26. Overseas subsidiaries swung to break-even at EBT in Q4 after a FY26 loss of EUR 2.56 million, though aluminium pass-through lags are expected to weigh on Q1 FY27. Management cited April manpower absenteeism and raw material shortages as the main near-term disruption, with May reported as better than April.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated Q4 revenue and EBITDA margin

financial_highlights.value: Revenue INR 257 crore, EBITDA INR 28.25 crore

financial_highlights.change: Q4 EBITDA margin 14.6%, EBT about break-even
Working capital debt INR 564 crore; term loans INR 384 crore

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 4,384 crore (+28%), EBITDA INR 472 crore (+32%). Management said industry grew 12.7% while Sandhar India grew 28%; two-wheeler business grew 35.1% vs industry 12.9%.

segments.name: Overseas subsidiaries
segments.commentary: FY26 loss of EUR 2.56 million; Q4 EBITDA margin 14.6% and EBT roughly break-even. Revenue of about EUR 46 million with full-year decline of about 8.5% in euro terms, per analyst. Pass-through lag of about 180 days in overseas contracts.

segments.name: Joint ventures
segments.commentary: Five JVs generated revenue of INR 257 crore and EBITDA of INR 28.25 crore in FY26; Sandhar investment about INR 62 crore.

segments.name: EV business
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 20 crore; 41,000 battery chargers and 5,500 motor control units sold. Targeted to double in FY27; EBT turnaround expected in FY28.

segments.name: New projects (Sundaram-Clayton die-casting, Khed City, Sanaswadi cabins/fabrication)
segments.commentary: INR 342 crore invested to generate INR 468 crore revenue in FY26; Sundaram-Clayton FY26 revenue INR 369 crore. Management expects about 2x-2.5x revenue (about INR 750 crore) in FY27. Turnaround timelines: Khed City and Sanaswadi from Q2 FY27, Sundaram-Clayton from Q3 FY27 (still EBT losses for FY27).

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at over 15% (15-16%), excluding a likely price re-trigger on input cost increases.
EBITDA margin expected to improve by about 0.25% in FY27 for existing businesses; new projects will dilute, with 1.5-2 years to profitability.
Management targets doubling revenue every three to four years, with a stated post-tax ROCE target of 15%, peaking at 20%; at INR 10,000 crore revenue, PAT of about INR 450 crore was cited.
FY27 capex estimated at INR 275-310 crore (5-7% of revenue), covering growth, maintenance and upgradation.
Overseas business expected to return to planned levels once aluminium pass-through lag clears; Romania targeted for break-even in FY28.
Manpower availability expected to normalise by end-June 2026 per management, with May better than April.
capex_capacity: Capital work in progress closing balance INR 104-115 crore (figure cited differently on call); mostly expected to capitalise by end of Q2 FY27 as Sundaram-Clayton relocation, Khed City and Sanaswadi projects complete.
Sundaram-Clayton die-casting business shifting to own premises, targeted by end of Q2 FY27.
FY27 capex outlay of INR 275-310 crore expected.

Technology: telematics and smart-key products presented to customers; POCs next, development in FY27, production thereafter. Partnering on royalty-based technology transfer, not JVs; target to take to market within 12 months.
Smart Key locksets at about 5,000 per month and growing.
demand_pricing: Management said domestic auto demand is strong, but manpower constraints limit industry output; absenteeism reached around 20% at one point in April, and state minimum wages rose 30-40%.
Two-wheeler inventory at some customers fell from about 60 days to under 14 days; industry lost an estimated 200,000-300,000 vehicles.

Aluminium and gas costs rose sharply in March-April; India pass-through lag is about three months (aiming for 30 days), and overseas lag about 180 days (aiming for 90 days). Pass-through from June expected to recover April costs.
Price re-trigger expected across the industry as input costs rise; not included in the 15% growth guidance.
Working capital: overseas inventory holding about 54-55 days vs about 12-13 days in India.

qa_highlights.question: How will the planned doubling of revenue every 3-4 years be achieved, and which segments drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited two-wheelers, new businesses in sheet metal and casting, and proprietary products like locks and mirrors; it said a 15-16% growth guide is conservative and excludes the price re-trigger.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the new projects and their profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 342 crore invested generated INR 468 crore in FY26 and is expected to reach about INR 750 crore in FY27; Khed City and Sanaswadi turn around in Q2 FY27, Sundaram-Clayton in Q3 with EBT losses for FY27, EV and Romania in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins improve and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing businesses are targeted to gain about 0.25% in EBITDA margin in FY27; new projects will dilute margins until they mature, with 1.5-2 years to turnaround.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position and debt-to-equity trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt INR 948 crore, of which INR 564 crore is working capital debt; term loans INR 384 crore with about INR 103 crore repayable this year. Management called the debt-to-equity ratio healthy versus peers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did overseas borrowings rise in INR terms despite a small euro increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Bill discounting was reclassified to borrowings under Ind AS, and INR translation at the closing rate (about INR 111 per euro vs INR 108 in March) inflated the INR figure; the euro increase was about EUR 5 million.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company keep the overseas business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the overseas presence supports Indian customer relationships; it will revisit the business after the year but gave no decision.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company's competitive advantage in castings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited integrated capability across high- and low-pressure die casting, machining, zinc, magnesium and aluminium castings, from small to very large parts including engine blocks.

risks_watch: Aluminium and gas cost pass-through lags of three months in India and about 180 days overseas, which will hit Q1 FY27 margins.
Manpower shortages and wage hikes in several states could keep volumes below demand; management expects normalisation by end-June 2026.
New project losses (Sundaram-Clayton, EV, Romania) in FY27 could slow the margin improvement.
Working capital intensity: receivable days at 44 (consolidated) and inventory days at 54-55 for overseas operations; overseas debt in INR rose partly due to reclassification.

rows.why: Volume grew 62% YoY and 7% QoQ with utilisation at 66%, and management expects utilisation to improve in Q3 and Q4 FY27 toward about 80% within two quarters.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 66%, below the 80% threshold, but INR250 crore is already committed and management said further capex to fill Buildings 3 and 4 will be discussed in the January or April call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY28 revenue at more than INR1,600 crore but cut the EBITDA margin wording to 'at least 20-plus%' and gave no upside on margins, while freight and gas costs remain unrecovered on fixed-price contracts to December.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Freight rose from INR10 crore to INR20 crore QoQ, management cannot forecast Nov-Dec freight, and fixed-price contracts run to December, so H2 margins could fall below 20% before pass-through takes effect from Q3 FY27.

rows.label: MNC special contract commercial supply
rows.why: Trial production by Q4 FY27 and commercial supply in Q1 FY28 on a ~INR120-150 crore contract, with INR120 crore already received and ~75% utilisation expected in FY28.

rows.label: Freight and gas pass-through from Q3 FY27
rows.why: Management expects to pass on freight (INR20 crore in Q2) and gas (INR1.8 crore) increases from Q3 FY27, except fixed-price contracts running to December.

rows.label: Debt-to-EBITDA falling

tone.note: Management was confident on volume, demand and the MNC contract, but cautious on margins, declining to commit beyond 20-21% EBITDA or 23-24% for next year; analysts pressed on the 300 bps QoQ margin fall, the freight pass-through and the phasing of Phase 2 utilisation.

541195|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 turnover hit a record INR552.7 crore (+34.63% YoY) and PAT rose 38.49% to INR77.75 crore; FY26 turnover INR1,208.63 crore (+12.52%).
541195|2026-03.overview: Mishra Dhatu Nigam reported its highest-ever quarterly turnover of INR552.7 crore in Q4 FY26, with value of production up 19.15% to INR392.19 crore and PBT up 38.67% to INR107 crore. For FY26, turnover reached INR1,208.63 crore (+12.52%) and PAT INR130.79 crore (+18.82%). Management highlighted record titanium output of about 700 tonnes, an order book of about INR2,290 crore as of April 1, 2026, and new qualifications (NADCAP heat treatment, CEMILAC airworthiness for 10 alloys). Management guided to roughly 15% top-line growth in FY27 with a 20% ambition, and EBITDA margin of 23-25%, conditional on raw material and energy (LPG) supply stabilising.

financial_highlights.change: Management also cited INR85 crore export done in FY26; figures differ in call

segments.name: Defence (PSU/MoD customers, turnover split)
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover from defence about INR301 crore and from PSUs about INR603 crore, per management. Defence is about 79% of the open order book.

segments.name: Space
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about INR93 crore, per management.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about INR2 crore, per management.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about INR129 crore, per management.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 exports about INR85 crore on one figure and INR78 crore on another; management targets at least INR100 crore in FY27.

segments.name: Investment casting
segments.commentary: Current investment cast business about INR10 crore, covering titanium and superalloys.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth of about 15% expected, with a 20% ambition dependent on raw material and energy supply.
EBITDA margin expected at about 23-25% (CFO-level comment cited 24-25%); PAT growth expected around 20%.
Open order book about INR2,250 crore; management expects about INR1,500 crore of new orders booked in FY27.
Metal bank expected to be established in about 4 months, with 3-4 months more needed for material receipt.
Inventory (WIP and scrap) targeted to fall 10-15% from opening levels.
Long-term 5-7 year ambition of INR5,000 crore top line cited, with 15-20% annual growth described as achievable; INR2,000 crore target seen as possibly achievable sooner than 3 years.
MOU targets for next year still under discussion with the Ministry.
capex_capacity: Planned capex of about INR1,000 crore over the next 3 years, mainly downstream forging and bar/wire equipment to replace machines installed around 1980-85; DPRs in progress, Board approval expected in 1-2 months, with more clarity by end FY27.
Funding preference: operating lease and term loans, with balance via working capital.
Metal bank (perpetual, for 6 critical raw materials) under civil works; establishment expected in about 4 months.
New vacuum arc remelting furnace installed; titanium capacity said to exceed the ~700 tonne FY26 output; titanium orders above INR660 crore in hand.
Aerospace fastener facility inaugurated, worth about INR40 crore, operational.
Spring plant for Vande Bharat being set up with an external subcontractor, expected to be fully operational in 1-2 months.
Powder manufacturing facility delayed by licence and dual-use clearance; purchase order placed, facility not yet installed; clarity expected next quarter.
demand_pricing: Open order book INR2,249-2,250 crore, of which defence is about 79%.
Titanium and maraging steel have higher margins than superalloys, per management; alloy-wise gross margins not disclosed.
Titanium orders above INR660 crore currently in hand.
Engine majors auditing facilities; commercial supplies expected towards end FY27 at earliest.
AMCA alloys (superalloys and titanium) under development; production orders expected once development completes.
ABHED bullet-proof jacket: one order of about INR1 crore executed for OCTOPUS; further orders anticipated.
Fixed-price contracts: management says raw material risk is priced into quotes; no price variation clause in fixed-price defence contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 see 20% top-line growth and 23% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 15% top-line growth (20% ambition), subject to raw material and LPG/energy stability. Margins expected at 23-25% EBITDA, with ~20% bottom-line growth.

qa_highlights.question: What order inflow to expect by end FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,500 crore of orders expected to be booked in FY27 against an open order book of about INR2,250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue is from products and by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 split: defence about INR301 crore, PSUs INR603 crore, space INR93 crore, energy INR2 crore, others INR129 crore, exports INR78 crore. Product-wise split not given as orders depend on customers.

qa_highlights.question: Alloy-wise gross margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose margins by alloy, calling it confidential.

qa_highlights.question: What is the metal bank and how is price risk handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Metal bank is a perpetual stock of 6 critical raw materials for customers, drawn only in emergencies; fixed-price contracts carry no price variation and pricing covers uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Fastener plant economics?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR40 crore facility is operational, serving missile and space; management expects at least INR20-30 crore order book per year, and a stable base of at least INR25 crore per year.

risks_watch: Raw material supply: India imports all key high-purity inputs (nickel, cobalt, molybdenum, tungsten, chromium, vanadium, rhenium), mainly from Europe, with titanium sponge from Kazakhstan; supply and sanctions risks persist.
Energy: LPG and energy issues linked to the Middle East and European crises could delay orders.
Fixed-price defence contracts with no price variation clause expose margins to alloy price spikes.
Powder facility licence and dual-use clearance still pending.
Export and engine-major orders depend on long audit cycles (expected towards end FY27).
Management did not give alloy-wise margins or product-wise revenue splits, limiting visibility.
Inventory build-up (WIP and scrap) to be reduced by 10-15%.
MOU targets with the Ministry not yet fixed.

Evasive on alloy-wise margins, product revenue split and specific FY27 order sizes for springs and powder, deferring these to the next call.

we are looking at the niche markets of Aerospace and Defence for manufacture of these very, very complex alloys.

541195|2026-06.headline: MIDHANI Q1 FY27 turnover rose 40.46% to Rs 239.49 crore, but LPG and raw-material costs compressed EBITDA margin to about 20%.
541195|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 turnover was Rs 239.49 crore (up 40.46% YoY) and value of production Rs 260.36 crore (up 7.9%). PBT rose 25.89% to Rs 23.92 crore and PAT rose 27.42% to Rs 16.31 crore. EBITDA was Rs 46.6 crore (up 12.89%), with margin about 20% versus roughly 23% expected, pressured by LPG price spikes and adverse raw-material price variance of about Rs 13-14 crore. Order book stood at about Rs 2,329 crore as of 1 July 2026, now won entirely through competitive bidding.

financial_highlights.value: About Rs 2,329 crore as of 1 July 2026

segments.name: Order book mix
segments.commentary: Defense about 66%, space (ISRO) about 21%, energy about 9%, others about 4%.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Current-year export sales Rs 33 crore to date with open export order book of about Rs 25 crore; target about 10% of turnover (about Rs 100-120 crore).

segments.name: Titanium
segments.commentary: Melted about 750 tonnes last year after new melting facility; titanium orders worth about Rs 600 crore cited. Management says titanium and super alloys carry higher margins than special steel.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 margins expected to be hit somewhat; management expects normalisation from Q3 FY27, with EBITDA margin returning toward 20-21%.
FY27 growth expected to exceed FY26 growth, though management said sustaining Q1's 40% growth through the year is not practicable.
FY27 normal capex about Rs 50-60 crore, mostly maintenance; Rs 1,000 crore modernisation capex over 2-3 years, with returns from year 4 and proposal still awaiting Board and ministry approval.
Metal bank: procurement under way for one customer; further clarity expected by end of Q2 FY27, with implementation targeted next quarter.
Aluminium JV plant at Nellore (with NALCO) being closed; a separate wide-plate rolling of customer-supplied 7000-series aluminium billets has been done as first commercial order.
Export expectation: at least 15-20% increase on the 10% export base over the next 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Rs 1,000 crore modernisation capex proposed for replacing ageing equipment; sent to ministry for evaluation, management declined to give timeline.
Isothermal forging completed in 6,000-tonne press for nickel-based super alloy for fighter aircraft engine; orders for four super alloy grades and three titanium grades to be executed this year.
New titanium melting facility commissioned last year; about 750 tonnes melted last year, with expected growth.
Spring plant in campus started; sample order received from BEML. Preliminary BAFA licence obtained for metal powder equipment, expected on campus by next year.
Bulletproof jacket (ABHED, from DRDO/IIT Delhi) fabricated; testing expected to complete this quarter, with test certificates by next quarter.
demand_pricing: Raw-material prices of nickel, molybdenum, tungsten rose sharply; cobalt also higher. Adverse price variance of about Rs 13 crore (or Rs 14 crore per later remark) in Q1.
LPG price nearly doubled due to Middle East conflict; furnaces are LPG-fired, affecting Q1 and possibly Q2.
Freight cost mostly booked at fixed terms; management said it sometimes absorbs freight increases on fixed-price contracts.
No nomination-based orders now; all orders won through competitive bidding.
Titanium sourced by import from Eastern Europe (former Russian Federation); management reports no import constraints currently.
Scrap usage in melt typically 50-60% for normal aerospace grades; virgin material mandated for human spaceflight and critical engine parts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin compress in Q1 and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Madhubala Kalluri cited raw-material prices and LPG prices, which nearly doubled. She said Q2 may be hit, with normalisation expected in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin return to 20-21% from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: CMD S.V.S. Narayana Murty said yes, and that the Q1 shortfall was due to the raw-material and LPG issues.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 1,000 crore capex yielding EBITDA, and what is FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex takes 2-3 years, with returns from year 4. FY27 capex will be about Rs 50-60 crore, mostly maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the aluminium plant still on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Nellore aluminium JV plant is being closed, pending ministry approval. The separate wide-plate rolling of customer-supplied aluminium billets is an alternative route.

qa_highlights.question: Will the S400 certification generate meaningful revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is testing-only revenue, conservatively estimated at about 10% of export base, with clarity in a couple of quarters.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin recovery to 20-21% in Q3 depends on LPG and raw-material prices easing; Q2 margin likely lower.
Fixed-price defence contracts leave the company exposed to raw-material and freight cost increases.
Rs 1,000 crore modernisation capex is not yet Board- or ministry-approved; no timeline given.
Metal bank benefits are customer-owned and not on company balance sheet; implementation and utilisation are still to be confirmed.
Scrap inventory policy and sales of titanium scrap; management says scrap is a strategic asset rather than surplus.

Management repeatedly attributed Q1 margin pressure to temporary LPG and raw-material factors and declined to quantify the Rs 1,000 crore capex return or the S400 revenue.

Only because of these little raw material and LPG issues only that was little lower bottom line.
So, we reduced our scrap inventory by Rs. 75 crores.
We are not going ahead with that plant.

541233|2026-03.headline: FY26 was Lemon Tree's best year: revenue Rs 1,452.7 crore (+13%), PAT Rs 288.3 crore (+19%), with margin down 126 bps to 48.1%.
541233|2026-03.overview: Lemon Tree reported record FY26 and Q4 FY26 on occupancy, ARR, revenue, EBITDA, PBT, PAT and cash profit, with Q4 revenue of Rs 419.5 crore (+11%) and PAT of Rs 116.5 crore (+8%). Net EBITDA margin fell to 48.1% for FY26 and 52% for Q4, which management attributes to renovation spend, technology investment and the GST change. Management guided that these three cost heads fall to about 3.7% of revenue by FY28, and set out a proposed demerger that would leave Lemon Tree as an asset-light entity and Fleur Hotels as an owner/lessor platform. Q4 demand softened in March and April from the Middle East conflict and airline disruption, with corporate travel weaker and occupancy hitting what management called a ceiling.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever for a full financial year
from Rs 1,699 crore a year ago

segments.name: Lemon Tree (asset-light, managed and franchised)
segments.commentary: Opened 20 managed/franchised hotels (1,523 rooms) and signed 55 (4,912 rooms) in FY26; total pipeline 22,581 rooms across 268 hotels, of which 131 hotels and 11,811 rooms are operational. Keys RevPAR grew 20% and Aurika 19% for FY25 to FY26 on management's figures.

segments.name: Fleur Hotels (owned/leased)
segments.commentary: Post-scheme, Fleur to have 5,600 rooms across 39 operational hotels; 4 hotels with 875 rooms in confirmed pipeline, including 572 rooms at Nehru Place (estimated capex Rs 700 crore). Fees Rs 95.8 crore, +8% on a same-store basis.

segments.name: Aurika brand
segments.commentary: Highest ARR and margin product; Aurika occupancy rose from 62% to 74% for FY26 with RevPAR +19%, though Q4 occupancy fell 2% as a large Mumbai wet-lease ended. Aurika has only two hotels (Mumbai and Udaipur).

guidance_outlook: Cost heads (GST impact, technology, renovation) expected to fall from 5.8% of revenue in FY26 to about 4.8% in FY27 and 3.7% in FY28 onward, adding roughly 1% of revenue a year, plus Rs 25-30 crore of one-off costs (Delhi property tax ex gratia, labour code) that drop out from FY27.
FY27 renovation spend about 1.9% of revenue, normal renovation thereafter at about 1.3% (possibly 1.0-1.2%); GST impact rising from 1% to 2% of revenue in FY27 as it becomes a full year.
Expected openings of about 2,000 rooms in FY27, rising to about 3,000 in FY28 and 4,000 in FY29; management says openings lag signings by about three years, with signings of about 5,000 rooms a year.

Lemon Tree standalone post-demerger: steady-state flow-through on management fees of 75-80%, currently about 60% pro forma; steady-state PAT about 60% of revenue (per management, after tax and no interest or depreciation).

Fleur targets up to Rs 3,000 crore of deployable capital over 12-18 months (including Warburg primary investment), and plans to add about 2,500 rooms; management does not give fee guidance for FY27-28.
Demerger: CCI approval received in April; SEBI and shareholder/creditor approvals underway; NCLT timing 6-18 months, with management giving 12-18 months as the outer limit.
Debt-to-EBITDA about 2.25x now; consolidated debt may rise to Rs 2,500-3,000 crore if Rs 1,500 crore is deployed, temporarily.
capex_capacity: Renovation: about 5,000 rooms to be renovated, of which 4,000 heavy renovation with about 85% complete; about 400-500 rooms under renovation in Q4 and similar in Q1.
Keys Whitefield renovation expected to complete in about 4 months; Keys Hosur Road under renovation; Keys Pimpri, Pune completed.
Aurika Naldehra, Shimla: 2 of 3 blocks to open by Q2 FY27 for the summer season.
Aurika Varanasi: 47-room heritage licence signed January 2026 on the ghat by the Ganges.

Nehru Place (572 rooms, North India's largest hotel) awaiting final approval before construction; estimated Rs 700 crore; Andaz (525 rooms) nearby, with cash flow over 3.5 years, 60% in the last 18 months.
Acquisition valuations cited at 8x-16x EBITDA; greenfield build 3-4 years, renovation-led acquisitions 1-2 years, operating assets immediate.
demand_pricing: Mid-March decision to prioritise occupancy over rate; April-May tactical pricing to keep an occupancy premium, with ARR roughly flat YoY; Q4 occupancy reached what management called a ceiling.

Corporate travel slowed in March as companies cut travel due to fares and the war; corporate share of occupancy fell to 55% from 59% in Q4 (negotiated room nights 55.4% for the full year vs 56.1%). Retail filled the gap at lower rates.
Indigo shutdown in December and the Middle East war (from early March, continuing into April) cited as headwinds; May described as surprisingly good.
Mumbai micro-market saw about 2,000 keys added in the last year (from Accor Fairmont to Ginger), creating a temporary supply glut for Aurika Mumbai.
Target: 65% of business from retail (direct, B2C, loyalty) once the portfolio reaches 20,000-25,000 operating rooms.
Loyalty programme has about 24 lakh members, driving about 25% of room nights per management.
Indian mid-market: management says demand outpaces supply; cites 2.5 million unbranded rooms in India as a conversion opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Would Fleur's inventory be managed by a non-Lemon Tree operator post-demerger, and how would that work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Fleur is brand-agnostic and would choose whichever brand makes economic sense, while Lemon Tree should not be discriminated against; it cited a lost 5-star NCLT bid as an example.

qa_highlights.question: Why Aurika RevPAR growth (3%) lags Keys (16%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to micro-market differences and timing; full-year FY26 RevPAR growth was 19% for Aurika and 20% for Keys, with Keys set to keep growing as renovations finish.

qa_highlights.question: How confident are you on conversion of signings into openings, and what fee numbers for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Openings lag signings by about three years; management declined to give fee guidance but expects about 2,000 rooms opened in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-saving path and steady-state margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Renovation, GST and technology costs to fall to about 3.7% of revenue by FY28; pro forma Lemon Tree flow-through is about 60% now, targeted at 70%+ and then 75-80%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised demerger timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: CCI approval came in April; SEBI/shareholder/creditor steps underway; NCLT is the main variable, with 12-18 months the outer limit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did incentive-linked management fees lag for third-party hotels versus Fleur?
qa_highlights.answer: Incentive fees (1-5% of revenue depending on GOP slab) fell as renovation and GST cut owned-hotel EBITDA margins; third-party fees rose 23% from net additions, Fleur fees rose 8% on a same-store basis.

qa_highlights.question: What peak debt level is comfortable after Fleur's deployment?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-to-EBITDA about 2.25x now; consolidated debt could rise to Rs 2,500-3,000 crore temporarily if Rs 1,500 crore is deployed.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation for standalone Lemon Tree post-demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Lemon Tree to be debt-free and cash-generative; Board to decide a dividend or buyback policy; no F&B expansion planned, with a high hurdle for acquisitions.

risks_watch: NCLT timing for the Fleur demerger: management guides 6-18 months, with 12-18 months as the outer limit; CCI approval received in April, SEBI, shareholder and creditor steps still pending.

Demand softness: corporate share of occupancy fell to 55% in Q4 from 59%; March and April were weak on the Middle East conflict and airline disruption, though management said May was surprisingly good.

Margin recovery depends on renovation spend falling to about 1.9% of revenue in FY27 and GST impact and technology costs easing; standalone flow-through is about 60% pro forma versus a 70%+ steady-state target.
Openings execution: about 2,000 rooms targeted in FY27 versus 1,523 rooms opened in FY26; openings lag signings by about three years and owner-finance delays could cause slippage.

Leverage post-deployment: consolidated debt could rise to Rs 2,500-3,000 crore from about Rs 1,500 crore if Rs 1,500 crore is deployed, versus debt-to-EBITDA of about 2.25x now; Fleur's 2,500-room pipeline is not yet firm.
Aurika weakness: Q4 occupancy fell 2% after a large Mumbai wet-lease ended and Mumbai micro-market supply rose by about 2,000 keys; Keys RevPAR growth depends on completing renovations.
key_quotes: FY26 was the best year in Lemon Tree's history across Occupancy, ARR, Revenue, EBITDA, PBT, PAT, Cash Profit and Q4 FY26 was the best ever fourth quarter on the same parameters.
I want to take this opportunity to continue the conversation on the demerger scheme.
I do not want to give guidance, but I can give you a direction.
Corporate travel is the first that kind of dries up when war happens because it is under the control normally of the CEO or an equivalent CXO and it is a one -person decision.
Lemon Tree will not need any significant capital other than potentially investments in technology or in marketing and so on.
541233|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the full-year record, the long-term margin path and the demerger, but cautious and evasive on near-term demand, the war's duration, and specific guidance; management repeatedly declined to give fee or revenue numbers for FY27-28 and to predict the NCLT timeline. Tone on the Q4 softness was defensive, attributing weakness to Indigo, the war and Mumbai supply.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.why: Management guides about 2,000 gross room openings in FY27 versus 1,523 rooms opened in FY26, with about 5,000 rooms signed a year, though openings lag signings by about three years and owner-finance delays could cause slippage.

rows.why: Q4 FY26 occupancy was 78.5% and FY26 occupancy 73.5%, but corporate share fell to 55% from 59% and March-April were weak on the Middle East conflict and airline disruption; management called occupancy a ceiling and gave no FY27 revenue growth number.

rows.why: Fleur targets up to Rs 3,000 crore of deployable capital over 12-18 months to add about 2,500 rooms, and Nehru Place (572 rooms, about Rs 700 crore) awaits final approval before construction; debt-to-EBITDA is about 2.25x now.

rows.label: Fleur demerger and asset-light Lemon Tree

541233|2026-06.headline: Lemon Tree Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to Rs 346.8 crore, but net EBITDA margin fell 99 bps to 43.8% on GST and SAR provision.
541233|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 9% YoY to Rs 346.8 crore and PAT rose 19% to Rs 57.3 crore, while occupancy rose 314 bps to 75.7% as the company shifted to a volume-led retail strategy. Gross ARR rose only 2% to Rs 6,361 because retail business carries lower net ARR after commissions, and management called Q1 an aberration driven by West Asia-related corporate travel softness. Margin compression came from a GST input-credit loss and stock appreciation rights provision, worth 3.1% of revenue combined. Management expects Q2 to be better, with July described as strong and August as solid. The call also covered the planned demerger of Fleur Hotels and Warburg's Rs 960 crore investment in Fleur.

segments.name: Owned hotels (Lemon Tree)
segments.commentary: Contributed Rs 320 crore of network revenue, 56% of network revenue. Net EBITDA margin hit by GST input-credit loss and renovation spend of about Rs 9.8 crore (2.25-2.3% of revenue).

segments.name: Managed and franchised (asset-light)
segments.commentary: Contributed Rs 256 crore of network revenue. Opened 6 hotels with 334 rooms and signed 13 hotels with 1,020 rooms in Q1. Same-store managed revenue grew 9-10%.

segments.name: Keys portfolio (Fleur)
segments.commentary: RevPAR up 19% YoY to Rs 2,885, with occupancy up 350 bps to 67% and ARR up 13% to Rs 4,311. Renovation is about two-thirds complete across 7 hotels.

segments.name: Fleur Hotels (pro forma)
segments.commentary: FY27 revenue Rs 311.4 crore (+7%), net EBITDA ex-GST Rs 125.1 crore (+10%, margin 40.2%), PAT Rs 34.7 crore (+23%).

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 net EBITDA margin to be better than the ~47% analyst estimate, and sees a path to at least 50% in FY28 as renovation spend drops and ARR improves.
Management targets a long-term Lemon Tree EBITDA margin of 75-80% as fee income doubles and corporate costs fall as a share of revenue.
Management targets Keys EBITDA of Rs 60 crore on revenue of Rs 115-120 crore, implying Rs 6.5 lakh per key EBITDA.
Target of about 2,000 rooms opened in FY27; management says it is broadly confident, with Q1 at 334 rooms.
Renovation spend is expected to fall to about 1% of revenue from FY28. GST impact is about 2% of net revenue and expected to decline gradually.
Demerger of Fleur expected to complete in H1 CY2027, with Fleur listing in late second half of calendar 2027 after SEBI, shareholder, creditor and GST approvals.
Fleur's long-term plan is to keep debt-to-EBITDA around 2x; Fleur targets roughly 15% ROCE after renovations are complete.
capex_capacity: Aurika Shimla (owned, 90 rooms): about Rs 108 crore deployed as of 30 June 2026; opening shortly as finishing and licences are in final stage.
Aurika Shillong (leased, 165 rooms): about Rs 33 crore deployed; opening expected H2 FY28.
Aurika Varanasi (leased heritage, 47 rooms): work begun; opening expected FY29.
Aurika Nehru Place Delhi: approvals pending; opening on or after FY30; DDA letter of award validity extended by one year.
Renovation: 300 rooms renovated in Q1 at about Rs 10 crore; similar number expected in Q2. Management expects 600-700 rooms in H1 and refurbishments of about 800 rooms in H2.

Fleur plans capital deployment of about Rs 2,500-3,000 crore, funded by Warburg's Rs 960 crore and about Rs 200-300 crore of balance-sheet cash. Management targets about 2,500 rooms of operating and under-development acquisitions.
Asset-light pipeline: 23,381 rooms across 279 hotels, of which 11,946 rooms across 135 hotels are operational.
demand_pricing: Q1 ARR growth was driven by a retail-led volume strategy, which lowered net ARR after commissions. Management calls this temporary and says the mix is returning to balance in July and August.

Corporate demand softened in high-density CBD markets such as Mumbai, Hyderabad and Bengaluru during the West Asia conflict, with lower travel, hiring and relocations. Delhi, Bengaluru and Hyderabad still outperformed; Mumbai and Gurgaon did not.
Mumbai airport micro-market absorbed about 2,000 new rooms over the last two years, creating a temporary supply mismatch. Aurika Mumbai pricing is being reset, with the stated aim of higher ARR.
Around 52% of company room sales are below Rs 7,500 (the GST threshold) and 48% above. Management is repricing demand-dense hotels to reduce GST drag.
OTA share of business is in the mid-30s%, and direct channels rose in Q1 with the retail push. Management expects a better negotiated versus non-negotiated mix from Q2.
Management says July was strong and August solid; Q2 demand is significantly better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is Keys' 19% RevPAR growth in line with the pre-renovation plan, and what remains to be spent on Keys renovation?
qa_highlights.answer: Keys is close to the Red Fox ARR target of about Rs 4,500 and is still a work in progress; management expects full performance next year with occupancy near Lemon Tree averages and reiterated a Rs 60 crore Keys EBITDA target. Remaining spend on about 300 rooms is about Rs 13-14 crore, at roughly Rs 4-5 lakh per key for second-tier Keys hotels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ARR grow only 2% despite Keys growth, and is the lower-ARR strategy continuing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the retail push to fill rooms during the West Asia-driven corporate slowdown lowered net ARR after commissions. It called this temporary, with a more balanced occupancy-ARR mix from July and August, and said Q1 was an aberration.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fleur's Rs 2,500-3,000 crore deployment and Warburg's Rs 960 crore be done at peak-cycle prices, and what are the IRR expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no hurry to deploy and that it is not in an up cycle, since India occupancy is in the mid-60s versus a 70-72% up-cycle threshold. It will focus on demand-dense top 6-7 cities, nearby 3-5 hour international markets and leisure locations, using brownfield, operating assets at 6-8x, greenfield and long leases, with returns targeted at about 60% post-fees ROCE and a conservative downturn assumption.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 and FY28 net EBITDA margins recover, given the 47% analyst estimate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 will be well above 47%. It targets at least 50% in FY28 as renovation spend drops to about 1% of revenue and GST drag falls from about 2% of net revenue, with ARR rising 5-6% in Q2 and further in winter.

qa_highlights.question: Is Mumbai guidance being cut, and will Aurika Mumbai reach double-digit RevPAR growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was an aberration and that Q2 will be better, citing about 2,000 new rooms near the Mumbai airport. It said RevPAR is stabilised and the focus is now on repricing Aurika ARR, and declined to give a numerical RevPAR target before Q2 results.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 2,000-room opening target for FY27 slip, given 334 rooms opened in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said slippage is normal in the business but it is broadly confident of about 2,000 rooms, based on the current pipeline and owner relationships.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net room additions lag the 334 rooms opened in Q1, and what was the management fee compounding outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tarudhan Valley (70 rooms) was terminated and Nestor (130 rooms, no fees) was removed, so fee-earning additions were lower. It said about 1,300 rooms were added year-on-year and that about 5,000 managed rooms signed in FY26 are due to open by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the renovation timeline, and how much margin was lost to renovation versus GST and SAR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 renovation spend was Rs 9.8 crore (about 2.25-2.3% of revenue) versus a normal Rs 3 crore, and that about 300 rooms were done in Q1 with a similar number in Q2. It said refurbishments of about 800 rooms are planned in H2 and that the renovation drag disappears in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fleur's acquisition push raise debt above 2x EBITDA, and how will the debt be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt may briefly exceed 2x EBITDA during construction, with a long-term target near 2x. Fleur debt is about Rs 1,100-1,200 crore; group debt is about Rs 1,275 crore after excluding about Rs 200 crore of cash. Warburg's Rs 960 crore will be deployed before listing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demerger timeline and status?
qa_highlights.answer: Kapil Sharma said CCI approval is done and SEBI and exchange scrutiny is in progress, followed by NCLT filing and hearings. Completion is targeted in H1 CY2027, with Fleur listing in the late second half of calendar 2027 as the conservative assumption.

risks_watch: Q2 delivery versus management's claim that July was strong and August solid; the Q2 ARR recovery of 5-6% and the balance of negotiated versus non-negotiated business are unverified until the next print.
GST input-credit loss persists at about 2% of net revenue; the pace of pricing above Rs 7,500 (52% of room sales currently below) determines whether the drag falls as guided.
Mumbai and Gurgaon corporate demand softness and the roughly 2,000-room Mumbai airport supply overhang; Aurika Mumbai repricing may not translate into RevPAR growth.
Execution risk on the ~2,000-room FY27 opening target (334 opened in Q1) and on managed-hotel friction, including terminations that reduce net room additions.
Fleur capital deployment of Rs 2,500-3,000 crore and the debt-to-EBITDA path, plus demerger approvals (SEBI, shareholders, creditors, GST, NCLT) that could delay the H1 CY2027 completion.
Renovation spend and margin recovery depend on the H2 refurb schedule (about 800 rooms) and on FY28 margin of at least 50%, which management itself called a stretch if not achieved.

And there is no reason why our EBITDA margins net should be less than 50%.
We are not in an up cycle. We are not in an up cycle.

It was guarded on giving numbers for Mumbai RevPAR and on capex, and it deferred several detailed questions to follow-up calls.

541301|2026-03.headline: Orient Electric Q4 FY26 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR948 crores and EBITDA margin improved to 8.2%, though gross margin fell to 31% on commodity inflation.
541301|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR948 crores, up 10% YoY, with Lighting and Switchgear up 16% and ECD up 7.6%. EBITDA rose 15.8% to INR77 crores (8.2% margin) and PAT rose 28.9% to INR40 crores, despite gross margin compressing to 31% from commodity inflation, labour shortage and West Asia gas disruption. For FY26, revenue grew 7.5% to INR3,326 crores, EBITDA rose 12.4% to INR229 crores (about 6.9% margin), and PBT before exceptional items rose 24.2% to about INR139 crores. Calibrated price increases of about 4% in Q4 and roughly 6% in April were taken, and management said these do not fully offset cost inflation.

financial_highlights.change: Hit by commodity inflation; about 100-150 bps impact from March price-action lag

segments.name: Lighting and Switchgear
segments.commentary: Revenue up 16% YoY on distribution expansion and premiumisation; consumer lighting grew double digits. High-value luminaires rose to 68% of mix from 63%; professional luminaires were flat. Wires roughly doubled, and switches and switchgear grew high double digits.

segments.name: ECD (Electrical Consumer Durables)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 7.6% YoY despite industry softness. Fans grew high single digit; BLDC grew over 50% and is 25% of domestic ceiling fan revenue. Premium mix is about 35% of domestic fan revenue, up from 30% last quarter.

segments.name: Appliances and e-commerce
segments.commentary: Appliances (heating, garment care) grew high double digits and e-commerce grew high double digits; quick commerce is 10% of digital channel. Exports grew double digits, with TPW a significant part.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 demand to improve, supported by a forecast of a hotter, more prolonged summer and a possible late-season surge in fans and cooling.
Further calibrated price increases are possible if commodity inflation continues; the company says cost recovery is a priority but competitiveness must be preserved.
Management remains committed to reaching double-digit EBITDA margins structurally once commodity inflation and supply disruptions subside; no specific timeline was given.
Gross margin guidance of 32-34% is unchanged, with Q4 running about 100-150 bps below it.
No FY27 numerical guidance was given; no share buyback is planned at present.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad plant utilisation is improving; TPW production is split between Kolkata and Hyderabad, and the plant is a hub for southern and export supply.
Hyderabad capex has been completed, per an analyst question; management did not add detail.
New products include Aero O2 (oxygen-enriching fan, about INR16,000), Aerosilent (under 50 dB, about INR8,000) and an inverter battery backup fan (about 6 hours of backup).
demand_pricing: Price increases: about 2.5-3% in January, 1-1.5% in March, and about 6% in April; fans, lighting and switchgear each about 6%, and wires increased roughly every 2-3 weeks.
Management says the incremental cost impact was slightly lower than the industry because part of its portfolio needed little spec change.
Market share gained about 30-40 bps per third-party data, described as broad-based across channels and markets, not limited to BLDC.
Channel inventory was elevated, and dealers were cautious on replenishment; Q4 channel build was described as normal.
Consumer offtake is about 45% in March-June and 55% in the balance of the year; premium and BLDC demand is more linear.
Cost pressure: labour shortage, commercial LPG unavailability, and minimum wage hikes of 35% in Haryana and 24% in UP.

qa_highlights.question: How much more price hike is needed to pass on the full incremental cost, and where are the fan market share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the price action was staggered (about 4% in Q4, about 6% in April) and the incremental impact was lower than the industry. Market share gains of 30-40 bps were broad-based across channels, not confined to BLDC.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital days rise to over 30 from 23?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to higher inventory built to hedge supply disruptions and higher payables.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the double-digit EBITDA margin target slipped, and when will it be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 100-150 bps gross margin hit from the lag in price action in March. It remains committed to double-digit margins once commodity inflation and supply disruptions ease, with no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Why has gross margin not improved despite a higher premium mix and price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases do not fully offset commodity inflation, and labour productivity, LPG costs and wage hikes add further cost pressure. Premiumisation has helped EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is 2026 a year of protecting margins, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 FY26 was a washout and H2 exited with better EBITDA margins. It gave no numerical FY27 guidance and said challenges remain.

qa_highlights.question: Is pricing now a structural tailwind toward INR3,000 crore revenue and INR100 crore profit over FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see this as pricing power, calling it a catch-22 industry situation. It pointed to consumer-led product value as the real pricing power and said the aim is INR5,000 crore revenue with double-digit EBITDA.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation, the West Asia conflict, and gas and LPG supply disruption could keep gross margin below the 32-34% guidance band.
Elevated channel inventory and cautious dealer replenishment could weigh on Q1 FY27 primary sales.
Demand depends on a hot, prolonged summer; Q1 weather has been mixed.
Working capital days rose to over 30 from 23 on inventory build and payables; watch the unwind.
Price increases may face elasticity limits; management says competitiveness is being preserved.
Hyderabad plant utilisation and cost absorption; the plant is still a fixed-cost drag.

I don't see it as a pricing power. I think it's a catch-22 situation that the industry has got into and I'm largely reflecting from an industry perspective right now.
Given the commodity inflation to subside and supply disruptions to go away, from a structural perspective, we are trending towards a double-digit margin.

541301|2026-06.headline: Orient Electric Q1 FY27 revenue grew 23.5% YoY with PAT up 79.7% to INR31.5 crores, though gross margin fell to 29.8% on commodity inflation.
541301|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 saw a strong summer-led demand recovery from mid-April, with revenue up 23.5% YoY and ECD revenue up 22.7% to INR669 crores. Gross margin moderated to 29.8% under commodity and labour cost pressure, but EBITDA margin rose 102 bps YoY to 7% as fixed-cost discipline and Project Sanchay savings (INR10 crores) offset the pressure. Management took multiple calibrated price increases across categories, with fans cited at around 15-16% cumulative since December. Management declined to give margin guidance, reiterating only an aspiration of 32-34% gross margin and continued path to double-digit EBITDA margin.

segments.name: ECD (Fans, Appliances)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR669 crores, up 22.7% YoY, with high double-digit fan growth and double-digit appliance growth. BLDC grew 36% YoY and new products were 30% of fan revenue; premium mix reached 36% of domestic fan revenue.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Consumer (B2C) lighting grew high double digits; B2B/C-Loom grew high single digits, with tender business deliberately reduced. Lighting margin declined 40 bps YoY due to a 2-3 week lag in passing on commodity costs. High-value looms share rose to 60%, up 500 bps.

segments.name: Switchgear and Switches
segments.commentary: Both grew at double-digit rates. Management is launching a higher-value MCB subcategory in Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Wires
segments.commentary: Grew more than 200% YoY from a small base. Currently house wires only, sold mainly in North and East markets, with cross-sell through the fan dealer network (about 45% of large fan dealers also sell wires).

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Grew double digits, led by Africa and SAARC; Middle East was impacted. Hyderabad plant certifications completed over the last 2-3 quarters.

guidance_outlook: Management aspires to a 32-34% gross margin, but declined to guide given volatile inflation.
Management is committed to a path to double-digit EBITDA margin; timing depends on inflation. EBITDA margin trend: 5.3% (3 years ago), 6.6%, 6.9%, 8.2% in Q4, 7% in Q1 FY27.
Further Sanchay accruals expected in Q2 FY27 after INR10 crores in Q1.
Long-term aim of a healthy double-digit revenue CAGR; first milestone of INR5,000 crores revenue, with a prior 14-15% CAGR framework.
Marketing spend held at 4.4-4.5% of revenue (5.5% last year on the old basis, per management's comparison).
Management expects employee cost to stay range-bound as a percentage of sales, with automation helping over the long term but not in Q2.
capex_capacity: Ongoing automation of plants and processes to reduce labour cost dependence; benefits expected over the long term rather than in Q2.
Hyderabad plant is a core export base; international certifications completed.
Continued capex on new products, maintenance and capacity enhancement, described as spent as required rather than cut.
New product launches: Aero O2 (oxygen-enriching ceiling fan), Aerosilent (under 50 dB), Ecotech Volt; 3 Red Dot Design awards won.
demand_pricing: Demand: cooling net demand revived from mid-April and stayed robust through May, moderating toward quarter end. Management said Q1 was a balanced sell-in and sell-out quarter with no inventory build-up.

Pricing: fans had 6 price increases from December to June, cumulatively about 15-16%, with about 10% sequential QoQ in fans. Appliances had about 4 increases (high single to double digit). Lighting rose about 10% over 5-6 months. Switchgear rose high double digit. Wires are priced with a 15-day lag to LME.
Competition: management said most leading brands did not take a June price increase, while start-up brands took about half of Orient's increase. Orient says it has priced slightly ahead of peers.
DTM network added about 3,600 retailers in the quarter. E-commerce grew double digits.
Management said Chinese TPW fans are more price-competitive than Indian products; Europe entry is targeted before the next season.

qa_highlights.question: How much of ECD growth came from price increases, and how much more pricing is needed to offset raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was volume plus value across categories, with fans taking about 6 increases from December to June (about 10% sequential in Q1). It said further price action will be calibrated to commodity moves.

qa_highlights.question: Is there trade inventory build-up in Q1, and how do DTM and non-DTM markets compare?

541301|2026-09.headline: Orient Electric Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25.2% YoY to INR879 crores and PAT more than doubled to INR27 crores, but gross margin fell to 29% on inflation.

Management said gross margin should recover only as inflation slows, and it held a long-run gross margin guidance of about 32% and a double-digit EBITDA margin aspiration.
