Expenses (employee, other) said to be at a fixed run-rate after Q1 one-offs; employee cost run-rate around INR 19 crore per quarter cited by analyst and not disputed.
Capex largely complete; INR 15-20 crore remaining to upgrade enzyme and Nutra plants, projects starting in Q2 FY27.
Debtor days target cut from about 100 to about 80; cost of borrowing said to be below 10%.
capex_capacity: EU-GMP reinspection by German and Portuguese authorities in May 2026 is complete; final report awaited, CAPA ready to submit on receipt.
Australia TGA audit in April 2026; final report received, CAPA submitted and under assessor review; certificate expected in coming months.
Remaining capex of INR 15-20 crore for enzyme plant and Nutra plant upgrades, projects starting in Q2.
Some API inventory being built ahead of approvals for products with scarce API; otherwise just-in-time production.
An alternate site is manufacturing a couple of products as risk mitigation; batches under stability, supplies once stability completes. Management said in-house manufacturing remains primary.
demand_pricing: First supplies to Australia expected in the next two to three months for one product; Australian market for that product about USD 20 million with few players.
Management expects supplies to Europe in Q4 FY27 if the EU-GMP certificate arrives in August, with about two quarters' lag to revenue.
Management said an impact from Middle East disruption was seen in Q1 but was stabilising.
Management said it had 2-3 OTF players in India and few in Europe; holds EU approvals for sildenafil and rizatriptan OTF products.
Neuraxpharm (buprenorphine) partner plans UK launch once EU-GMP is restored.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q1 expenses (other expenses ~INR 33-34 crore a quarter, higher employee cost) a new normal or one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one-time items (TGA audit, MIDC charges, repair and maintenance, about INR 1.8-1.9 crore) will not recur and the expense run-rate is now fixed, with a few hires still pending.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gross margin of 58.1% higher than the usual 55-56%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product mix drove the Q1 level and the normal range is 55-58%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EU-GMP status, and are there major observations?
qa_highlights.answer: The draft report has no critical observations, but there are some major and minor ones. Management said the CAPA alone should be enough for recertification, with no reinspection.

qa_highlights.question: How quickly will sales follow EU-GMP approval, and what growth is expected in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about two quarters of lag, with supplies starting in Q4, and 30-35% FY28 growth with EU-GMP. Growth without EU is 10-15%. About 60-70% of growth is attributed to EU.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 8-10 EU MAs need refiling if EU-GMP is delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: No refiling is needed unless the delay goes beyond three to four months. The MA depends on a valid EU-GMP certificate, and the 210-day procedure is near its end.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be double digit at about INR 500 crore revenue, and what are the non-EU economics?
qa_highlights.answer: At INR 410-420 crore margins stay near last year's level. At INR 450-460 crore management said margins would be mid-teens or 13-14%. Q2 results will show whether FY27 overshoots INR 420 crore.

risks_watch: Timing of the EU-GMP final report and CAPA acceptance; management said it could take two to three months after the report for approval, and any delay beyond three to four months may require MA refiling.
Q1 EBITDA margin of 3.7% and PAT loss; investors questioned low ROE (below 5% historically) against a cost of capital around 10%.
Debt of INR 145.2 crore with high debtor days (about 100), and a target to reduce them to about 80.
Dependence on NIP/OTF revenue ramp and on 8-10 EU approvals; partner launches (UK star product, Neuraxpharm) depend on EU-GMP.
Middle East disruption; management said there was an impact in Q1 that appeared to be stabilising.
541400|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the EU-GMP outcome and FY28 growth, but cautious and sometimes evasive on near-term margins and revenue, which management tied to Q2 results. Several answers were vague on numbers, such as the FY28 INR 500 crore question, which was not confirmed.
key_quotes: So, we believe that if without EU, if we look at INR 410-420 number, we would have EBITDA margin similar to last year because of the increased costs.
It's about timing now. So, hopefully, that will come soon enough, and then we can start getting the revenues from EU.
There are no adverse observations. There is no critical observations, which is what is important.
Obviously, if it goes beyond three to four months, it'll have to be redone.

541402|2026-03.headline: FY26 standalone EBITDA margin rose to 14.45% from 8.96% on 4% lower revenue; consolidated PAT turned to ₹6.97 Cr profit from a ₹11.65 Cr loss.
541402|2026-03.overview: FY26 was framed as a transformation year: management chose selective, higher-margin projects over volume, and standalone total income fell to ₹11,093 lakh from ₹16,069 lakh. Consolidated EBITDA swung to ₹1,716 lakh (14.19% margin) from a loss of ₹233 lakh, helped by about ₹151 lakh of GST provision reversal and ₹130 lakh of ODI loan interest in other income. Humro (ARAPL RaaS, 83% subsidiary) secured a ₹48 Cr strategic investment, which will dilute ARAPL's holding below 50% once allotment completes. Management stopped giving numerical guidance, citing only a directional aim to beat FY26 "much much better".

segments.name: Automation (ARAPL, domestic)
segments.commentary: Welding lines for automotive OEMs such as Honda, Magna, Tata, Mahindra and Suzuki. Order book ₹4,496 lakh at 31 May 2026 (opening ₹2,696 lakh plus ₹1,800 lakh new bookings, per the presentation). Management said the verticals' combined book is about ₹127 Cr.

segments.name: Car parking (ARAPL)
segments.commentary: Multilevel parking, with customers including Lodha. Order book ₹820 lakh at 31 May 2026 (opening ₹580 lakh, new ₹155 lakh per the slide). Management plans to start exporting parking products in 6-9 months and to scale domestically.

segments.name: Warehouse automation (Humro / ARAPL RaaS, 83% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Mobile robots and WES for Fortune 50 customers; about 15 units and roughly $25,000 per month of revenue since December 2025. Order book ~$3 Mn (30-35 units, lease model, ₹36 Cr); outright-sale pipeline ~₹60 Cr. Target 225 robots in FY27, which management has not revised.

guidance_outlook: No numerical revenue or margin guidance; management said it has stopped giving number guidance and expects FY27 to be 'much much better' than FY26.
Humro FY27 target of 225 robots maintained; management said demand is 'much more' than supply.
Humro margin target of 15-18% on RaaS and outright sales, described as a moving target. Management said year-one EBITDA is not the focus; the aim is 15-20 good customers.
Next-quarter timing: Q1 is seasonally weak and profitability is expected from Q2 onward.
Humro pricing aim to cut prices by 50% over the next two years, with product-level price deflation.
ARAPL's first new product (exportable) targeted for mechanical completion in June/July 2026 and readiness by November/December 2026; radical growth expected in FY28.
capex_capacity: Five plants covering 350,000 sq ft; around 300 permanent staff and 100 contract workers (per the chairman's remarks).
Humro in-house manufacturing line: first product targeted by end-June 2026, a second model by August, and five products manufactured locally this year.
Humro inventory in the US is about 29 units, of which 5-6 are demos and 5-6 are in sales. About 20 units are to be commercially sold, with 12-15 already deployed.
FY27 deployment schedule: first 15 units ship around end-June/first week of July 2026 and a further 10 around 15 July, for deployment July-September; a further 50-60 units are being built.
Planned US strategic partner to hold local inventory, cutting delivery lead time from about 4 months to about 15 days.
demand_pricing: Humro's ₹36 Cr lease-model book equates to about $100,000 per month of lease rental; about $25,000 per month is currently billing, with $75,000 expected within one to two months.
Management said it is priced around 15-20% below Chinese competitors; named US competitors are Vecna, Seegrid and VisionNav.
Management said the April-May 2026 Humro deployments were nil; 24 units were contracted and expected to deploy over the next couple of months.
Order timelines for automation work have slipped 6-8 months as customers deferred spending (per management), and some orders were rejected on profitability.

Domestic AMR opportunity: management says customers importing more than 500 AMRs from China into India are being targeted as a substitute. Management said it will not take low-margin India execution work.

qa_highlights.question: How many Humro robots were deployed in April-May against the 225-unit FY27 target, and is the target being revised?
qa_highlights.answer: No new installs in April-May; 24 units were contracted for deployment in the following months. Management said there is no revision to the 225-unit target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY26 revenue fall sharply when the Q3 call indicated flat revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it rejected low-margin orders and added a cost-control department. Customers also deferred timelines by 6-8 months from February 2026 amid a global constraint, which delayed dispatch and revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How does Humro compare with competitors on quality and price in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management named Vecna, Seegrid and VisionNav, saying they are about two years ahead. It claims pricing 15-20% below Chinese offers and cites technology, Indian software and easy integration as advantages.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ₹48 Cr investment will go to which uses, and what happens to ARAPL's holding?
qa_highlights.answer: The ARAPL holding is 83% now and will drop below 50% once allotment completes. Most funds go to operations and marketing, with some to product development; management said it does not plan local US manufacturing for now.

qa_highlights.question: Can minority shareholders still benefit after Humro is no longer a subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ARAPL will consolidate its share of around 43-45% of Humro profit, and that minority benefits are intact. No detailed structure was given.

risks_watch: Humro's execution: deployments have slipped, with only about $25,000 per month of revenue against a $100,000 per month lease target.
Dilution of ARAPL's stake in Humro below 50% and the consolidation impact (around 43-45% share of profit), which minority shareholders questioned.
Dependence on imported components (motors, motor controllers and radar sensors) that management said are European or Japanese brands but imported via China.
US tariff exposure, which management said has come down from 50% to 25% (and about 20-22% now), with a further policy change expected within two years.
Order-book slippage in automation: customers deferring timelines by 6-8 months.
Lack of numerical guidance for FY27 and FY28, plus Q1 seasonal losses.
541402|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on margins and the Humro pipeline, but evasive on numbers: management declined to give revenue or margin guidance and repeatedly redirected questions on FY27 revenue and Humro's quantified economics.
key_quotes: So, as of now, no revision. Yeah, we are still very positive.
We are very, very competitively priced, around 15 to 20 percent lower than what the Chinese are offering.
So, number guidance or margin guidance we have stopped giving.
So, my sole target is to reduce the price by 50% in next two years.

541403|2026-03.headline: Dollar Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13.2% YoY to INR622 crore, but gross margin fell 169 bps to 28.1% on mix and cotton costs; price hikes of 4-6% planned.
541403|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating income grew 13.2% YoY to INR622 crore and volume grew 12.0%, but gross margin compressed 169 bps to 28.1% as the economy segment rose to 47% of revenue and cotton/yarn costs rose. Operating EBITDA grew only 2.0% to INR58 crore (9.3% margin), while PAT rose 11.4% to INR33 crore. For FY26, operating income rose 10.0% to INR1,881 crore, EBITDA 9.3% to INR200 crore (10.6% margin) and PAT 18.0% to INR107 crore. Management implemented a calibrated price hike in April (3-4%) and plans another 2-3% in June, and it deferred FY27 guidance to the Q1 call.

segments.name: Economy (Dollar Always)
segments.commentary: Rose to 47% of Q4 revenue from 45% in Q4 FY25 and about 41% for FY26 (FY25: 39.1%); management cited this as the main driver of lower realisation.

segments.name: Dollar Man / Regular and Big Boss
segments.commentary: Regular 41.5% and Big Boss 36.5% of FY26 revenue; Dollar Man category share fell to 36.5% from 38.8% in FY25.

segments.name: Missy (women's)
segments.commentary: About 7.5% of FY26 revenue, down from 8.0% in FY25.

segments.name: Thermals
segments.commentary: 6.1% of FY26 revenue, up from 5.9% in FY25.

segments.name: Force NXT (super premium)
segments.commentary: Value +16.5% and volume +26.2% in FY26; 4.5% of revenue, up from 4.2%. Q4 value +16.0%, volume +24.3%.

segments.name: Dollar Protect (rainwear)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume +49.9%; FY26 volume +18%; 2.1% of revenue.

segments.name: Quick commerce / non-traditional channels
segments.commentary: Quick commerce grew 437% YoY and rose to 2.5% of revenue from 0.5%; non-traditional channels (MT, e-commerce, QC) grew 24.2% in FY26.

segments.name: G.O.A.T alliance
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR49 crore (+45% YoY), PAT INR4.9 crore (~10% margin).

segments.name: Pepe Inner Fashion JV
segments.commentary: Only bottom line consolidated (51% stake); revenue not in top line; D2C via large-format stores.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 guidance; management will give full-year guidance on or before the Q1 FY27 call.
Management expects double-digit volume and value growth in FY27 and says margins should be better than FY26 (FY26 EBITDA margin 10.6%; management cited ~10.82%).
Price hikes: about 3-4% in April and 2-3% in June (total 4-6%; CFO cited 6-7%); management says no further hike is needed as cotton and yarn prices stabilise.
Cash conversion cycle to fall a further 5-7 days in FY27, mainly from receivable days.
Modern trade expected to grow 20-25% in FY27.
Debt of about INR264 crore expected to be reduced to zero by FY28; no major capex planned.
capex_capacity: No major capex commitments in the near term; capacity can be flexed 20-30% by adding job workers without capex.
FY26 production volume about 28 crore pieces; knitting, bleaching and cutting are in-house, while stitching (mainly economy and mix) is outsourced to job workers.
Pilot run of Phase 2 of Project Lakshya has started, focused on deepening active retailers in gold states; non-dominant state entry is on hold pending tailored strategies.
Merger of nine promoter (RPT) companies: NCLT application filed and first motion approved; expected to save INR4-5 crore a year in royalty, service charges and rent, with negligible revenue effect.
demand_pricing: Q4 gross margin decline attributed mainly to economy-segment mix (47%) and higher yarn prices that were not passed on; management denied meaningful down-trading and said the shift was temporary.
Demand described as stable; Q4 retail footfall dipped due to heat, which management called timing, not structural.
Management says the price hike has not hurt demand and that competitive intensity is stabilising; no market share loss is expected since peers are also raising prices.
Lakshya contribution to revenue was about 27% in Q4 versus 29% a year earlier, but management said the full-year contribution was flat.

qa_highlights.question: Is the price hike a one-off, how large is it, and does it come with scheme rollbacks?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry-wide hike after about 2 years: 3-4% in April and 2-3% in June, total about 4-6% (CFO cited 6-7%). It is a pure price increase; schemes and discounts are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Can debt of INR264 crore be substantially reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said debt can be reduced to zero by FY28; about INR50 crore of short- and long-term borrowings were repaid last year. Management expects further cash from a 5-7 day cycle reduction.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 gross margin decline, cotton or competition?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said mix (economy at 47%) and yarn costs were the main factors; prices were unchanged while realisation fell. Management denied meaningful discounting.

qa_highlights.question: Is the economy-segment shift structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is temporary, citing high demand in Tier 2/3 and rural areas, formalisation from unorganised players, and advertising of Dollar Lehar from the past three years. Force NXT grew 25-26%.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin return to double digits and what is the FY27 growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 margins should be better than FY26 and it is eyeing double-digit growth, but gave no specific number and deferred guidance to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory and working-capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days fell from about 130 to 100; management said optimised inventory is 95-100 days given the 90-day production cycle, and receivables are the main lever for the next 5-7 day reduction.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure: Q4 gross margin fell 169 bps; whether June price hike offsets yarn costs and mix is the key Q1 test.
Economy-segment share at 47% of revenue; a continued shift would keep realisation and margin pressured.
Q1 demand softness from heat and footfall; management says it is timing, not structural.
Lakshya Phase 2 pilot results and the pace of new-state entry, which management has put on hold.
Working capital: receivable-day reduction of 5-7 days is targeted; inventory days may not stay at FY26 levels.
Merger of promoter companies (NCLT) and the JV's contribution to consolidated bottom line.
541403|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand and margin recovery, and on debt reduction, but evasive on FY27 numbers: guidance was deferred to Q1, and the growth percentage was not given when pressed. Audio issues interrupted the call several times.
key_quotes: Our net cash from operating activities as a proportion of Operating EBITDA stood at 70% as of 31st March 2026, affirming that our reported profits are backed by real cash generation.
So the price hike that we have taken in the Q1, I think we don't have to take any further price hike now.
It's not a structural thing which is happening. It's a very temporary thing.
Right now, I'm unable to give you a number and we will surely come back with a number on or before the Q1 earnings call.

rows.why: No specific new product or brand launch was discussed; Force NXT and Dollar Protect growth were cited but no new launches.

rows.why: CCC fell from 160 to 154 days in FY26 and inventory days dropped from about 130 to 100; management targets a further 5-7 day cut, mainly receivables, and debt of INR264 crore to zero by FY28.

rows.label: Modern trade and quick commerce growth
rows.why: Management eyes 20-25% modern trade growth in FY27; quick commerce grew 437% and rose to 2.5% of revenue from 0.5%, non-traditional channels grew 24.2% in FY26.

rows.why: NCLT first motion approved on merger of nine RPT companies, expected to save INR4-5 crore a year in royalty, service charges and rent against FY26 PAT of INR107 crore.

541403|2026-06.headline: Dollar Industries Q1 FY27: operating EBITDA up 11.4% to INR 48 crore at 11.8% margin, on price hikes and no discounting, while volume fell 1.6%.
541403|2026-06.overview: Operating income rose 1.4% YoY to INR 405 crore, with gross margin up 192 bps to 37.4% after a 4-5% calibrated price increase taken in April. Management chose not to match market discounting, so revenue growth was limited and volume declined 1.6% YoY, mainly from Dollar Man. PAT rose 22.1% to INR 26 crore and net debt fell to INR 192 crore from INR 277 crore at March 2026. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 11-13% and operating EBITDA margin of 11.5-12.5%.

541729|2026-03.headline: HDFC AMC FY26 profit after tax rose 16% to INR28.6 billion; QAAUM grew 20% to INR9.3 trillion and dividend of INR54 per share was recommended.
541729|2026-03.overview: HDFC AMC closed FY26 with revenue from operations of INR41.2 billion (up 18% YoY), operating profit of INR32.1 billion (up 18%, 35 bps of AUM) and PAT of INR28.6 billion (up 16%). QAAUM reached INR9.3 trillion (up 20%), with equity-oriented AUM at INR6 trillion and unique investors up 3.5 million to 16.7 million. Management highlighted record March 2026 SIP flows of INR321 billion industry-wide and said investor behaviour during the market correction was disciplined. The major open issue is the SEBI base expense ratio (BER) change effective April 1, 2026, which management expects to offset through commission changes with no material P&L impact.

segments.name: Equity-oriented funds
segments.commentary: Equity-oriented AUM reached INR6 trillion. Actively managed equity yield was about 60-61 bps, versus 56 bps including index funds.

segments.name: Debt and liquid funds
segments.commentary: Debt yield was 28 bps and liquid 13 bps in Q4. Management said the balance sheet debt book is run with modest duration and largely passive management.

segments.name: Alternatives, PMS and international
segments.commentary: Alternatives margins are marginally above equity margins, and discretionary PMS is in line with equity margins. Non-discretionary EPFO/SPFO mandates earn thinner net economics. GIFT City has five live funds, all wholly owned.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the gross impact of the base expense ratio change on existing book at about 3-4 bps, to be largely offset by commission restructuring and cost management, so targeted P&L impact is not material.
The 5 bps trail previously paid in lieu of exit load has been removed, and GST on management fees now sits outside the expense ratio, requiring margin adjustments.

No formal cost guidance is given. Employee cost ex-ESOP grew about 12.5% YoY, with five-year CAGRs of about 13% for employee cost and 13.5% for non-employee cost; costs are expected to grow broadly in line with business.
Management said flow market share is above book market share, and the company will launch SIF products only after careful design, not as a race.
Management said the SEBI-classified category presence is complete and new launches will be selective, with focus on sharpening existing funds.
capex_capacity: Physical branch network significantly expanded over the last couple of years, with further expansion under evaluation.
Investment in AI, cloud technology, cybersecurity and talent for PMS, international and alternatives; management called these foundational investments.
Rajan Anandan (Peak XV) appointed as invitee and external expert on the Technology Committee for a three-year term.
Seven new schemes launched in FY26, and first close of a private credit fund with IFC as partner and anchor investor announced.
Two EPFO/SPFO fixed income PMS mandates won. SPFO is already being managed, and the EPFO agreement is being signed.
demand_pricing: Industry: FY26 net inflows INR7.4 trillion, with equity-oriented funds about INR4.9 trillion; March 2026 SIP collections INR321 billion (up 24% YoY, 97 million contributing accounts). Industry market share is around 12.8-13% for the last eight to nine quarters.
HDFC AMC: direct plans about 31% of equity AUM; 97% of transactions digital; total accounts above 30 million; unique investors 16.7 million, up 3.5 million, versus industry addition of 7.2 million.
Unique investor penetration rose from 17.6% (March 2023) to 27% (March 2026). Folios rose from 2.3 crore to 3 crore, and SIP and STP flows were INR48.8 billion in March 2026 (up 33% YoY).

Management said flow share is higher than book share across channels, including fintech and HDFC Securities. HDFC Bank share of the distribution pie is declining, which management attributed to broad-based growth across other channels.
Competitive pressure: management stated SBI is almost closed-architecture, and some banks are more guided in retail distribution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the new TER/BER regulation and how will distribution commissions change?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross impact on the existing book is about 3-4 bps, to be offset through commission optimisation and cost management, so no material P&L impact is targeted. New commission structures already reflect removal of the 5 bps exit-load trail, and the company will share more detail over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why does a third-party calculation show Q4 flow market share below Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the calculation missed IDCW (dividend) payouts in Q4 that were recorded as redemptions; the company does not accept the computed figure. Management said overall flow share remains above book share.

qa_highlights.question: Why has one-year scheme performance and industry ranking weakened?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the funds remain in the top two quartiles across most categories and that many are rated 4 or 5 stars by Value Research. It pointed to long-term alpha track records, with 12-13 funds having 15-year-plus records.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY27 and FY28 expense growth targets available?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific guidance is given. Employee and non-employee costs have grown at about 13% CAGR over five years and are expected to grow in line with business and investments.

qa_highlights.question: What was the reason for the other income increase, and how is the balance sheet positioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said balance sheet equity is mainly SEBI skin-in-the-game MF holdings, which saw drawdowns in Q4. The remainder is in liquid and debt funds with modest duration and passive management.

qa_highlights.question: Will HDFC AMC launch new NFOs or SIF products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has secured all regulatory approvals for SIF. It is designing a couple of differentiated products but views the category as strategic rather than immediate. Management will stay selective on new launches.

risks_watch: SEBI base expense ratio change from April 1, 2026: margin effect depends on commission restructuring, and management said the impact is not yet quantified precisely.
Sustainability of flows if markets stay weak for longer; management cautioned that investor behaviour has not been tested over an extended downturn.
HDFC Bank channel share is declining, and management said the bank remains open architecture, with event-driven flow variability.
Rising costs from talent, technology and AI investments versus margin targets, with no formal cost guidance.
Alternatives and PMS economics are thinner for non-discretionary government mandates (EPFO/SPFO), and SIF launch timing is undefined.
Mark-to-market exposure on the SEBI skin-in-the-game equity holdings on the balance sheet.
541729|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on flows, investor maturity and long-term growth, but defensive on market share, the HDFC Bank channel and performance ranking. Management was cautious and non-committal on cost guidance, SIF timing and the quantified TER impact, saying it is still early.
key_quotes: And that clearly shows a very mature behaviour of investors.
So overall, the targeted impact on our P&L should not be material.
So overall flows are higher than the book share, that much I can tell you.
Real question is, how do we participate in a way that is consistent with our philosophy?

541729|2026-06.headline: HDFC AMC Q1 FY27: quarterly average AUM INR9.35 trillion (+13% YoY), PAT INR8.4 billion (+12% YoY), with debt AUM weakening.
541729|2026-06.overview: Quarterly average AUM reached INR9.35 trillion, up 13% YoY, with market share of 11.2% (12.4% ex-ETFs). Revenue from operations rose 14% YoY to INR11 billion and PAT rose 12% YoY to INR8.4 billion. Management said margins were maintained despite a regime change from TER to BER accounting, the removal of the 5 bps exit-load-linked charge, and brokerage rationalisation from 1 April 2026. Debt QAAUM fell and debt market share was under pressure, while SIP and systematic flows kept growing.

financial_highlights.change: Equity active market share ~12.8% YoY, down ~20 bps QoQ
vs INR2.1 billion in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Equity
segments.commentary: Equity-oriented QAAUM is 65.7% of company AUM vs 56.6% for the industry; blended equity yield 58 bps. Equity market share held at around 12.8% YoY.

segments.name: Debt
segments.commentary: Debt QAAUM INR1.66 trillion with 12.9% market share; debt AUM fell about 6% QoQ on closing basis per analyst, with industry debt outflows of INR757 billion. Debt yield 28 bps.

segments.name: Liquid
segments.commentary: Liquid QAAUM INR851 billion with 10.7% market share; liquid yield 13 bps. Industry liquid inflows INR984 billion in the quarter.

segments.name: Alternatives / PMS / AIF
segments.commentary: Total alternatives AUM INR148 billion vs INR60 billion a year ago. Management says alternatives economics are slightly better than mutual fund equity; a private credit fund closes this quarter and a VC/PE fund of funds was approved with a proposed $50 million seed commitment.

guidance_outlook: Management said margins have been maintained through the new TER-to-BER regime, offset by commission optimisation and cost control; it asked not to read too much into quarterly yield movements.
Net operating margin to stay within the 33-35 bps of AUM corridor, per CFO; management will not underinvest.
Non-cash ESOP cost guided at INR79-80 crore for FY27, INR63 crore for FY28, INR41 crore for FY29 and INR11 crore for FY30.
Company declined to forecast AUM growth. Buyback vs dividend is a Board decision.

PMS Category 3 product in process of raising money after approval; senior resources hired for PMS and SIF.

Investment team: 37 investment professionals on mutual fund side; 6 on PE/VC, 6 on private credit, 8 on PMS (debt and equity).
demand_pricing: Industry SIP contributions INR318 billion in June 2026 vs INR273 billion in June 2025 (+17%); folios 279 million; unique investors 61.9 million.
HDFC AMC added about 0.46 million unique investors vs industry 0.53 million; base 17.1 million; penetration 28% (from 25%).
Management said fintechs registered 8.6 million SIPs (gross new registrations) in the quarter; bank channel share fell to 9.6% from 10.4% in Q1 FY26.
Debt fund outflows attributed to rupee and rate volatility, crude and geopolitics; management said industry must make debt funds more attractive to retail.
Distributor economics described as a long-term partnership; management said manufacturer-distributor economics do not change with market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt AUM fall about 6% QoQ and why are debt outflows strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said investors redeemed debt funds on rupee, rate and crude volatility while liquid funds saw inflows; HDFC AMC has a decent share of both moves.

qa_highlights.question: Is the yield uptick from product mix or the TER/BER change, and what is the PMS/AIF contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not read too much into early-quarter movement post the accounting change. Alternatives earn 80-90 bps management fee; PMS discretionary book is in line with equity margins, non-discretionary is very tight economics.

qa_highlights.question: Has the distribution commission been rationalised and will revenue yield benefit in later quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Changes from 1 April 2026: removal of 5 bps extra TER charged in lieu of exit load, shift from TER to BER plus statutory levies, and brokerage rationalisation. Offset through commission optimisation and cost control; margins maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ESOP cost jump, and is FY27 guidance unchanged?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 cost of about INR23 crore reflects a June 2025 grant under the new plan; FY27 non-cash ESOP cost guided at INR79-80 crore, unchanged at INR67 crore level per analyst reference point is for prior guide. Management said costs should be viewed annually.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an operating cost growth guidance of 12-13% ex non-cash?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said to focus on the 33-35 bps net operating margin corridor rather than quarterly cost trends.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the performance improvement in June?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited top-two-quartile performance over 2 and 3 years on AUM-weighted basis; Balance Advantage Fund in Q1 over 3, 5, 10 years, and Flexicap in Q1 over 2, 3, 5, 10 years.

risks_watch: Debt AUM outflows and debt market share pressure; management said it needs to make debt funds more attractive to retail.
Sustainability of SIP momentum and first-time investor behaviour through an extended market downturn, which management said has not yet been tested.
Distributor-channel share shifts toward fintechs; bank share fell to 9.6% from 10.4%.
Operating cost growth and rising non-cash ESOP cost; management said it will not underinvest.
Yield trajectory under the new TER-to-BER regime; management did not give forward yield guidance.

541729|2026-09.headline: HDFC AMC Q2 FY27: revenue from operations up 14% YoY to INR11.7 billion; operating profit up 16% to INR9.1 billion at 36 bps of AUM.
541729|2026-09.overview: Quarterly average AUM rose 10% YoY and 4% QoQ to INR9.69 trillion, with equity-oriented AUM at 67.1% versus 57.5% for the industry. Revenue from operations was INR11.7 billion (+14% YoY), operating profit INR9.1 billion (+16%), and PBT INR9.8 billion (+12%). Reported PAT is not comparable YoY because the year-ago quarter had a INR468 million tax provision reversal. Management pushed alternatives, PMS and GIFT City as growth areas, and defended cost growth as a mix of routine costs and forward investment.

segments.name: Active equity
segments.commentary: Yield of 61 bps; overall equity yield 58 bps, with a marginal sequential rise attributed mainly to asset mix. Active equity AUM INR6.08 trillion at 12.7% share.

segments.name: Debt
segments.commentary: Yield about 28-29 bps. Debt AUM INR1.62 trillion, 13% market share.

segments.name: Liquid
segments.commentary: Yield 13 bps. Liquid AUM INR860 billion, up 10% YoY.

segments.name: Alternatives and PMS
segments.commentary: Two new alternative funds launched: a Category II late-stage venture/growth fund and a first Category III fund; a Category II private equity fund (fund of funds) is fully committed to 13 GPs. EPFO fixed income mandate went live this quarter; management says AIF fees run 80-90 bps above equity MF fees. Share of non-MF revenue described as small.

segments.name: Passive and GIFT City
segments.commentary: Around 50 passive products; second-largest in index funds among retail-heavy categories. Six inbound and two outbound GIFT City funds.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give timelines for alternatives revenue (e.g., INR100 crore target).
New SIF (specialised investment fund) product launches expected over the next couple of quarters, after hiring two senior investment professionals.
Two new AIF launches in progress: Select Opportunities fund final-close process and Emerging Opportunities Category III fund fundraising continuing.
Management expects a steady CSR-related cost skew to unwind; asks investors to assess costs on a full-year basis.
FY27 non-cash ESOP expense expected at about INR79-80 crore.
capex_capacity: Cost commentary: investments in people (alternatives team of over 20 investment professionals; MF team about 40 versus 30 a couple of years back), investor servicing, operations, distribution, international and technology/AI.
Balance sheet cash deployed as seed capital for alternative platforms; Board has distributed almost all post-tax distributable cash profits over the last three years.
Systematic transactions 19 million in September (up from about 17 million in June); monthly SIP flows INR325 billion in September.
demand_pricing: Industry: equity-oriented net inflows INR1,161 billion in the quarter; 67th consecutive month of positive equity flows. Debt funds net outflows INR607 billion; liquid inflows INR457 billion; ETFs INR367 billion.
Systematic flows (SIP + STP) INR48 billion in September, up 6% YoY. Management says softness is in STP (paused by wealth managers when markets were choppy), while SIP-only market share rose.
Unique investors 17.7 million (28% penetration), added 3.2 million in last year versus industry 6.3 million. Live individual accounts 32 million, up from 26 million.

Market share in the quarter was 11.1% versus a prior best of 11.5% per an analyst; hybrid categories such as multi-asset, aggressive hybrid and equity savings saw share correction, with a new hybrid fund manager brought in.
Management said mid-cap fund is above INR1 lakh crore; small-cap fund about INR40,000 crore and ranked second or third in its category.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of sequential yield improvement and asset-wise yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Active equity 61 bps, overall equity 58 bps, debt 28-29 bps, liquid 13 bps. Improvement largely asset mix; not material.

qa_highlights.question: Alternatives revenue target and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give timelines; launched two new alternative funds and says the platform now works as full stack.

qa_highlights.question: Is SIP market share at risk from newer AMCs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident; SIP share has grown on track record, products, distribution and focus on SIPs, though competition is intense.

qa_highlights.question: Why is systematic flow share down in the last three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the comparison is not like-for-like; the softness is in STP, while SIP-only share rose. Systematic transactions rose from about 17 million to 19 million.

qa_highlights.question: Why did staff and non-staff costs fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company keeps tight cost control while investing in people, alternatives, international, digital and AI; no split of routine versus investment cost was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the equity yield gap versus peers due to product mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yields vary by fund size; TER falls as AUM rises, and three funds are above INR1 lakh crore. No yield guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is H1 expense growth high?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CSR expenses were taken in Q1, skewing H1; asked investors to look at full-year costs.

541741|2026-03.headline: Fratelli Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR36 crores and EBITDA turned near breakeven at INR1.06 crores for FY26, with FY27 guidance of about 30% growth.
541741|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 net revenue rose about 13% YoY to INR36 crores, with gross margin at 79% and EBITDA loss narrowing to INR3.7 crores from INR7 crores a year earlier. The RTD brand Shotgun sold about 100,000 cases in its first year.

541929|2026-03.headline: Synergy Green guides FY27 revenue to about ₹500 crore (+33%) with PBDIT margin up over 300 bps, while FY26 PBDIT margin fell to 13.10%.
541929|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was ₹123.45 crore with PBDIT of ₹14.83 crore (12.01% margin); FY26 total income was ₹376 crore (+3.5% YoY) with PBDIT of ₹48.67 crore (13.10%). Management attributed the weak year to brownfield expansion delays, outsourcing and relocation costs, and early West Asia-linked commodity and energy inflation. Capacity was expanded from 30,000 to 45,000 TPA foundry and a 20,000 TPA machining plant was added, but ramp-up is slow with utilisation expected to reach 80-90% only over 4-5 months. Management guided to ₹500-530 crore revenue and debt of ₹175-180 crore at FY27 end.

541929|2026-06.headline: Synergy Green Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹75.71 crore and 7% PBDIT margin were weak; management reiterates ₹500 crore FY27 revenue and 300 bps margin uplift.
541929|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 total income was ₹75.71 crore with absolute PBDIT of ₹5.3 crore at a 7% margin, as dispatches slipped on customer lifting, prototype approval delays and shipping constraints. Production rose about 10% YoY and the new 45,000 tpa capacity reached 66% utilisation in Q1, with July utilisation at 85% (about 3,200 tons). Raw material, consumable and energy inflation (linked to the West Asia conflict and an MSEDCL solar banking change) cut margins, which management expects to partly recover from Q2 via one-quarter-lagged indexation. Management maintained FY27 guidance of ~₹500 crore revenue (33% growth) and ~300 bps PBDIT margin expansion.

541956|2026-03.headline: IRCON FY26 revenue fell to Rs 9,502 crore (from Rs 11,131 crore) and PAT to Rs 592 crore; FY27 revenue guided flat at ~Rs 9,000 crore.
541956|2026-03.overview: FY26 total revenue was Rs 9,502 crore against Rs 11,131 crore in FY25, and PAT declined to Rs 592 crore from Rs 724 crore. Management said the order book rose to about Rs 24,984 crore (about 2x annual revenue), but sectoral headwinds and tougher bidding competition are pressuring margins. Management said FY26 revenue was about Rs 9,000 crore against earlier guidance of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore, citing execution delays beyond its control, and guided FY27 at similar levels. Standalone core EBITDA margin is guided to 4.0-4.2% on the Q&A call (4.0-4.5% in a later answer), with consolidated PAT margin of 6.1-6.3%.

541967|2026-03.headline: Sky Gold guides FY27 revenue INR8,100 crore and FY30 PAT INR945 crore, targets 50%+ debt reduction in FY27 with working capital cut to 59 days.
541967|2026-03.overview: Management said Q4 FY26 outpaced industry peers on wedding and festive demand, with B2B volumes steady despite the recent customs duty hike and government appeal to curb gold consumption. Net working capital days fell to 59 from 71 a year earlier, and operating cash flow improved from negative INR272 crore to negative INR45 crore for the year. Management revised its guidance framing: it will no longer give volume guidance, keeps FY30 PAT of INR945 crore, and sees 30-35% revenue CAGR with an advanced gold model that lowers reported revenue but adds margin. Phase 3 is funded wholly from internal cash, with a net debt-free balance sheet targeted by FY30.

Management says gold price correction of about 10% in recent days is driving customer demand; gold price was about INR1,55,000 per 10g as quoted on the call.
Akshaya Tritiya on 20 April: some Q4 inventory was held back and delivered in early April, which raised inventory days.

qa_highlights.question: Will the customs duty hike and government appeal to reduce gold consumption hit revenue or volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no order softening has been seen at B2B level as the company is focused on lightweight jewellery; the retail gold exchange share reportedly rose from 20% to 40%, and it is too early to call June-July demand.

qa_highlights.question: Is the shift to lower karat and bullion/coins a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is part of the strategy; 9kt, 14kt and 18kt carry better margins, while 22kt remains 70-75% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why has gold metal loan usage dropped to zero?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said GML is currently costlier than local market purchases, so it is used only when PAT-accretive; GML facility of INR170 crore remains sanctioned.

qa_highlights.question: Does the setup of a Dubai office for duty-free gold get affected by the 100 kg advanced licence restriction?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the restriction applies only to advanced authorisation licences, which the company is not using now, so there is no impact; gold availability is not seen as an issue.

qa_highlights.question: Will receivable days return to FY24 levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivable days should return to 22-23 days within 4-6 quarters as export and shorter-credit customers are prioritised.

qa_highlights.question: How does volume growth fit with 30-35% revenue CAGR, and what is the hedging policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 27-28% of growth is volume-led; the company is about 99% hedged, using MCX futures as the only tool available in India, with zero GML now.

541967|2026-06.headline: Sky Gold Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 78% YoY to INR2,013 crores, with gross margin at 9.3% and operating cash flow of about INR30 crores.
541967|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q1 FY27 was INR2,013 crores, up 78% YoY, implying an annualised run rate near the FY27 guidance of INR8,100 crores. Gross margin rose to 9.3% from 9.1% in Q4 FY26, driven by a higher share of non-22KT jewellery and studded products. EBITDA was INR157 crores (7.8% margin) and operating PAT crossed INR100 crores for the first time. Operating cash flow turned positive at about INR30 crores, and working capital days edged up to 60 from 59 in March. Management said it will revise FY27 guidance only after Diwali.

541974|2026-03.headline: Manorama FY26 standalone revenue rose 76.1% to INR 1,357 crore with EBITDA margin of 27.1% and PAT of INR 233.2 crore.
541974|2026-03.overview: FY26 standalone revenue grew 76.1% YoY to about INR 1,357 crore, with EBITDA of INR 367.7 crore (27.1% margin) and PAT of INR 233.2 crore (17.2% margin). Q4 standalone revenue was INR 382.3 crore, EBITDA INR 102.9 crore (26.9%) and PAT INR 59.5 crore (15.6%), with a forex net loss of INR 7.58 crore after a INR 17.05 crore mark-to-market provision. Management announced a roughly INR 460 crore capex plan over two to three years covering solvent fractionation, a cocoa butter alternatives plant, refining and Burkina Faso raw material processing. Consolidated margins were softer as nine new subsidiaries were in their first year, and the company filed revised results due to a wrong file being uploaded.

Funding through internal accruals (about INR 130 crore fixed deposits); QIP enabling approval up to INR 500 crore, with no decision yet.
demand_pricing: FY26 volume growth about 80-90% and price growth about 5-10%, per management in Q&A.

Manorama Africa supplied about 20-25% of raw material purchases in FY26 versus about 60% previously cited by an analyst; FY27 share to follow the same procurement line.

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to first-year operations of new subsidiaries, with higher freight, production and setup costs; said 45-50% gross margin is the normal range.

qa_highlights.answer: A wrong file was uploaded inadvertently due to a technical issue; the revision is corrective and the revised financials should be used.

qa_highlights.answer: Dekel is a processing-cost model paid per tonne processed, with no profit sharing. Subsidiary losses were attributed to first-year setup costs and expected to normalise; no separate breakdown was given.

541974|2026-06.headline: Manorama Q1 FY27 revenue rose 39.5% YoY to INR 404 crore and PAT rose 67.6% to INR 79 crore, with PAT margin at 19.5%.
541974|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 39.5% YoY to INR 404 crore, crossing INR 400 crore for the first time, with management attributing growth mainly to volume (about 85% YoY per management). EBITDA rose 42.2% to INR 106 crore at a 26.3% margin, and PAT rose 67.6% to INR 79 crore. Management said the QIP of about INR 500 crore has closed and it has lined up a ~INR 460 crore capex plan spanning India and Burkina Faso, with commissioning targeted around Q3 FY28. Several answers were qualitative or deferred, notably on guidance, Brazil revenue, and subsidiary losses.

segments.commentary: Consolidated PAT loss narrowed to about INR 3 crore from about INR 8 crore in Q4 FY26, with negligible subsidiary revenue; West African entities are sourcing vehicles and Brazil is in build-out.

guidance_outlook: FY27 utilisation guidance is about 80% (management internal target 80-85%) on expanded capacity of about 52,000 tonnes per annum after 4,500 t debottlenecking; the company declined to restate the INR 1,600-1,800 crore revenue guidance from November, pointing to utilisation metrics instead.
FY27 capex guidance of about INR 225-250 crore; about INR 70 crore spent to date and about INR 220 crore more planned in FY27.

Gross margin expected in a 45-50% range, with EBITDA margin the preferred tracking metric; management said margins should hold broadly stable at current range, with quarter-to-quarter movement possible.

Burkina Faso facility (about INR 120-130 crore) has an estimated payback of about 3 years once operational; the remainder of the ~INR 460 crore plan is for India (solvent fractionation 3 and refinery).
Solvent fractionation 3 and refinery targeted for commissioning around Q3 FY28; full impact expected in FY29 as plants ramp up.
Balance sheet: no further equity dilution planned; working capital to be funded via existing banker lines led by SBI, plus ~INR 150 crore FDR outside the QIP proceeds.
capex_capacity: Current fractionation capacity 47,500 t per annum; additional 7,500 t already operational, with a further 4,500 t debottlenecking targeted around Q3 FY27, taking capacity to about 52,000 t.
Debottlenecking cost estimated at INR 5-6 crore.

Burkina Faso: about 10 hectares (24 acres) land acquired for shea nut and mango nut processing with regulatory approvals pending; facility covers extraction and expelling, solvent fractionation and related capacity, about INR 120-130 crore.
Overall proposed capex plan about INR 460 crore; about INR 70 crore spent to date; Q1 spend about INR 20 crore across Manorama and subsidiaries.
Brazil (LatAm) partner: trial production started in the last quarter; ramp-up expected gradually over the next 2-4 quarters, with production sourced from the Indian plant.
Asset turn currently about 7x; management would not guide to 7x-9x going forward.
demand_pricing: Demand described as volume-led; management attributed about 85% YoY growth to volume.
Pricing described as largely stable for value-added products, in line with the costing model that passes through raw material inflation.
Raw material mix: about 50-60% imported seeds and butters, the rest domestic seeds (sal, mango) and butters.
Contracts are 9-12 months and renew on a rolling basis; no renewal percentage was disclosed.
Nigeria's temporary shea nut export ban was called non-material given sourcing across about 10 African subsidiaries.
Exports to more than 30 countries; export share about 55-60% in Q1 FY25 and 60% in Q1 FY27 per management.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of the 4,500 t debottlenecking and greenfield capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Debottlenecking is due around Q3 FY27; solvent fractionation 3 and refinery are targeted around Q3 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Brazil ramp-up and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production started; gradual quarter-on-quarter ramp expected over 2-4 quarters; no revenue guidance given yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall about 20% QoQ, and is it the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Prior quarter included a performance incentive provision; run-rate guided at INR 14-15 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin decline and raw material cost ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin expected at 45-50%; management disputed the 75-80% H1 raw material ratio, saying it has been about 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated subsidiary losses and whether they will narrow?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses reflect operating costs of sourcing vehicles and Brazil build-out; drag expected to reduce as entities scale, with no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Utilisation guidance versus the 85-90% cited in the presentation?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal target 80-85%; 80% advised for stakeholders, with upside to be communicated if achieved.

qa_highlights.question: Funding of working capital for the new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Funded by existing bank lines (SBI lead), the QIP of about INR 500 crore and FDR of about INR 150 crore; no further equity dilution planned.

Working capital needs for new capacity (analyst estimate INR 900-1,000 crore) and reliance on bank lines.

541988|2026-03.headline: AAVAS Q4FY26: net profit up 18% YoY to Rs 1.82 bn, NIM up 44 bps QoQ to 8.45%, GNPA 1.05%; management targets 20%+ AUM growth aspiration.
541988|2026-03.overview: Q4FY26 disbursements rose 16% YoY and 36% QoQ to Rs 23.5 bn, and net profit grew 18% YoY to Rs 1.82 bn on 17% NII growth. FY26 AUM reached Rs 234.5 bn (up 15% YoY) while FY26 disbursements grew 11% to Rs 67.8 bn, below the aspiration. Asset quality improved sequentially, with 1+ DPD at 3.17% (down 63 bps QoQ) and GNPA at 1.05% (down 14 bps QoQ). Management acknowledged weak volume productivity and opex growth outpacing AUM, and is pushing risk-adjusted pricing and direct sourcing to address these.

financial_highlights.metric: Net interest margin (Q4FY26, on total assets)

financial_highlights.change: +38 bps QoQ; net worth growth 16% YoY

segments.name: Home loans / core retail (assessed income)
segments.commentary: Management cites best-in-class underwriting in the assessed income segment; Q4 home loan volumes declined YoY per analyst analysis, with the company acknowledging volume productivity as an immediate focus area. Borrower repayment rates rose mainly due to prepayments, with balance transfer-outs held at 5.5% for FY26 against a sub-6% cap.

segments.name: Geographies
segments.commentary: Vintage states show 1+ DPD and GNPA well below 4% and 1.25% of AUM; emerging markets are at 1+ DPD within 4% and GNPA within 1% of AUM. Q4 branch additions were concentrated in Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat, with focus also on Maharashtra and southern states.

guidance_outlook: Long-term aspiration of consistent 20%+ AUM growth, outperforming the industry; no specific FY27 growth number given.
ROE target set in the high teens (current Q4FY26 ROE 14.67%).
Spreads to be maintained at 5%+ despite PLR cuts, with the slight yield placement improvement expected to offset cost of borrowing stabilising.
Opex-to-AUM targeted below 3% on a 2-3 year horizon; the CFO's earlier comment indicates 2.75% once the balance sheet doubles.
Credit cost guidance maintained below 25 bps on a sustainable basis; no move into riskier segments.
Management expects branch investments to yield results in the next full year, with growth expected to recover in FY27.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded to 435 across 15 states after 31 additions in Q4FY26, with focus on Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra and southern states.
Technology: most capitalisation done on Oracle FLEXCUBE and Oracle Fusion ERP; only small annual spend planned for collection software and AI/GenAI in underwriting and collections.
Opex rose YoY in FY26 due to branch-expansion manpower, new ESOP/PSOP retention scheme after CVC entry, and lower-than-planned growth in denominators.
Management expects the branch and people investments to start producing results in the next full year.
demand_pricing: Competition intensified in Q4 as lenders pushed to underwrite volume in the year-end quarter; management says it does not see competition materially affecting yield placement over the full year.
Yield decline of about 20 bps QoQ in Q4 was attributed mainly to a 15 bps PLR cut effective 1 March 2026; a further 10 bps PLR cut is expected in June per an analyst.
Management is shifting toward risk-adjusted pricing at branch level; it says early results are visible but the journey is gradual.
Average ticket size is to move only with inflation; no deliberate ticket-size expansion.
April 2026 bounce rates were lower than March and lower than April 2025, per the CRO; the Middle East war has not yet shown up in collections.
Sourcing mix: management is rebuilding direct sourcing (branch-driven, CSC, website, app with referral programme) while stating indirect channels will continue.

qa_highlights.question: Where does the sector's medium-term growth stand and what are FY27/FY28 growth targets, and where does ROE settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Aspiration is 20%+ AUM growth. Near-term focus is sharper execution across product, channel mix, geography and funnel leakages. High-teens ROE is the long-term target.

qa_highlights.question: With the PLR cut, how will spreads and disbursement yields evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a full-year cost of borrowing reduction of 62 bps stabilising, spread at 5.2%, and confidence in maintaining spreads at 5%+ via better product placement. It did not give a quantified yield outlook.

qa_highlights.question: Why has growth been below 20% for two years and what is the channel plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed past performance to different variables and times. It plans to rebuild direct sourcing muscle while keeping indirect channels, and to invest in southern and other high-potential states.

qa_highlights.question: Has risk-adjusted pricing started and does higher yield imply higher risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing improvement began in FY26 across 435 branches and is progressing gradually. Management said higher yield does not mean higher risk and that it will not enter riskier segments or breach credit cost guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is competition from larger HFCs entering the company's ticket sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 competition was a seasonal year-end push. It does not see a structural competitive impact on yields over the full year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the opex-to-AUM trajectory and what are the tech-led efficiency use cases?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex rose in FY26 for branch and ESOP reasons. Management targets below 3% over 2-3 years and expects the branch investment to pay off in FY27. Tech spend is limited to small collection-software and AI investments.

qa_highlights.question: Why have loan volumes been flat or down despite headcount and branch growth, and what changed in April?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called this an immediate priority, reported improved April numbers, and said productivity per person and revenue per field employee will be tracked quarterly. It also noted a shift to requiring realised instrument receipt in customer accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did repayment rates rise while balance transfer-outs fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance transfer-outs were 5.5% for FY26 against a sub-6% cap. The rise in repayments was mainly from customer prepayments and part-payments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure to the Middle East war and inflation shock?
qa_highlights.answer: No adverse trend in bounces or collections so far. The company is not financing energy-linked or directly affected profiles and is tracking 5-6 profiles it considers at risk.

542011|2026-03.headline: GRSE posted record FY26: revenue INR 7,002 crore (+38%) and PAT INR 748 crore (+42%), with order book down to INR 15,324 crore.

542011|2026-06.headline: GRSE Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 39% YoY to ₹1,815 crore and PAT 44% to ₹173 crore; order book ₹13,596 crore.
542011|2026-06.overview: Management reported total income of ₹1,914 crore (+38% YoY), revenue from operations of ₹1,815 crore (+39%), and PAT of ₹173 crore (+44%) with EPS of ₹15.09 versus ₹10.49. The company said this was its 17th consecutive quarter of upward trend in financials. Order book stands at ₹13,596 crore across 11 projects and 44 marine platforms, and the Next Generation Corvette (NGC) contract is still awaited with management guiding signing within the quarter. Capacity expansion (brownfield and greenfield, roughly ₹4,200 crore combined capex) was the main strategic update, alongside Navratna status granted on 19 June 2026.

financial_highlights.change: First time below ₹15,000 crore in 10 years, per management
Attributed to absence of ship commissioning costs incurred in Q4 FY26
Management called it sinusoidal, tied to delivery phase

segments.name: Shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Shipbuilding order book ₹12,980 crore (~95% of total); P-17 Alpha ~₹4,519 crore, NGOPV ~₹3,075 crore, anti-submarine shallow water craft ~₹1,815 crore, Ocean Research Vessel ₹740 crore, Acoustic Research Ship ₹450 crore, Multipurpose Vessels plus Dredger ~₹1,355 crore.

segments.commentary: Order book about ₹96 crore.

segments.commentary: Order book about ₹219 crore.

segments.commentary: Order book ₹158 crore; management says 100% indigenous.

segments.commentary: Order book ₹58 crore; about 90% indigenous per management.

segments.commentary: Order book ₹82 crore; co-production with foreign OEM targeting 55-60% indigenization.

Concurrent construction capacity to rise from 28 to 32 platforms by end of calendar 2026; to 43 platforms after Raichak (West Bengal) and western-seaboard facilities.
Management said current quarter's performance can be replicated in coming quarters, citing P-17 Alpha (~₹4,500 crore left) and ASW craft (~₹1,816 crore left) as major execution drivers.
Expects employee cost increase of 15-20% from next pay commission, consistent with past pay commissions.
Bonus or stock split: awaiting directions from administrative ministry and DIPAM.
capex_capacity: P-17 Alpha large ship ~85% complete; delivery targeted by November 2026 (calendar year). First two P-17 Alpha ships delivered ahead of schedule.
Four of eight anti-submarine shallow water craft delivered; remaining four to be delivered in FY27 (fifth ~91%, sixth ~88%, seventh and eighth ~65-70%).
NGOPV: first ship launched, second launched ~11 August 2026; third and fourth launches in Q3 and Q4 FY27; first delivery Q2 FY28, last Q2 FY29.

Expansion capex: ~₹200 crore for two Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port facilities (18-month revitalization, already started); ~₹2,200 crore for Raichak greenfield shipyard in West Bengal (DPR in final stages, 3-5 years to operationalise, infra work from 2027); ~₹2,000 crore for a Gujarat-side total ship solution facility (shipbuilding, green recycling, repair) on PPP model, DPR complete, environmental clearance obtained, ~3 years to operationalise.
demand_pricing: Live defence RFPs ~₹80,000 crore (Navy and Coast Guard): 120 fast interceptor craft ~₹3,500 crore (bid due next month); 31 follow-on water jet FAC ~₹3,500 crore; 22 interceptor boats ~₹1,200-1,300 crore (bids submitted); six NGOPVs for Coast Guard ~₹2,500 crore; P-17 Bravo (DAC AON ₹70,000 crore).
RFPs expected in calendar 2026: mine sounder measure vessel (~₹36,000 crore AON, split between two yards, 8 and 4) and four LPDs (~₹35,000 crore).

Non-defence tenders out via PSU demand aggregation: four MR tankers; six VLGCs and six Aframax vessels (GRSE partnering with a foreign yard and a sister yard); container ship tender expected (partnering with an Indian yard due to lack of dock capacity).
Letters of intent received for four platform support vessels (ONGC) and one green electric tug (SMP Port, Kolkata); GRSE L1 in NGC (~₹ high value, contract awaited).
Water metro opportunity: ₹200-300 crore per metro; ~₹1,500 crore and 30-40 platforms if five states proceed.
Next Generation Destroyer not expected at RFP stage before FY29 per management (no DAC approval yet).
Export strategy: no export orders currently pursued given domestic non-defence demand (~200+ platforms); will consider attractive European orders.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Next Generation Corvette contract been delayed, and when would revenue recognition start if signed today?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the contract slipped from FY26-end/Q1 and is now expected to be signed this quarter, with no red flags seen. Revenue recognition would begin in FY28 after a pre-production design and equipment-ordering phase; the eight-ship project completes around 2034-35.

qa_highlights.question: Does GRSE have capability for unmanned and autonomous naval vessels, and does the expansion plan address it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has capability, citing an unmanned surface vessel prototype, a project for NSTL (DRDO) and an autonomous underwater platform prototype tested about a year ago. It is taking part in Navy-steered autonomy projects and was shortlisted for another underwater unmanned platform.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex quantum for greenfield and brownfield expansion, and what capability will it add?
qa_highlights.answer: Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port revitalisation is about ₹200 crore over 18 months. Raichak greenfield yard in West Bengal is about ₹2,200 crore with 3-5 years to operationalise; the Gujarat-side total ship solution facility is about ₹2,000 crore with about 3 years to operationalise. Capacity goes from 32 to 43 platforms, including larger Aframax/VLGC-type vessels.

qa_highlights.question: How will GRSE participate in large commercial tenders (MR tankers, VLGC, Aframax, container ships) given capacity limits?
qa_highlights.answer: MR tankers and VLGCs are being bid with a sister yard and, for VLGC, a foreign yard with proven capability. Container ships are being pursued through a partnership with an Indian yard that has the dock and berth infrastructure, as GRSE lacks physical capacity for them.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 execution momentum be sustained, or will growth slow from the ~35-40% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current quarter's performance can be replicated, pointing to about ₹4,500 crore left on P-17 Alpha and about ₹1,816 crore on anti-submarine craft. It noted FY26 delivered eight ships and that the next quarter should see deliveries and higher contract workforce costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the indigenisation level and where is GRSE still import-dependent?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall indigenisation is about 80-85% by value. Hull/float is 100% but about 10% of cost, weapons about 60%, survival about 70%, and diesel alternators 100%; propulsion engines are not yet indigenous. Bailey Bridge is 100%, deck machinery about 90%, and the diesel engine co-production targets 55-60%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp fall in other expenses and employee costs QoQ, and what is the pay commission impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses fell because Q4 FY26 included commissioning costs for three ships that did not recur. Contract workforce cost is sinusoidal with delivery timing and will rise when a couple of ships deliver. Management expects the next pay commission to add 15-20% to employee costs, in line with past commissions.

So, the current quarter's performance will be able to replicate in the coming quarters too.
It is for the first time in the last 10 years that our order book has dropped below ₹15,000 crore and I consider it the reflection of an excellent execution rate.

542066|2026-03.headline: Adani Total Gas Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16% to INR1,696 crore and EBITDA 13% to INR310 crore; management guided FY27 EBITDA to about INR1,500 crore.
542066|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 16% YoY to INR1,696 crore and EBITDA rose 13% to INR310 crore, with PAT up 4% to INR156 crore. For FY26, revenue grew 18% to INR6,415 crore, EBITDA rose 5% to INR1,225 crore, PBT fell 1% to INR863 crore and PAT was INR637 crore. Volumes carried the quarter: CNG grew 17% YoY in Q4 and PNG 5%, with a record ~50,000 domestic PNG connections added. Management said the West Asia crisis raised gas costs, which were partly absorbed to protect consumers, and that gas pool supply from the government was used to keep CNG and domestic PNG supplied.

segments.name: PNG (domestic)
segments.commentary: PNG volumes grew 5% YoY in Q4 and 6% in FY26. Total household tally reached 1.1 million (ATGL standalone) and 13.1 lakh including the IOAGPL JV.

segments.commentary: 214 customers added in Q4, taking the total to 9,965. Management said industrial volumes saw about 1% degrowth here and there during the crisis; industrial is about 20% and commercial about 2.5% of volume.

segments.commentary: Operates 5,100 EV charge points across 26 states and UTs and 226 cities, with about 54 MW installed capacity. Target of 10,000 charge points in the near term.

qa_highlights.answer: Pool price is the weighted average of pooled volumes: RLNG, fertiliser and ONGC volumes withdrawn, plus Vedanta and HPHT gas. March 2026 pool price was USD 12.42 per MMBtu; imported LNG was excluded in March but included later in April.

qa_highlights.question: Is supply sufficient for incremental CNG and PNG demand, and is spot LNG used (Dolat Capital)?
qa_highlights.answer: Government supplied the full six-month average, with additional volumes above it allocated later for the priority sector. Management did not give a split of spot versus government molecules for incremental demand.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue growth and EBITDA guidance (Mody Fincap)?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Preyash Jhaveri guided revenue growth in line with FY26, with EBITDA growth tracking volume growth and cited around INR1,500 crore of EBITDA for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: When will new GAs reach peak utilisation and contribute to profit (Percept Capital)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most of the 34 directly served GAs are now connected to city gas stations or LCNG plants. The initial focus is widening the consumer base, and it cited the highest-ever quarterly EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing flexibility to pass on higher gas costs (Percept Capital)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices were calibrated and not fully passed on to protect consumers; industrial volume was down only about 1% here and there during the crisis.

qa_highlights.question: Returns on new investments and ROCE targets (Percept Capital)?
qa_highlights.answer: No fixed target was given. Management said returns start lower in new GAs (around 8-10%) and rise to 12-15% with incremental investment on the same pipe, and it looks at 2-3 year and longer horizons.

qa_highlights.answer: PNG was about 50% of volume; CNG plus domestic about 78% and industrial plus commercial about 22%, with industrial about 20% and commercial about 2.5%. Sourcing mix: 85% APM, HPHT and WG plus contracts, 16% spot.

542066|2026-06.headline: ATGL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR1,908 crore and EBITDA was INR281 crore, while gas volumes grew 13% to 303 MMSCM amid margin pressure from spot gas.
542066|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 gas sales of 303 MMSCM (up 13% YoY), with CNG up 18% and PNG up 4%, and revenue of INR1,908 crore (up 27% YoY) with EBITDA of INR281 crore. West Asia tensions pushed Brent-linked RLNG and NWG prices higher, and the government withdrew the pooled gas mechanism after a peace deal, forcing ATGL to buy spot gas (around 15% of consumption after curtailment). Management acknowledged that operating margins have compressed over six to eight quarters, which it attributed mainly to market-driven gas prices and declining APM allocation. Management expects margins to recover once Middle East supply normalises, but gave no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why have operating margins compressed from about 25% to 15% over six to eight quarters, and when will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited market-driven gas prices and the declining APM allocation as the main causes. Management expects margins to recover once Middle East supply returns, with US and Qatar supply expected to lower rates, but gave no timeline.

qa_highlights.answer: Domestic volumes are about 62% and imported RLNG about 38%. Higher Brent prices lifted NWG and RLNG costs. Management said NWG is 12% of the Indian crude basket and was above $5/MMBTU in the quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: Spot volumes are around 15% of total consumption after curtailment. Management said curtailed volumes should return over time, but it could not predict the timing given the Middle East situation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the government likely to restart the pooled gas mechanism?

So, we have to be careful how many fronts we open.
But overall, I think Jaypee is known for building very good plants and technically excellent asset.

financial_highlights.change: Third straight quarter of healthy growth excluding Rajgangpur breakdown impact last quarter

financial_highlights.metric: Raw material cost per ton of production
Power and fuel cost per ton of production

financial_highlights.change: Mainly mark-to-market gains on treasury investments
Stamp duty and transaction costs on Jaypee acquisition

financial_highlights.value: INR45 crores accrued / INR60 crores collected

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Input cost headwind of INR70-75/t in Q2 (raw material INR823/t up 12% QoQ, blended fuel INR1.47/Kcal from INR1.36) and negative operating leverage flagged for Q2, with EBITDA already down 11% QoQ to INR805 crores; only partial offset from packing cost easing and the INR150/t permanent fuel saving.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Belgaum commercial production due within 6 months, Jaypee already acquired (5.2 Mt cement, 3.3 Mt clinker), and cement capacity guided to about 67 Mt by Q3 FY28 with Kadapa and Pune; Pune start-up already slipped on execution issues, so timing risk is real.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Organic volume growth guided at about 7-8% in line with industry (industry ~7% FY27), Dalmia running 200-250 bps above industry in its markets, June stronger post-elections, and Jaypee expected to contribute meaningfully from Q3; Jaypee volume ramp not quantified.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is handling 116-117 Mt while stabilising Jaypee and said more projects will be announced in a couple of quarters; Jaypee brownfield and debottlenecking options exist with reserves and land, but no capacity figure given yet, and FY27 capex is held at INR3,200-3,400 crores.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides in line with industry (~7-8%) and gave no upgrade; Q2 input cost headwind of INR70-75/t and Jaypee ramp uncertainty argue against raising guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The 75 Mt target has slipped about a year to FY28, Pune start-up pushed back, Jaypee breakeven is only 'a couple of quarters' out with no volume guidance, and the INR182 crore exceptional item is provisional; fuel (pet coke USD130-135/t vs USD110-115/t pre-war) and packing costs are volatile.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Premium products already at 25% of portfolio and Weather365 premium-plus launched this quarter, but no further named launches were guided.

rows.label: Jaypee EBITDA breakeven and ramp
rows.when: within 2 quarters for EBITDA neutral; 6-8 quarters to Dalmia
rows.why: Management says EBITDA neutral in a couple of quarters, but Jaypee's older plant was shut for a long time with legacy issues and INR550 crore refurbishment spend, and volume ramp is not quantified.

rows.label: East price gap versus other regions
rows.why: Price hikes of INR15-20/bag in East but Bengal prices suppressed; management declined to say what would narrow the gap, while South saw some uptick in July.

rows.label: Leverage headroom under 2x
rows.why: Net debt INR4,431 crores at 1.47x EBITDA after acquisition funding, gross debt INR9,108 crores, with analysts questioning strain from the 110 Mt pathway and 110-130 Mt target described as directional.
